idea.name: Kill the same-second double send (pin bot)
idea.family: lose less / order structure of the live pin bot
idea.mechanism: In pinrun, allow at most one in-flight ENTRY order per ticker and side. A second pass inside ~1 s cannot yet see the first order's fill, so block it until the first order's acknowledgement returns. Intentional legs (early leg then top-up, late add) keep their own path; hedge orders (kind 'hedge') are never touched. `--one-coin-max` already exists in the code and is not in the live argv. This is a code fix, not a new market; it needs a VERSIONS.md entry, versioncheck, and a startup-path run with the new flag before restart.
idea.why_mispriced: Not a mispricing. The bot accidentally doubles its size, and in the logs the doubled contracts land disproportionately on losing markets (4 of 27 duplicated markets lost vs a ~3.5% base loss rate). Plausible but unproven mechanism: a second same-second pass fires only while a large offer is still showing, i.e. someone is dumping size into us, the 'fresh level + toxic flow' pattern from earlier work.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Attribution: duplicate contracts share each market's outcome pro rata (price differences between the two orders ignored). (2) The fix never gates a hedge and never blocks legitimate top-up/late-add legs. (3) Only 4 losing markets drive the dollar sign. If duplicates were in fact random, removing them would cost the pin's small per-contract edge on ~1,046 contracts over the period, while still restoring the intended bank/11.76 sizing. Artefact risk: 'full+full pairs' that are really intended legs mislabelled as entries.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: About +$3/day: removes -$86.36 of losses and gives up +$35.16 of wins over the logged period (net +$51.20). Halves the worst single-market loss: BTC 09-23 20:30Z was -$130.41, of which -$65.20 came from the duplicate 88 contracts.
idea.data_needed: None to decide. After deploying, count duplicate filled entry orders in one week of live logs (target 0). Cross-check against CURRENT_STATE open item #5.
idea.evidence_so_far: sweep/combine-structure-incentives-hedging/dupsend_all.py/.out (live order logs + Kalshi ledger): 28 of 907 entered markets had a filled entry order sent within 1,000 ms after an earlier filled one on the same ticker and side; 21 were full+full pairs (the bug). Duplicate contracts: 1,046.5 of 2,510.8 in those markets. Losing markets 4 of 27, duplicate share -$86.36; winning 24, +$35.16; net -$51.20. pin_conc2.out: capping same-direction markets per close does NOT cut the worst close (-$130.41 at k=1, 2 and 3), so the fix belongs at the order level.
merged_from: combine-structure-incentives-hedging: Kill the same-second double send
idea.novelty_vs_killed: Known bug (CURRENT_STATE open #5) listed as unmeasured; what is new is its dollar cost and its share of the worst single loss.
idea.prior_reason: Measured on our own live fills and Kalshi's ledger (top of the evidence hierarchy); deterministic effect on size; cheap fix; serves the #1 priority (lose less). Not 5 because the net dollar sign rests on 4 losing markets.
idea.worst_case: A fix that wrongly blocks a top-up or late add costs a few dollars of wins; a fix that touches the hedge path would repeat the 09-19 'gate blocked a hedge' loss class, so it must be scoped to entry legs only.

chk.measured:
The bug I01 describes does not happen, so the fix would block nothing. The source is our own live order logs (138 files, results/pinrun-live-*.jsonl) plus Kalshi's settlement ledger (results/kalshi_ledger.json), 908 entered markets from 09-08 to 09-25.

1) There is no in-flight double. The bot sends entry orders synchronously from its main loop (pintake.take; its only other thread is the index websocket). So a second pass cannot run until the first order's reply is back. Measured: 27 of the 28 "<1 s duplicate" orders have millisecond timestamps, and 0 of those 27 were sent before the earlier order's reply arrived. In the worst case, BTC 09-23 20:30Z, the first order was sent at ...774390 and its reply came back 107 ms later. The second decision was made at ...774696, about 200 ms after the bot already knew about the first fill. Right after that, the log shows close_budget refused with spent=176, so the bot had booked both orders.

2) The "21 full+full pairs = the bug" label is wrong. The log writes leg="full" on top-ups and scale-ins too. I re-ran each of the 28 orders through pinrun.rebuy_ok's branches, using the SIZE from the autosize records at that moment. The P&L column is the order's share of the market's ledger result, hedges included:
- 14 top-ups of positions that were not yet full size. This is intended (A29). +$1.23, 2 small losers.
- 2 top-ups after an early leg. Intended. +$3.92.
- 2 late adds. Intended (v-lateadd-live). +$2.59.
- 7 scale-ins after the market was already full size, since 09-14. This is A23 under the live --max-per-market 2 --improve-max 0.010, deployed by operator decision. Total -$42.89.
- 3 scale-ins from 09-08 to 09-11, under rules that no longer run. -$16.06.
- Total -$51.20, which matches the sweep's figure.

The dollar sign comes from one market, not four. BTC 09-23 20:30Z accounts for -$65.20. That trade (13c edge at 26 s left, after a single-print spike) is now refused twice over: by v-nospike's spike gate and by v-cap20's 10c edge cap above 20 s. Both were deployed about 1.5-2 h after the loss (VERSIONS.md lines 514-617, and the v-nospike write-up is built on this exact market). NEAR 09-08 (-$17.83) predates the current per-market rules.

3) What is left is a known issue already on hold (CURRENT_STATE v-safety2: "the scale-in double buy, A23 compares against the sweep-inflated average paid"). The scale-in rule compares the new ask against the AVERAGE we paid, which our own sweep pushed up. So "1c cheaper" can fire when the best offer has not moved at all: BTC saw 86c on both orders but had paid an 87c average. Since 09-14 there were 8 scale-ins, 683 contracts, -$40.46, 1 loser. Leaving out the now-gated BTC, 7 won +$24.75, about 4.2c a contract. Six of the eight were the average-inflated kind: -$51.09 with BTC, +$14.11 without it. Only 1 scale-in has fired since v-cap20, in 31 hours (+$1.86).

4) Correction to the idea: --one-coin-max does not cap anything. It is a paper-only multiplier that lets one market hold MORE than SIZE, only under --one-coin-depth, which live refuses. And --improve-max cannot switch scale-in off, because the code requires it to be above IMPROVE_BY (0.005).

5) Tail check: across 694 closes, only 1 had two losing markets at once (09-19 23:45Z). So piling a close into one coin, which is what scale-in does, does make the single-market tail bigger than spreading the same budget over two coins would.

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
I01 as written: $0 a day at $900 and at $5k. It would block 0 orders, because the entry path cannot have two orders in flight.

The variant that could still matter is the held item: compare a scale-in against the best offer seen earlier, not the sweep-inflated average paid. Over 09-14 to 09-25 (about 11 days) it would have removed 6 orders: the -$65.20 BTC loss (now already blocked by later gates) and +$14.11 of wins.

Looking forward, with the BTC pattern already gated: it gives up about $14 / 11 days = about $1.3 a day of wins. Against that, at a roughly 3% losing rate on about 0.55 such scale-ins a day, the extra half of a hedged loser (about $50-65 at SIZE ~88) comes to about 0.016 x $60 = about $1 a day. Net is about $0, plus or minus $1 a day at $900. At $5k, sizes are about 5.5x, so about $0, plus or minus $6 a day. The sign cannot be measured at n=8 scale-ins with 1 loss. What the variant buys is lower variance, not expected dollars.
chk.worst_case:
For I01 itself: nothing is avoided. The only risk is a restart with a no-op gate.

What the scale-in rule can still cost: one market that passes every gate and then loses while holding a doubled position. At $900 (SIZE ~88) that is about 2 x 88 x ~0.9 = ~$155 unhedged, about -$130 hedged (the BTC 09-23 case). The touch-price variant would halve that to about -$65. At $5k (SIZE ~480) it is about -$700 doubled versus about -$360 single. The worst close (MAX_PER_CLOSE x SIZE) is unchanged either way.
chk.killer_risks:
The mechanism is absent. Orders are sent synchronously, and 0 of 27 millisecond-stamped duplicates were in flight. The proposed gate would be a no-op that still needs a restart and a VERSIONS entry.

The evidence it rested on was an artefact of the "full" leg label, and of counting top-ups, staged top-ups and late adds, all intended, as bugs.

Its dollar case rests on 1 market, BTC 09-23, which two gates deployed 09-24 02:0x-02:22Z already refuse.

For the salvage variant: an EV sign that cannot be measured at n=8. Pro-rata attribution ignores that a refused scale-in frees close budget for another coin. And any edit must stay out of the hedge path (the lesson "a gate must never block a hedge"): rebuy_ok is entry-only.
chk.next_test:
No test for I01. Close it and fix the CURRENT_STATE open item 5 wording: the "same-second double sends" are the A23 scale-in plus A29 top-ups working as designed, not an in-flight race.

For the held scale-in item, the cheapest decisive step is a data pull, not a trade. Each week, re-run rebuy_class.py over the new live logs and count scale-ins split into average-inflated vs genuine, with the market result from the ledger.

Pre-registered bar: ship "compare against the lowest earlier ask_seen, not the average paid" on the operator's variance preference alone, which CURRENT_STATE allows ("favour lower variance over expected value at the margin"), as long as average-inflated scale-ins stay under about 1 a day and their winners add up to under $2 a day. Revert it if a paper arm with the old rule shows more than +$15 a week over live at equal losses.

A win-rate verdict is out of reach: telling a 3% loss rate from 10% needs about 150+ scale-ins, which is months at the current rate.

idea.name: LIP payment decider: Kalshi's paid_out scoreboard plus a $30 probe
idea.family: identify better / Kalshi Liquidity Incentive Program (gates the whole 1c-filler family: I04, I05, I15, I16, I19-I23)
markets: GET /incentive_programs status=closed and status=paid_out (all liquidity programs)
one slow LIP market whose full side bids 98c or lower
idea.mechanism: Read-only half (runnable now): once a day page status=closed (~12 GETs) and status=paid_out. A program that ended more than ~1.5 days ago and still reads paid_out=false paid nobody. Rank series/strikes by unpaid dollars (target list for the fillers). Decisive read-only check tomorrow after ~12Z: join exchange-mechanics/empty_watch.jsonl (5-minute polls 07:12-10:15Z 09-25) with the flags for those Miami hours -- strikes one-sided at every poll must be unpaid, strikes two-sided at any poll should be paid. Live half (needs per-order operator sign-off): three post-only 1,000-contract bids at 1c ($10 each): (a) one KXTEMPMIAH dead strike for one hourly program (must pass the crossing guard -- opposite best bid 98c or lower -- and not be the strike nearest the current index reading), (b) the empty YES side of a non-leader coin-race leg for minutes 0-9 of one window, (c) one slow market that passes the guard. Cancel at period end. Readout 48-96 h later: Kalshi balance residual (ledger + pinxfer, which reconciled to $0.0000 over the account's life), app activity, and whether that exact program flips to paid_out. Pre-registered: an unexplained credit of $1 or more on at least 1 of 3 means the rules work as filed, build I04/I05; $0 on all 3 after 96 h kills the 1c-unlock family. Separate the monthly APY credit by date.
idea.why_mispriced: Not a trade. It prices the one fact no read-only method can settle: whether OUR lone 1c stack gets paid. Also serves as a free competition monitor: if the unpaid share on far Miami strikes starts falling, copiers have arrived.
idea.must_be_true: paid_out=false on a processed program means no user reached the $1 payout floor (not 'held for review' or 'cancelled'). Artefact check done: volume does not decide it (12 zero-volume Miami programs WERE paid; 341 with volume were NOT). The ledger residual must stay attributable (no other unexplained flows in the window); the probe markets must not be traded by our bots; the probe must not look like abuse (1c, size = Target, bona fide orders we accept being filled).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 directly. Cost <= $30 worst case (all three stacks fully filled and losing), typically < $1. Turns a $0-vs-$100s/day unknown into a yes/no within ~4 days; ~15 GETs/day thereafter.

idea.novelty_vs_killed: The 09-07 gold test would have measured a crowded shared side (0.63% share) and was NO_GO; the 09-06 coin-race attempt earned $0 because orders were almost never resting. This tests a side where we would be the only depth, on hourly programs so the answer comes in days. Nothing in the kill lists covers LIP payment.
idea.prior_reason: Prior here scores the value of the decision, not profit: the read-only half rests on Kalshi's own 8-day payment record across every series (strong), and the live half costs at most $30 to settle the largest dollar question in the sweep.

chk.measured:
What would decide this is whether Kalshi pays OUR lone 1c stack. No read-only method can answer that. Everything read-only that I checked says the rules work as filed, the pool is large, and the dead-side fill cost is small next to it. The one number the whole family hangs on (our own credit) has never been observed. Only the live probe settles it.

1) THE RULES (filing text exchange-mechanics/lip_2026-07-15.flat.txt, plus Kalshi help center article 13823851):
- Scores on each side normalize to 1 separately. The help center says "a single snapshot is worth at most 2.0". So a lone bidder on the empty side gets 50% of every valid snapshot.
- A snapshot counts only if resting size is at least Target on BOTH sides. The walk-down has no price-distance limit, so bids far from the best still count toward Target.
- Payout floor is $1. There is no minimum price.
- For Miami, the params from inc_active_0645.json are $100 per strike-hour, Target 1,000, discount 0.5 per tick, window :02 to :00.
- So if we are alone, payout = $50 x the fraction of the hour that is valid. The $1 floor is crossed after about 72 seconds of valid snapshots.

2) THE LIVE SIDE ALREADY MEETS TARGET (check-I02/depth_now.py; 27 GETs across two KXTEMPMIAH snapshots, 10:12Z and 10:17Z on 09-25, plus one coin-race snapshot):
- All 7 one-sided Miami strikes had 2,225 to 3,451 contracts resting on the live side. The numbers were identical 4 minutes apart.
- So filling the empty side with at least 1,000 is the only missing piece.
- 1 of the 7 (T78.99, live side bid 99c) fails the crossing guard.

3) HOW MANY TARGETS, 09-25 07:12-10:12Z (check-I02/watch_summary.py, reading exchange-mechanics/empty_watch.jsonl):
- Miami: 40 strike-hours. 25 were one-sided at every 5-minute poll. 14 of those passed the 98c-or-lower guard at every poll, about 3.5 per hour.
- Coin race: only 3 of 65 fifteen-minute periods were one-sided at every poll. Other people usually fill its thin side.

4) FILL COST on the population closest to ours, a 1c dead-side bid that actually existed (check-I02/onecent_fills.py, 138 GETs, output onecent_fills.json; clustered by strike-hour):
- 90 paid Miami strike-hours, 09-19..21. The 1c bid was hit in 86 of the 90.
- Contracts hit per strike-hour: mean 560, median 164, p90 1,766, max 2,795.
- That is at most $5.60 mean, and never more than the lot size, because each hit loses at most 1c.
- Timing (hit_timing.py, 25 strike-hours, 11,749 contracts): 34% were hit more than 30 minutes before the end and 1% in the last minute. The earliest hit per strike-hour had a median of 2,055 seconds before the end. In 7 of 25 the first hit came in the first ~8 minutes.

5) A COMPETITOR ALREADY RUNS A FILLER (check-I02/filler_seen.py):
- Thin-side bids of 1,000 to 1,600 contracts at 2c or less (Target-sized, not retail lottery tickets) appeared in 6 of 40 Miami strike-hours today.
- All were on near-money strikes (75.99-77.99) and intermittent, 1 to 4 of 12 polls. Live example: a NO bid of 1c x 1,061-1,062 on T75.99, and a YES bid of 2c x 1,195 on T77.99.
- None were on the deep-dead strikes.
- This is indirect support that the payment happens (someone keeps doing it). It also means copiers exist.

6) ARTEFACT CHECKS:
- 'paid_out=false means nobody reached $1', not 'pending': the prior join found 0% two-sided minutes gave 3 paid / 142 unpaid and 100% gave 68 / 0. KXRT: 0 / 50 vs 283 / 0. Under the filed formula, any valid stretch longer than ~72 seconds pays a lone bidder at least $1, so unpaid equals one-sided. That is consistent.
- A 1c minimum-price exclusion: the help center lists none.
- Correction to the idea: the proposed 'decisive read-only join tomorrow' is NOT decisive for our payment. It only re-confirms point 6 with 5-minute polls instead of 1-minute candles. Run it as the competition monitor, not as the decider.

NOT MEASURED: any LIP credit to this account, ever.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
I02 itself makes $0 a day. It is a $10-36 test.

Expected probe cost: 3 probes x mean fills of $1.64-5.60 each, about $5-15. Worst is $30 at 1,000-lots or $36 at the recommended 1,200-lots.

If the probe passes, this is the family's ceiling. It is arithmetic from the filed rules plus measured fill rates, NOT measured for us:
- Per dead Miami strike-hour, alone with a 2,000-lot: $50 x ~0.85 valid = ~$42 gross, minus ~$5.60 in fills, = ~$36 net.
- Today's rate is 3.5 targets an hour. If that holds all day it is ~84 a day, so a theoretical ~$3,000 a day.
- The unpaid Miami pool 09-16..23 averaged $7,550 a day, so a 50% share caps Miami at ~$3,775 a day.
- That number is not believable as a durable result. At the same 1c price the pool splits by size, so a copier posting 10,000 contracts ($100) takes ~83-91% of the side. A competitor is already on the near-money strikes, and Kalshi can re-parameterize.

Same at a $900 and a $5k bank. Capital is not the constraint: roughly 3.5 lots of $10-20 are resting at once, $35-70 tied up. The limit is the pool and competition.

The honest realistic number is unknown until our first credit and a week of share data.
chk.worst_case:
Probe: $30 if all three 1,000-lots are fully filled and lose, or $36 at 1,200-lots. Loss is capped at 1c x lot, because a 1c bid on a dead side only fills when the seller thinks it is worth under 1c. A storm turning the strike live makes our bid better, not worse.

The real danger is scaling BEFORE a credit is seen. Run blind at 84 strike-hours a day with no payout:
- Mean fills cost about $470 a day (84 x $5.60).
- The worst plausible day, every lot swept, is about $1,000-1,700 (84 x $12-20).

So the family must not start until the probe credit is seen. Once running, it needs a daily ledger reconciliation that kills it if no credit appears for any program over 48 hours old.
chk.killer_risks:
1) Kalshi's implementation differs from the filing, or it treats the 1c filler as 'inconsistent with the purpose' and revokes LIP status. Only the probe tests the first; the second can come later.

2) Competition: pro-rata at the same price means anyone with a bigger 1c stack dilutes us. A Target-sized filler is already active on near-money strikes (6 of 40 strike-hours today). Watch the daily unpaid share on the far strikes; it was flat at ~40% 09-16..23.

3) False negative from the probe design as written:
- A lot of exactly Target (1,000) goes invalid on the first hit.
- 7 of 25 strike-hours had their first 1c hit in the first ~8 minutes, and about 1 in 25 within ~70 seconds, which is under the $1 floor.
- Fix: size 1,200 (like the competitor's 1,061-1,062), place at :02, and pick a strike whose live side is at least 1,500 deep, bids 98c or lower, and is at least 4F from the current reading.

4) The coin-race probe (b) is a bad site and should be replaced:
- Its thin side was one-sided at every poll in only 3 of 65 periods, so it tests a crowded side.
- KXCRYPTOLEAD15M is traded by the live coin-race bot. That risks self-trading (a hard-rule violation) and muddies ledger attribution.
- Replace it with a second Miami dead strike in a different hour.

5) Per-order sign-off (hard rule 1) makes the family operationally impossible at ~84 orders a day unless the operator grants a class sign-off after the probe.

6) Attribution: the ledger residual must be clean in the window. The monthly APY credit must be separated by date, and no other LIP-eligible resting size may be on the account (pinrun's post-only orders are tiny and would fall under $1).

ref.strongest_objection:
The checker's key premise is wrong: filling the empty side is NOT the only missing piece, and we would NOT be the only filler.

1) Most of the busy side's depth belongs to another rewards farmer, and it comes and goes.
- The 2,225-3,451 contracts the checker saw on the busy side (10:13-10:17Z) were mostly one participant's ladder of very low bids: 1,000 at 1c, 500 at 2c, 200 at 5c, 100 at 20c, plus a few more. The same ladder sat on all six one-sided strikes.
- Between 10:17 and 10:26Z it was pulled from all six at once, with no trades.
- The busy sides then held only 400-755 contracts on 5 of the 6, below the 1,000 needed. They stayed below for about 10 minutes, and one strike (T73.99) stayed below all hour.
- At the 11:00Z hour the ladder came back: about 1,716 of the roughly 2,200 contracts on each busy side were bids at 5c or less.
- Across my 16 polls, the busy side met the 1,000 minimum only 64% of the time on the strikes we could fill.
- So a filler on the empty side depends on another farmer's switch. When that farmer pulls, our snapshots stop counting and earn nothing, but our 1c stack can still be bought.

2) That farmer could take 100% of the pool by also posting the 1c stack on the empty side, and doesn't. The empty-side stack is the leg that gets picked off.
- Buyers take 99c offers on near-certain strikes; each 1,000-lot hands them about $9 after fees.
- 09-20..23 had 255 strike-hours 4F or more from the settled temperature. On 28 of them, a full 1,000-size stack on the losing side was bought in a single trade: mostly exactly 1,000, 1,050, 1,060 or 1,100 contracts, some as small as 500.
- First such sweep: median 959 s after :02; a quarter came within 209 s; 9 of the 28 came within 5 minutes.
- On the 09-23 17:00 hour, reposted stacks were swept every 100-130 s. Today 09:04Z, 1,256 contracts were taken in one print on T70.99.
- The checker's fill cost ($5.60 mean, first hit about 26 minutes in) came from paid hours where a 1c bid showed up in 1-minute price data. That only catches stacks that lasted until the end of a minute, so it undercounts the fast sweeps.

3) Novelty claim is false. 'None on the deep-dead strikes' and 'we would be the only depth' do not hold: full-size fillers worked 4-9F strikes on 28 strike-hours over 4 days.

What I could NOT refute: that Kalshi pays.
- All 28 programs where a full-size 1c stack provably sat on the empty side were paid. Only 31 of the other 227 were paid.
- Under the filed formula, a lone filler gets the biggest single share of those payouts.
- So reading the records already mostly settles the payment question at the level of the program. The probe only adds proof for his own account.
- The probe's 'passes, so build I04/I05' rule is mis-specified. The deciding unknowns are how fast stacks get picked off and the other farmer's ladder, not whether Kalshi pays.
ref.independent_checks:
All numbers below come from my own read-only Kalshi requests (about 350), in scratchpad/sweep/refute-I02/.

1) facts.py: KXTEMPMIAH.
- Fee type is quadratic with multiplier 1, so makers pay nothing.
- Prices move in whole cents from 1c to 99c. Nothing can be bid below 1c, so the 1c edge for buyers cannot be removed.
- Settles on the Synoptic temperature at the top of the hour.
- Each program pays $100 per strike-hour (period_reward 1,000,000), needs 1,000 contracts a side, and discounts each 1c step by half.
- The filing and help centre confirm: no price floor, both sides must reach 1,000 for a snapshot to count, each side's share adds up to 1, and the minimum payout is $1. Payouts also need a verified SSN.

2) depthpoll.py: full books every 2 minutes, 10:26-11:07Z, compared level by level with the checker's depth_now.jsonl.
- The identical ladder (1,000 at 1c, 501 at 2c, 203 at 5c, 100 at 20c, 16 at 30c, 10 at 50c) was on T71-T74 and T78-T80, and was gone from all of them by 10:26.
- Busy-side totals on those strikes: 418, 416, 446, 755, 579 and 512. T79.99 was the exception at 1,649, of which 721 was someone else's 1c bid.
- From 11:02Z, the ladder made up about 1,716 of each busy side of about 2,200.
- Busy side at 1,000 or more on the fillable strikes: 61 of 96 polls, 64%.
- No trades on those strikes in either hour, except 25 contracts at 5c on T79.99. So nobody posted the empty side, including the farmer who owns the ladder.

3) sweeps.py and survival.py: trade tape, 09-20..23. There are 720 strike-hours in all; I pulled 180 tapes for 09-23 and all 4F-plus strikes for 09-20..22.
- 4F or more from the settled temperature: 255 strike-hours, 59 paid.
- A single trade of 500 or more at 1c on the losing side: 28, all paid.
- Of the 196 unpaid, none had such a trade.
- First sweep, seconds after :02: median 959, a quarter by 209, a quarter still unswept at 1,796. 9 of the 28 came within 300 s.
- 09-23, all distances: under 2F, 31 of 31 swept hours paid; 2-4F, 26 of 29; 4F and over, 7 of 7. The 3 unpaid ones had their stack taken before :02 or had one too small to reach 1,000.
- Arithmetic if Kalshi pays as filed: a 1,200 stack posted at :02 and swept at the observed times earns on average $15.80 (median $13.80), against $12 lost on the buy. So it roughly breaks even on the swept half.

4) Today's tape: T75.99 at 10:03:05Z, 2,875 contracts at 99c, 65 s after the start. The competitor's 1,061 stack was taken at 10:23:01 in a single 1,000-contract trade. On the 09:02-10:00 hour, T70.99-T73.99 were swept at 147-196 s.
ref.revised_dollars_per_day:
I02 itself makes $0 a day.

The probe would cost about $6-12 expected per probe hour: roughly half of 1,200-contract stacks get bought within the hour, losing $12 each time. Worst case is $12 per stack.

To stop the probe being wiped out by another farmer pulling their orders, it needs its own 1,000-contract 1c bid on the busy side. Nobody sells into that, so it costs about $0. But it is plainly there to farm the reward, and that raises the risk that Kalshi's chief regulatory officer revokes eligibility.

Family, if Kalshi pays as filed. This is not measured; it is arithmetic from the filed rules:
- Per strike-hour where we are the only filler: about 0.5 x ($50 x 0.64 of the hour the busy side is deep enough), plus 0.5 x ($14 - $12) = about $15-20 before competition.
- The ladder farmer can take the whole pool the moment filling proves profitable. Existing fillers already cover 23% of dead strike-hours. Buyers of 99c offers get paid more the more stacks we post.
- Realistic: tens to low hundreds of dollars a day at best, not the checker's theoretical ~$3,000.
- The same at a $900 or a $5,000 bank.

idea.name: Late-dry rain NO (KXRAIN after 8 PM local), with sensor-down gate and idle-bank sizing
idea.family: weather / daily rain, observation-timed taker (plus capital-efficiency sleeve)
markets: KXRAIN (about 27 cities a day; Denver, Miami, Boston, Atlanta, Chicago, NYC, Dallas, Phoenix, Houston carry the most volume)
idea.mechanism: KXRAIN pays YES if the station's day total (Weather Company = NWS daily climate report; a trace counts as 0) is above 0 in; the day runs on local STANDARD time and closes at local midnight. From 20:00 LST read the station's public METARs (aviationweather.gov). Fire only if: no METAR since the day began shows measurable rain (hourly P group or 6-hour 6 group > 0); none of the last 3 METARs shows rain, drizzle, thunder or a trace; and NO METAR that station-day carries 'PNO' in remarks (precipitation sensor not operating -- a dead gauge produces exactly the same 'dry' METAR while the official report can still record rain). Candidate extra remark filters: LTG, CB, VCSH/SHRA. Then buy NO once, at the first minute the NO ask is 90-97c (this hits resting YES bids of 3-10c), and hold to settlement next morning (~11-14Z). Entries fire 01:00-08:00Z, so size from idle bank with a hard cap that always leaves pinrun its per-close budget (~bank/11.76). Optional exit: rest a 1c YES bid for the held size; if a 99c NO buyer fills it the position closes at 99c, capital returns 4-10 h early and the overnight tail is dropped (costs ~1c/contract of edge vs holding; where the empty side is LIP-funded it may also earn part of the pool, see I04).
idea.why_mispriced: The other side is resting YES bids of 3-10c left late at night: lottery buyers, or stale quotes still pricing the whole day's rain chance after most of it has passed dry. The price does carry information below 80c (NO lost 9 of 56 Jul-Aug and 5 of 30 Aug-Sep there -- real evening storms, which radar shows), but in the 90-97c band NO lost ~1 of ~440 market-price cases vs the 3-10% the price implies. Our fill is a taker order we time ourselves, hitting a resting bid -- not the crypto case where someone chose to sell to us.
idea.must_be_true: (1) METAR P and 6 groups record all measurable rain in real time, except when the gauge is down (PNO), hence the gate (Miami 08-31: PNO, METARs dry, official 1.10 in). (2) Late-evening rain after a dry METAR stays near 0.4% outside Jul-Sep; winter frontal night rain is untested. (3) The 3-10c YES bids stay there when we sell 50-100 contracts into them. (4) Artefacts ruled out or to rule out: candle bid not executable; rain across the LST day boundary misassigned (the NYC/EWR 09-21 1c NO asks were a boundary bug and the price band excludes them); two unusually benign late-summer months. (5) Rain nights are not correlated with pin loss days (no mechanism seen).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: About 4.4 entries/day (max 10) at +4.45c per contract after the 0.07*p*(1-p) fee: ~$10/day at 50 contracts per market (~$475 overnight capital), ~$20/day at 100 (worst sample day -$46, ~$950 capital). Tape-based: OUR loss rate is unknown until a live test. Realistic tail: a regional evening storm hitting 3 held cities at 100 contracts = -$250 to -$300. The PNO gate costs 6 of 255 entries (2.4%). Exit-at-99c variant nets ~+3.8c/contract (vs +4.45-4.85c held).
idea.data_needed: (a) Re-run both months from the cached files with PNO/LTG/CB/VCSH filters (no API calls). (b) Entry at 18:00 and 19:00 LST (~500 candlestick GETs). (c) A winter month once history exists. (d) Pre-registered 1-contract live test: 30 entries; pass = at most 1 loss and average fill <= 97c. (e) For the exit option: ~30 orderbook GETs at 02-05Z on one night (is the dead YES side < 1,000 contracts and the NO bid 99c?).
idea.evidence_so_far: 1-minute candlestick book prices with a 3-minute METAR lag. Band 90-97c: Jul 25-Aug 24: 143 entries, 1 loss (Atlanta 07-28), +$6.02 per 1 contract per market; Aug 25-Sep 23: 112 entries, 0 losses, +$5.33. Together 255 entries / 58 days / 1 loss, average ask 94.8c, +4.45c/contract after fee; median day +$0.20, worst day -$0.46 per contract per market. Band 85-97c: 262 entries, 4 losses, all at 85-87c. NO win rate in the late-dry state by NO ask (each market once per band): Aug-Sep 80-89c 50/50, 90-94c 77/77, 95-97c 108/108; Jul-Aug 80-89c 75/79, 90-94c 98/99, 95-97c 139/139. Executed supply (tape, not our fills): after the rule fired on the 114 Aug-Sep entries, 509,388 NO contracts traded at <= 97c (avg 90.1c), all winners, ~15k/day median. Live book 06:36Z 09-25: Phoenix 571 YES-bid contracts at 3-8c 24 min before close. PNO: pno_check.py found 160 of 49,113 METARs across 29 stations with PNO (Miami 9 local days, Phoenix 8 since 07-20, PHL 2, MSY 5); 6 of the 255 entries fell on PNO days (KXRAIN-26AUG22-MIA, 26AUG30-MIA, 26JUL30-MIN, 26SEP01-PHX, 26SEP14-PHX, 26SEP15-PHX), all 6 won by luck. KXRAIN carries a $100 LIP pool per city-market over ~44 h, target 1,000 (rainlip.py); at 07Z 7-8 of 8 one-sided KXRAIN markets had the NO favourite bid at 99c, so a 99c exit exists by mid-night. Files: sweep/weather-science/raindry.py, raindry_jul.py, raindry_trades.py, raindry_2026-07-25_20.json, raindry_2026-08-25_20.json, iem/rainmetar2_*.csv; sweep/combine-wild-card/pno_check.py, rainlip.py.

This is the opposite side and state: NO late in the day with nothing measurable yet. Not D16 (resting lottery sales): we take resting bids at a time we choose, with a public observation behind it. D15 (selling our crypto winner at 99.5c) failed because the bid vanished before the flip in seconds; here the tail is hours of weather.

Held from 5 by: summer-only sample, tape not our fills, correlated storm nights.
idea.worst_case: A regional thunderstorm complex after 8 PM hits several held cities, or a gauge outage without a PNO remark: ~$90-95 per market at 100 contracts, up to 10 markets open on one night (-$900 theoretical, -$250 to -$300 realistic). A rain loss night could briefly leave pinrun short unless the cap is enforced in code.

chk.measured:
Scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/check-I03/. All reads, about 110 Kalshi GETs.

1) BACKGROUND RATE FROM WEATHER DATA ONLY, NO MARKET PRICES (clim.py, which has a self-test, and clim_report.out). Sources: IEM METAR archive plus the NWS daily climate report, 2021-01-01 to 2026-09-24, 23 stations. That is 30,239 station-days where the rule was armed at 8 PM local standard time (LST).
- 2021-2025, all months: rain came after 8 PM on 2.47% (747/30,239). It falls with a later start: 1.77% from 9 PM, 1.09% from 10 PM, 0.49% from 11 PM.
- By month the rate runs from 1.7% (October) to 3.3% (May). By season: Dec-Feb 2.48%, Mar-May 2.97%, Jun-Aug 2.53%, Sep-Nov 1.94%. So winter is not worse overall.
- Some city-seasons are over break-even with no price filter: Seattle Nov-Mar 6.4% (20/312), Boston Nov-Mar 5.5%. Miami Apr-Oct is 5.0%.
- The idea's test window (Jul 25 - Sep 23) was the calmest of the last six years: 2026 had 1.41% (15/1,067) against 3.24%, 2.61%, 2.89%, 1.74% and 1.81% for 2021-2025. Rain was about 0.57 times normal, so the 'benign summer' worry is real.
- Of 863 losses, 795 showed up as rain in later METARs, 51 had dry METARs but the official report recorded 0.01-0.03 in, and 17 fell on sensor-down (PNO) days. Adding the stricter filter (thunder, showers in the vicinity, no PNO) cuts the rate from 2.47% to 2.27%.
- Losses cluster by night: on 35 of 1,826 nights, 3 or more armed cities lost. The worst night was 5 of 18.

2) DOES THE KALSHI PRICE SEE IT COMING? (gridcal.py, gridcal.out). I read prices at fixed times, H:05 LST, from the idea's cached 1-minute candles, for 983 markets armed at 8 PM in 2026.
- Every one of the 12 losses that had a price was quoted below 90c: 0.82, 0.79, 0.75, 0.63, 0.57, 0.55, 0.44, 0.33, 0.31, 0.30, 0.10, 0.06. The other 3 losses had no YES bid at all, so there was nothing to buy.
- Band 90-97c: 176 distinct markets, 0 losses. The 95% upper bound is 2.1%, or about 3.6% after scaling for the calm summer. The idea's own first-in-band rule: 1 loss in 255, upper bound 2.2%.
- Break-even at the 94.8c average ask is about 4.85%.
- My settlement check matched Kalshi's result on all 3,924 armed market-hours (0 disagreements), so the Weather Company data is the NWS report.
- My arming code independently agreed with 253 of the idea's 255 entries. The other 2 are MKE and LEX, which I did not pull.
- The one idea loss (ATL 07-28) was at 82c at 8:05 PM and rose into the band later.

3) KXRAIN STARTED 2026-07-16 (the /historical/markets endpoint only goes back that far). No price history exists outside summer.

4) SUPPLY, from the trade tape (tapetiming.py/.json): these are other people's fills, not ours. I sampled 40 of the Aug-Sep entries.
- NO buys at 97c or less after the rule fired: median 1,399 contracts per market; at or below the entry ask, median 599. One market had zero.
- They were spread out: 53% came 30-120 minutes after firing and 17% after 2 hours. Only 62 contracts (median) came in the first 5 minutes.
- Trades were small: median 10 contracts, 90th percentile 29.
- Buyers of YES late in the day (the lottery flow) were thousands of contracts per market.

5) THE BOOK RIGHT NOW (booknow.py/.json, 10:15Z). The YES bids that matter are at 3-10c (NO at 90-97c). They are often thin (0-120 contracts) but sometimes 1,000-3,100.
- A large YES bid of about 5,350 contracts sits at 1c (NO at 99c), outside the band.
- KXRAIN has a $100 liquidity reward per market, target 1,000 contracts (inc_active.json). That reward is the likely reason the cheap YES bids keep coming back.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
The assumptions:
- Entries: 4.4 a night (the idea's scan; the fixed-time check gives 2.9).
- Average ask 94.8c. The fee is about 0.34c a contract on a 50-contract order; on 1-contract orders the fee rounds up to 1c.
- Loss rate: central 0.7% (the measured 0.4% scaled for the calm summer); pessimistic 2.5%. Edge is 100 - 94.8 - 0.34 - loss, so 4.2c central and 2.4c pessimistic.
- How many contracts we would actually get is NOT measured.

$900 bank:
- 50 contracts a market ties up about $210 overnight on a typical night, $475 on a 10-entry night, while pinrun keeps about $77 per close.
- Central: 4.4 x 50 x 4.2c = $9.2/day.
- Pessimistic (25 filled, 2.4c): 4.4 x 25 x 2.4c = $2.6/day.
- Realistic range $3-9/day.

$5k bank:
- Supply is the limit, not money. At 150 a market with a worse average price (about 3.5c edge): 4.4 x 150 x 3.5c = $23/day.
- If only 75 fill: about $12/day.
- Realistic range $10-25/day. Capital is held about 7-13 hours, from entry at 01-08Z to settlement around 14:30Z.
chk.worst_case:
At 50 contracts a market:
- One loss is -$47.50.
- A regional storm that 3 held cities fail to see coming: -$143.
- The ceiling, 10 entries all lost: -$475.

At 100 contracts, double those: -$95, -$285, -$950.

Nights with 3 or more losses happened on 1.9% of nights in 2021-25, but that is with no price filter. With the 90-97c filter, no multi-loss night has been seen in 58-61 summer nights. A bad night with no sensor-down flag is possible: 51 of 863 background losses had dry METARs but the official report recorded 0.01-0.03 in.
chk.killer_risks:
1) The out-of-summer loss rate in the band cannot be tested before it happens, because the series only started 2026-07-16. The background rate is similar across seasons (1.9-3.0%), but Seattle and Boston in Nov-Mar run 5.5-6.4% with no price filter, above break-even. If winter night rain turns out less visible on radar, the 90-97c band could stop filtering it out.
2) Our fill size is unmeasured. The tape shows plenty of volume, but in small trades spread over hours, and other bots are already buying NO at these prices. The first-minute price may cover only 2-20 contracts.
3) The supply probably depends on Kalshi's $100-per-market liquidity reward. If Kalshi ends it, the cheap YES bids may vanish. That would kill the income, not lose money.
4) The test window was the calmest of 6 years (0.57 times normal), so the 0.4% rate is optimistic. Even so, the scaled upper bound (about 3.6%) stays below the 4.85% break-even.
5) A price that climbs INTO the band after being lower (the one loss, ATL 07-28, went from 82c to 90+) may be a riskier case. That is n=1, so it is only a candidate filter.
6) If nothing enforces the cap in code, a loss night could leave pinrun short of its per-close money.
chk.next_test:
Cheapest decisive step, in two parts.

(a) A read-only book watcher for 7-10 nights, starting tonight at 01:00Z. For each market the rule arms, poll the orderbook once a minute from 20:00 LST to close. Record the YES-bid contracts at 3-10c at the moment of firing and in each later 30 minutes, and whether the bid refills after the tape shows it taken. About 20 markets x 4 h x 60 polls = about 5k GETs a night, too many to share with the bot. So poll every 3 minutes, only on markets the rule arms (about 4-8), which is about 500-600 GETs a night.
Pass bar: the median market offers at least 50 contracts at 97c or less, within 60 minutes of firing, at an average of 96c or less.

(b) If (a) passes, a live test at 10 contracts an entry (about $40 overnight), pre-registered before looking. Run 60 entries through October into November.
Pass: at most 2 losses, a fill-weighted average price of 96.0c or less, and at least 60% of wanted size filled.
Kill at once if there are 3 losses in the first 40 entries.
Exclude Seattle and Boston from Nov-Mar until a cold-season sample exists.
chk.capital_needed: $900 bank: about $210 on a typical night and $475 on the busiest, held about 7-13 hours overnight. A hard code cap should keep pinrun's per-close money (about $77) free. $5k bank: about $650-1,400, limited by supply rather than money.

ref.strongest_objection:
The "1 loss in 255" figure comes from how the backtest was built. It reads the YES bid only at the close of each minute. A live bot sees the price during the whole minute, and brief dips into the 90-97c band happen mostly on jumpy, storm-threatened markets.

- **Same candles, whole-minute view:** 266 entries and 3 losses, not 1: KXRAIN-26JUL28-ATL, 26AUG17-MIN and 26AUG18-DEN. The 11 markets that only the whole-minute view enters lost 2 of 11 (18%).
- **Confirmed on the trade tape:** takers really did buy NO at 90-97c while the weather-report checks were clean. MIN bought 412 contracts and DEN 820, and both settled YES.
- **The losers carried the size:** in the first 10 minutes, the losing markets traded 350 and 412 contracts in the band. A typical winner traded 40. So the loss rate per contract is about 1.5%, not 0.39%.
- **Correcting for the calm summer:** the checker found this summer had 0.57 times the usual evening rain. Adjusted for that, the central loss rate is about 2.6%. The 95% upper bound, about 5.7%, is above break-even (about 5.0% at a 94.6c average price). The sample cannot rule out a strategy that loses money outside this summer.

**Second problem: the rain money is not idle for the crypto bot (pinrun).**
- pinrun re-sizes every 300 s from Kalshi *cash* (`read_bank`, which reads `/portfolio/balance` `balance`). Any rain money held overnight shrinks its bets from about 01Z to 14Z. That window earned most of pinrun's measured profit from 09-15 to 09-25.
- About 40% of pinrun's markets fill the full size, so a smaller size costs it real money.
- `classify_bank_move` records each rain buy as a "withdrawal" and lowers the high-water mark. Rain losses would therefore never show up in the 20% drawdown halt or the $200-a-day loss cap.
- pinrun's code needs changing before both run on one account. Its position-adoption check does ignore KXRAIN, so it would not try to hedge the rain positions.

This does not make the idea negative in-sample. The profit per contract is still about +3 to +4c. It does cut the checker's $9/day and 0.7% loss rate a lot, and it moves "worth running" onto facts not yet measured: winter, and how much resting size is really there when the rule fires.

All scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/refute-I03/. I used about 330 Kalshi GETs, all read-only, plus 28 IEM downloads. Both recorders were alive afterwards (collector pid 2532788, feeds pid 105352), and 15.3 GB disk was free.

1. **My own data reproduced the idea exactly.**
   - Sources: 1,411 settled KXRAIN markets (319 YES, 1,092 NO) via `/markets` plus `/historical/markets`, and my own IEM weather reports (METARs) for 28 stations from 07-14 to 09-25, with my own parser.
   - Result: 255 entries, 1 loss, 94.82c average price, +4.45c/contract (r5_intraminute.py). The inputs match.
2. **Loss side from the trade tape (r3_losses.py, 38 GETs).**
   - Of the 319 YES markets, 24 were still dry by the weather reports at 8 PM local standard time.
   - In 3 of those, takers bought NO at 90-97c while the report checks were clean: MIN 08-17 (412 contracts), DEN 08-18 (820) and ATL 07-28 (274).
   - The candles show why the backtest missed MIN and DEN. The YES bid's minute *low* reached 7-10c, but its minute *close* never went under 11c. The backtest only reads the close.
3. **Whole-minute execution on the same candles:** 266 entries, 3 losses (1.13%), average price 94.64c, +3.89c/contract. The 11 markets only this view enters had 2 losses.
4. **Losses weighted by size (r7_sizeweight.py, 266 GETs).**
   - Band trading in the 10 minutes after each entry: winners had a median of 40 contracts (56 of 263 had zero); losers had 350, 412 and 17.
   - Capping our order at 50: about 29 contracts per entry on average, 1.51% of contracts lost, +4.16c/contract, $322 over 60 nights = $5.3/day.
   - That $5.3/day is the most we could make if we took ALL of that band trading, which we would not.
5. **Break-even:** fee 0.07*p*(1-p) ≈ 0.36c at 94.6c, so break-even is about 5.0% lost. 3 losses in 266 gives a 95% upper bound of about 3.3%. Scaled by the checker's 0.57 calm-summer factor, that is about 5.7%, which crosses break-even.
6. **Settlement timing** (settlement_ts minus close_time): September median 6.5 h, 90th percentile 10.5 h (settles about 11-14Z). July's median was 18 h. The rules say "Trace amounts and missing daily precipitation values are counted as 0". In daylight-saving months markets close at 23:00 standard time, but the official day runs to 24:00.
7. **pinrun coupling** (pinrun.py lines 14958-15070 and 14794).
   - It sizes from cash only when its own book is flat, every 300 s, stepping straight to the new size in either direction.
   - 09-22 to 25: 38% of 162 filled markets filled the full size and 43% filled at least half.
   - Its live profit 09-15 to 09-25 was $454.56 in 11 days (r6_pinbind.py, pinhours.py).
   - Its position-adoption check (ktruth) skips markets outside its own series, so it would not adopt or hedge KXRAIN.
8. **Winter** (from the checker's climate rows): rain the reports missed but the official total counted hit 0.18-0.20% of dry evenings in Dec-May vs 0.09% in Jun-Nov. So that invisible-rain case doubles in cold months.
9. **After-the-fact filter** (hypothesis only, based on 3 losses): skipping markets whose NO price was under 80c earlier that evening removes all 3 losses and keeps 230 of 266 entries. Pre-register it as a separate test group, do not deploy it.
ref.revised_dollars_per_day:
$900 bank: about $1-4/day, most likely about $2.

- **How it adds up:** about 4.4 entries a night × 15-29 contracts actually filled × about 3.1c. The 3.1c is +4.16c per contract with the calm-summer correction applied. That gives $2-4/day.
- **Minus pinrun's smaller bets:** $0.6-1.8/day, unless pinrun's bank reading is changed to ignore the rain money.
- **Upside:** $5-7/day, only if at least 50 contracts are resting at 3-10c at every entry (not measured) and pinrun's bank reading is fixed.
- **Downside:** it loses money if more than about 5 in 100 in-band entries lose outside summer. Winter has not been tested and cannot be before it arrives.
- **Worst night:** about -$80 at 29 contracts across 3 cities; -$285 at the idea's 100 contracts.
- **At a $5k bank:** still capped by how much is on offer, roughly $3-10/day.

Next test, changed from the checker's plan:
- Run it live with streaming execution, not minute closes.
- Record the resting YES-bid size at the moment the rule fires.
- Judge pass or fail on the share of contracts lost, not the share of entries.
- Pre-register the "skip if NO was under 80c earlier" filter as its own test group.
- Change pinrun's bank reading first.

idea.name: Miami hourly dead-side 1c filler (KXTEMPMIAH LIP unlock, with crossing guard and wxwatch side selection)
idea.family: incentive programs (Kalshi LIP) x weather index watcher x capped adverse selection
markets: KXTEMPMIAH (10 strikes/hour, $100 per strike per hourly program, Target 1,000)
idea.mechanism: Kalshi counts a LIP snapshot only when BOTH sides hold Target size; on far-from-temperature Miami strikes the dead side is empty, so the $100 per strike-hour pays nobody. Each hour at program start (:01-:02Z): (1) use Kalshi's own live Miami index (research/wxwatch.py) to list strikes 3F or more from the reading (never the nearest strike); (2) keep strikes where one side has zero or sub-Target depth, the other side holds >= 1,000 contracts, AND the other side's best bid is 98c or lower (crossing guard: if the favourite is bid at 99c, a 1c bid on the dead side is a 99c offer that trades at once -- we buy the dead side at 1c and leave the side empty); (3) rest a post-only bid for 1,000 contracts at 1c on the empty side ($10 per strike; rail refuses any price above 1c and any size above Target); (4) refill after a fill only while the remaining reward exceeds the $10 refill cost; (5) cancel at the hour close. Weight toward 00-09 ET, where most pools go unpaid. Under the filed scoring a lone 1c stack IS the reference price, so our side scores 1.0 and we receive ~50% of each now-valid snapshot. Alternative variant kept for completeness (weaker): two-sided quotes at the reference price on far strikes with index-triggered pulls -- population maker P&L was -$89 per market-hour against the $100 pool, i.e. ordinary quoting only breaks even.

chk.measured:
What kills it: other people are already doing this exact trick, and their 1c stacks get bought out within minutes. On a Miami strike 3F or more away from the temperature, a full-size (at least 1,000 contract) 1c stack on the empty side gets bought by people paying 99c for the near-certain side. At night, across 3 nights (hours closing 00-09 ET on 09-22, 09-23 and 09-24), there were 96 far strike-hours and 12 of them had a stack of 900 or more bought out. The stacks were placed at the top of the hour, as sizes like 1100 show, and the median buyout came 220 seconds after open (all times: 70, 120, 160, 190, 220, 220, 220, 230, 1120, 1340, 3230, 3270 s). When the stack was refilled it was bought out again 10, 10, 120 and 340 seconds later. The reward is at most $0.86 a minute (a 50% share of $100 over 58 minutes). About 3.7 minutes of paying time therefore earns about $3.20 for each $10 stack eaten, a loss of about $6.80 per filler even if Kalshi pays us.

A second, independent measure agrees. It counts minutes where 1-minute candles show a 1c bid on the empty side of a far strike, against the 99c buyouts on the same markets. Night: 232 stack-minutes, 20 buyouts of 300 or more, $243.66 eaten, which is $1.05 per stack-minute. Day, last 24 h (56 far day markets): 233 stack-minutes, $249.87 eaten, $1.07 per minute. Counting only buyouts inside or right after a minute where a stack showed gives $0.67 per minute. Every version is at or above the $0.86 reward rate, before any sharing with other stackers. The near-certain side lost 0 of 92 (24 h) and 0 of 96 (nights) far markets, so every buyout cost the full 1c; winning 99c on an upset never helped.

Artefact checks. (a) Candle closes miss stacks bought within the same minute and include small 1c bids, two biases in opposite directions. The buyout-timing measure uses trades only and gives the same answer. (b) Payment flags: 142 of 145 programs with zero two-sided minutes went unpaid (earlier scout, lip_paidflag_KXTEMPMIAH.out), so the idea's picture of a pool paid to nobody is correct. (c) The Kalshi help center page matches the CFTC filing: no price floor, a snapshot counts only when both sides reach Target, and a snapshot is worth at most 2.0. So a lone 1c stack would score. The rules are not the problem; the buyers are.

Also confirmed live at 10:15Z (06:15 ET): all 10 KXTEMPMIAH-26SEP2507 strikes carry $100, Target 1,000 programs, and 6 of 10 are one-sided and fillable with no crossing, so the pools are real. In the night hours of 09-25 (closes 00-05 ET), exactly 7 of 10 strikes went unpaid every hour. The empty sides are empty because stacks get eaten, not because nobody thought of the idea. KXTEMPMIAH is the only hourly temperature series with active programs right now; NYC, LA and Chicago have none. Payout flags land within about 20 minutes of a program ending.

idea.mechanism: The coin race carries a continuous LIP program: $20 per leg per 15-minute window, Target 1,000 (~$9,600/day). Late in each window the losing legs' books go thin or one-sided and snapshots are excluded. Each window: whenever a NON-leader leg's YES-bid side holds < 1,000 contracts, its NO side holds >= 1,000, and the best NO bid is 98c or lower (crossing guard), rest a post-only 1,000 YES at 1c on that leg ($10). If fewer than 200 contracts sit above 1c, the reference price drops to 1c and our stack takes nearly all of that side's credit. Never rest on the leader's NO side. Cancel at close. Self-trade safety: the live race bot only BUYS the leader's YES; our orders are YES buys on other legs, and a buy cannot match a buy. Dropping the leader/NO side gives up only ~8% of the reward.
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi's subsidy; in ~25% of late snapshots the pool pays nobody. The only people trading against the stack are buyers of dead-leg NO at 99c, and each of their fills costs us 1c.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Kalshi pays 1c stacks as filed (decided by I02). (2) The tape book rebuild counts depth correctly: collector gaps would make sides look thinner and overstate the unlock. (3) The tape's 1c sell rate (measured only over seconds when someone's 1c bid existed) is a fair proxy for flow into a new 1c bid. (4) No second stacker on the same sides. (5) The race bot never buys NO or non-leader legs in a way that could match our resting orders (verify in pinrun's race code). Our own race-bot fills are inside the tape's 1c cost and cannot be separated out.

   - new 99c NO bids arriving while we would rest: 334 per race, 325 of them in the last 180 s = another $3.30

- $9.18 reward per race
- minus $1.59 (sales we can see) to $4.89 (sales plus arriving 99c bids, capped at 1000 per leg)
- = $4.29 to $7.59 per race
- times 96 races per day = $412 to $729 per day, before three haircuts nobody has measured:

Per race: all 4 stacks (4 x 1,000 at 1c) get sold to us and every leg settles NO = -$40, offset only by whatever reward is paid. The worst race on the tape with the arrivals counted was -$35.49.

With no stop rule, a whole day of that is 96 x -$40 = -$3,840 in theory. With a stop after the first races where fills cost more than the reward, the worst day is about -$80 to -$150.

A leg we get filled on coming back to win is a GAIN (99c per contract), so it is not a risk. Over 490 leg-windows it happened 0 times.

chk.killer_risks:
1) Late fills nobody can see. In the last 3 minutes the tape has nobody's 1c YES bid, so how much would be sold to ours is invisible. Arriving 99c NO bids alone halve the net ($7.59 down to $4.29 per race), and take-only bots could erase it. The best-funded farmer pulls every stack at about 3 minutes before close without being filled, which suggests it thinks something is there.
2) Kalshi may not pay a 1c-only stack (I02). The rules text says it counts; that has never been checked against a real payout.
3) The farmer already running 1,000-21,120 at 1c on every leg could stay 3 minutes longer and take half or all of it.
4) The self-trade guard depends on one constant (PRICE_CEILING 0.98 in pinracearm.py). If anyone raises it to 0.99, the race bot fills against our own stack. Kalshi's self_trade_prevention_type should be set on both bots.
5) A post-only YES bid at 1c is rejected whenever a 99c NO bid rests. Late in the window that happens often (in the 10:30Z race, 3 of 4 dead legs in the last 90-130 s), so time on the book is patchy.

The probe: on ONE losing leg per race, in the last 180 s, whenever YES depth is under 1000, NO depth is at least 1000 and the best NO bid is 98c or lower, rest a post-only 1000 YES at 1c with self_trade_prevention set; cancel at close. Run 20 leg-windows, about 5 hours.
- Worst case $10 per probe, $200 total; about $1-3 per probe expected.
- Records the two unknowns directly: our own fills in contracts, and the program payout for each probe window.

Pass bar, written before looking:
(a) Kalshi pays at least $1.00 on at least 15 of the 20 probe windows where we sat alone for 90 s or more
(b) fill cost is at most 50% of total payout over the 20
(c) zero self-matches.
If it passes, widen to all losing legs with a stop when a rolling 8-race window's fills cost more than its payout.

Free and read-only in the meantime: keep latent.py running on new hours, and log for each race when the incumbent's 1c stacks are cancelled, to see whether it ever moves into the last 3 minutes.

I could not refute it. My own data makes the cost side look better than the checker thought, so what remains is two things nobody has checked with money. (1) Nobody has ever seen Kalshi actually pay for a stack of bids sitting only at 1c. The rules text and the help center say it counts, and the big incumbent farmer uses 1c stacks as filler, which points the same way, but no payout has been observed. (2) Competition. The pool is fixed at $20 per leg per window. The farmer already running 1,000-21,120 at 1c keeps its stacks on the winning leg to the end, and on 54 of 732 losing leg-windows someone's 1,000+ stack stayed on a dead leg into the last 3 minutes. If they start staying on every dead leg, our share drops toward 1000/(1000+their size), which is about 5% against 21k. Smaller risks: Kalshi can revoke program status for "inconsistent with the purpose", and there is a rare tail where one taker buys 1,000 NO at 99c in a single print. I saw that once in 180 races, on a leg that did not yet look dead, costing -$10 on that leg; the worst race in my sample was -$25.90.

The checker's killer risk, late invisible takers plus arriving 99c NO bids hitting our stack, is NOT supported by the tape:
(a) Big 1c YES stacks that DID stay on dead-looking losing legs (no YES bid above 1c, best NO >= 97c) in the last 180 s. Main sample: 54 leg-windows, 4,393 stack-seconds, 2 contracts sold into them. Separate holdout hours: 21 leg-windows, 1,572 stack-seconds, 16 contracts sold.

The stack offering exactly that 99c NO sat unhit. So the late 99c bidders rest and do not cross, and counting them as fills against us (checker's $3.30/race) overstates the cost.
(c) Live, 11:45Z race today, REST polls every 15 s over the last 4 minutes: 4 losing legs, placeable most of the time (XRP and BTC in all 16 polls), NO depth 2,800-3,900, best NO bid 88-97c. Zero 1c prints on any leg in the last 240 s.

idea.name: Frechet combo desk: quote 15-min crypto/commodity combos only at prices the leg books make riskless
idea.family: combos (RFQ layer) x 15-min crypto/commodity leg books we already stream
markets: KXMVECROSSCATEGORY (combos whose legs are all 15-min markets)
idea.mechanism: A combo pays $1 only if every leg wins, so regardless of true odds: (1) combo <= its weakest leg, so combo NO + that leg's YES pays >= $1 in every outcome; (2) combo >= 1 - sum of each leg's loss chance, so combo YES + the losing side of every leg pays >= $1. Steps: poll the public RFQ list (GET /communications/rfqs) for combos whose legs are all 15-min markets on our tape; from live leg books (walked through full depth) quote no better for the requester than weakest-leg cost + fee + margin when they buy YES, or 1 - sum(opposite-leg costs) - fees - margin when they sell YES; when a requester accepts, use the confirmation window (docs: 3 s high-volume, 30 s standard; the other scout read a 1 s maker last look) to buy the hedge leg(s) with immediate-or-cancel orders FIRST and confirm only if the hedge filled, otherwise let the quote lapse; hold to settlement (<= 15 min). Variant considered and rejected: price combos from pinrun's own partial-average fair value and carry the risk (the 'crypto-combo house'): measured +$732 and -$49 for makers at two closes, n=2.
idea.why_mispriced: Requesters look like pin-stacking bots and retail (one 9-leg family re-requested 11-21 times in 2 minutes at 2 AM ET); they take the best quote. Incumbent makers quote ~8c wide around the leg books without hedging and without the bounds, and the leg books lag the index in the last minute. A hedged maker wins whether or not the requester is informed. At 07:15Z every leg won, so the unhedged incumbent lost 6.1c/contract where a hedged maker would have locked ~37c.
idea.must_be_true: (a) A retail API account may create and confirm RFQ quotes -- unverified (Create Quote docs list no restriction; a public GitHub CLI quotes; Oddpool saw zero maker quotes on non-sports RFQs in its test, yet crypto combos are being filled now). (b) Hedge legs fill at walked-book prices within the window (our Kalshi ack ~115 ms). (c) Combo maker fee ~0.035*p*(1-p) (50% of taker). (d) Our quote is the best one often enough. (e) Kalshi permits hedge-then-confirm and lapsed confirmations without penalty. (f) The flow is not one requester family at night: all 7 measured closes were 02:15-04:00 ET and one burst is most of the dollars. Artefacts already addressed: ticker-channel lag (book rebuilt from orderbook_delta), dust on top of book (full-depth walk; one case had 0.1 contract at the weakest price), legs known only for combos seen in the RFQ list (undercounts).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 if the account cannot quote. If it can: realistic $10-50/day with occasional $100-600 bursts. Measured pool anyone could have locked at prices that actually traded, walked through full depth: $697 over 7 closes -- per close $31.31, $4.41, $1.16 (06:15-06:45Z), $635.44, $16.08, $5.89, $3.27 (07:15-08:00Z); typical ~$5, one $635. Ceiling ~96 closes x $5 x half the gap x half won ~ $120/day, before incumbents tighten, multi-leg hedge slippage and daytime differences.
idea.data_needed: (1) One DEMO-environment test that POST /communications/quotes works for his account type (zero risk; demo orders are permitted) -- decides whether the idea exists. (2) A 3-day read-only shadow desk: poll RFQs with legs on our tape, compute the bound quote from live books, log every combo trade, record whether our quote would have been best and what walked hedge we'd have got. Pre-registered bar e.g. >= $10/day of shadow riskless profit after margin, including daytime closes.
idea.evidence_so_far: Book-confirmed full-depth walk: hour 06: 56 candidate trades, 36 with riskless profit, $36.88; hour 07: 96 candidates, 62 riskless, $660.68. Near-close: 06:15Z 11 crypto-combo trades in the last 110 s, 966 contracts, $732 premium, all lost for the buyer (e.g. 451 at 85.7c 31 s before close on a 9-leg combo); 06:30Z 21 trades, settled ones gave makers -$48.60 on $189 premium (maker bought YES at 90.2c when legs implied 98% and sold at 98.2c). chk.measured:
HEADLINE: 91% of the claimed pool ($635 of $697) comes from a gap in our recording. The part left over is mostly the other maker's last-look luck, and we could not have captured it.

1) The $635 "burst" at the 03:15 ET close on 09-25 is an artefact. Our tape has zero orderbook and ticker records for every market from 03:10 to 03:16 ET (tape_minutes_07.out: minutes 10-15 of hour T07 are missing for every close, and the 03:30 window starts at minute 16). The scout's leg books were frozen at 03:09:46 ET. Kalshi's REST trade history shows the COPPER-down leg trading at about 98-99c at 03:13 ET, not the "55c" the frozen book showed (legtrades_0315.out). The market settled NO, so that leg won. The 1,102-contract combo at 93.9c was fairly priced and was never outside the bounds. The fingerprint of a frozen book is edges that are identical when evaluated at 0, 1, 3 and 10 s before the trade, and that is what walkoff_night07.out shows. Side finding: any study that uses tape hour 2026-09-25 T07 is contaminated by this 6-minute hole.

2) I rebuilt the walker with a filter that drops frozen books (walk.py and walk_off.py; the self-test passes). It covers 9 closes with live books: 3 daytime (10:15, 10:30, 10:45 ET on 09-24; the 10:45 close is undercounted because the GET cap was hit) and 6 night closes (02:15-04:00 ET on 09-25, excluding 03:15). The sample is 593 combo trades whose legs are all on our tape, 86,094 contracts. Walking full depth at the trade instant, the pool is $94.03, or $10.45 per close. It reproduces the scout's $36.88 for hour 06 exactly.

3) The trade instant is the wrong moment. Makers quote when the RFQ appears, and the trade prints a median 3.8 s later (quartiles 2.8-5.2 s; n = 29 crypto-only RFQs matched to a trade within 10 s, from sports-props-parlays-futures/rfqs.json and alltrades_recent.json). For each trade I kept the smaller of its edge at the trade instant and its edge N seconds earlier:
- 1 s earlier: $64.35
- 3 s earlier: $31.01. Of that, $14.06 comes from micro-price combos (priced under 2c or over 98c) that each need $700-$5,900 of capital to earn $1-$5.50.
- Excluding micro-price combos: $16.95 over 9 closes. That is $1.88 per close on average, with a median of $0.09. 4 of the 9 closes were at or below $0.10, and one close (02:15 ET, $9.66) is 57% of the total (check-I06/tape_minutes and walkoff_*.out; table printed in this session).

The edges grow toward the confirm instant. That is what the incumbent maker's last look produces: it quotes, the legs move its way, and it confirms. This also supports reading taker_side as the requester's side.

4) Can a retail account quote? Kalshi told Sportico that "any Kalshi member may respond to RFQs via Kalshi's API", and the Create Quote docs list no restriction. Our account is usage_tier basic with a write bucket of 100/s, and GET /communications/id returns an ID. None of this is proven until a demo POST works. The confirm window is 3 s for combos (they are classed as high-volatility markets) and 30 s for standard markets. The docs say nothing about penalties for failing to confirm. The combo series fee_type is quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees, so makers DO pay. I could not find the rate (the fee PDF returned 429); I assumed 0.035·p·(1−p) (the scout's working assumption, 50% of taker; not taken from Kalshi). Oddpool counted 13 quoter IDs, 5 of which quote only combos, and they answer in under 200 ms.

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
The ceiling assumes we win every one of these trades at the full gap and quote 3 s before the trade, excluding micro-price combos. It is $1.88/close × 96 closes = $181/day. Without the one big close (02:15 ET): $0.91 × 96 = $88/day. From the median close: $0.09 × 96 = $9/day.

We cannot see the incumbent's quote, so we would capture about half the gap and win about 60-80% of the time, with some lapses. That is a realistic fraction of about 0.3-0.4. Leg taker fees and the assumed combo maker fee are already deducted. If the combo maker fee is the full 0.07·p·(1−p), subtract up to 0.9c per contract.

- $900 bank: about $30/day as a point estimate, honest range $0-60/day. Capital fits, because the non-micro trades are at most about 600 contracts, roughly $600 tied up for up to 3 minutes. But it competes with pinrun for the bank in the same final minutes.
- $5k bank: about $45/day, range $0-100/day. The micro-price trades become affordable, but they pay only 0.04-0.2c per contract and the gaps are below one tick, so they add little.

With n = 9 closes (sd about $3.1 per close), the sample cannot tell a $0/day pool from a roughly $200/day ceiling.
chk.worst_case: The hedge leg fills with an immediate-or-cancel order, but the confirm fails (the 3 s window is missed or the API stalls). That leaves a leg bet with no combo against it. At a 300-contract size cap on a leg near 60c, that is about -$180 if the leg loses. If several quotes on the same close fail together during an outage, it is about -$500. A leg-side mapping bug would leave a sold combo unhedged: up to size × combo NO cost, about -$280 at 300 contracts. Mitigation: cap each quote at 300 contracts and total pending hedge exposure at $150-200 per close at the $900 bank. Separately, Kalshi could restrict the account's quoting if it lapses often, and lapsing is the core of the design.
chk.killer_risks:
1) Most of the measured "free money" is the incumbent's last-look drift. It shows up only at the confirm instant, not when quotes are made. The ceiling we could have captured is about $1.9/close on average and about $0.1 at the median.
2) The trade price is the best incumbent quote. We never see it, so how much of the gap we keep and how often we win are unmeasured.
3) Retail quoting permission is unproven, and so is Kalshi's policy on makers who routinely fail to confirm.
4) The combo maker fee rate is unknown. The series confirms makers pay.
5) The sample is 9 closes in two time-of-day slices, and one close is 57% of the dollars.
6) The capital overlaps with pinrun in the same final minutes.
7) The build is not small: an RFQ WebSocket, live bounds on up to 14 leg books, and an immediate-or-cancel hedge followed by a confirm inside 3 s.
8) Also: 6-minute tape hole 03:10-03:16 ET on 09-25; the scout's leg books for the 03:15 ET close were frozen at 03:09:46 ET. Any other study that uses hour T07 is affected.

Three steps, cheapest first. Step 0 needs no new code: the pull and walker scripts already exist.

Step 0 (about 1,500 read-only GETs, about 1 hour unattended). Run pull.py and walk_off.py on 8 more tape hours spread over 09-20..09-24, covering weekday day, evening and night plus one weekend hour. First run tape_minutes.py on each hour and drop any hour with a recording gap. Pass bar, written now: with micro-price excluded, the mean smaller-of-two edge 3 s before the trade is at least $1.00 per close, and no single close is more than 30% of the total. Fail means dead.

Step 1 (zero risk, and demo orders are allowed). POST /communications/quotes against one demo RFQ, then DELETE it. Pass: a 201 response, and the quote appears in GET /communications/quotes?creator_user_id=<our comms id>.

Step 2 (3-day read-only shadow). Subscribe to the communications WebSocket for new RFQs. For each RFQ whose legs are all crypto or commodity 15-min markets, compute the bound 0.3 s after it appears from our live leg books. For each combo trade, log the price, the size and the bound at the trade. Metric M = Σ max(0, px − max(bound at quote, bound at trade) − 1c), over trades priced from 2c to 98c with at most 300 contracts. Pass bar, written now: M is at least $40/day on each of the 3 days, including a weekday 9am-5pm ET session, with no single close above 30% of that day's M. That works out to roughly $13/day realised. Fail means dead.
chk.capital_needed: About $600 per close, tied up for 3 minutes or less, for the non-micro trades; each hedged package costs about $1 per contract until settlement. At $900 this competes with pinrun's final 45 s. At $5k it is not binding, and the micro-price trades ($700-$5,900 each) become possible, though they add only a few cents to a few dollars each.

ref.strongest_objection:
Kalshi's own rulebook forbids the step that makes this "riskless". Rule 5.3(g) was filed with the CFTC on 2025-11-25 and took effect 2025-12-11. It says: "A party to private pre-execution communications shall not enter, modify, or cancel orders on any market to take advantage of information conveyed during such communications, except in accordance with this Rule." The acceptance message is private: only the quoter learns which side the requester took and how many contracts. The design waits for that message, buys the leg hedge with IOC orders, and confirms only if the hedge filled. That is entering orders in other markets on private pre-execution information, and the Rule has no pre-hedge carve-out. Two more rule problems:
- Rule 5.3(h) says quotes must be for "bona fide Transactions". In my replay, 27-34% of the quotes a requester accepted would have been left unconfirmed because the hedge no longer paid.
- Rule 5.3(e) makes the requester's order match better resting combo orders first. Our quote can therefore fill for less than the hedge we already bought, leaving a naked leg.
Kalshi says it surveils every order that comes out of this system. Pre-hedging is also the step FX's Global Code frowns on during last look.

The compliant alternative is to hedge only after the combo trade prints publicly. That version is not riskless, and my data cannot tell it from zero. On 10 clean closes it made +$13.98 per close at a 3c margin. But the 95% band is about -$17 to +$45 per close, 86% of the profit came from one close, and the worst single trade was -$51.72: SILVER-up went 54c, then 86c, then 98c in the 2 seconds after the confirm decision.

Timing is also uncertain. The rulebook says high-volatility markets get a 2 s confirm window and a 3 s execution timer; the docs say 3 s and 1 s. Under the rulebook timing, the pre-hedge pool halves.

The data side is NOT where the idea fails, and I said so rather than hide it. On clean tape the pool is larger than the checker found. The checker's hours 07-08Z on 09-25 sit after a collector reconnect that restarted the sequence numbers. Both walkers applied the new snapshots at the wrong point, so 324 evaluations saw books with negative sizes, and those closes scored about $0.

Unverified, all bearing on whether it works at all:
- whether a retail account may quote (only the demo POST can settle it);
- the combo maker fee (secondary sources say 0.0175·p·(1−p), not 0.035);
- whether our quote reaches the requester before it accepts (incumbents answer in under 100-200 ms);
- whether collateral is reserved per open quote, which would cap a $900 bank at a handful of RFQs at once.

idea.name: Print-to-Fed staircase: read the jobs/CPI number, beat the Fed-decision book's 10-60 s repricing (plus slower sibling series)
idea.family: economics x Fed-decision markets (one public number moves a slow, liquid Kalshi complex)
markets: siblings: KXFED-<meeting>-T* (rate level; e.g. T3.75 = same event as a hike of >= 25), FEDHIKE-<date>, KXFEDDECISION later meetings, KXRATECUTCOUNT, KXFEDCHGCOUNT
read-only consensus inputs: KXPAYROLLS, KXU3, KXCPI, KXCPICORE
idea.mechanism: (1) Before 8:30 ET on NFP/CPI days, take each Kalshi release ladder's last pre-release prices as the consensus distribution. (2) At 12:30:00Z (EDT) read the number from api.bls.gov, polling from 12:29:59; require the reference-period field to match the expected month. (3) If the headline lies outside the ladder's 20-80% band and the secondary number (U3 / core CPI) does not contradict it, buy the matching direction on the next-meeting KXFEDDECISION leg (hot/strong -> hike more likely: buy H25 YES / H0 NO; cold/weak -> the reverse), limit a few cents through the pre-release price, target on the book within ~3 s, size capped at the bank. (4) Exit 2-15 minutes later at the new level; do not hold to the meeting (adds direction risk, no edge; the 08-07 trade would have lost at settlement). (5) Sibling leg: when the lead book moves >= 5c inside 15 s, compute each exact sibling's implied price and lift siblings still >= 4c stale; exit on convergence or hold where the sibling is the identical event. Do not chase scheduled LOCKS (swept in 2-5 s); only probability updates leave a window.
idea.why_mispriced: The Fed book re-prices in steps over 10-60 s after a big print while resting orders at the old price are swept: the resting side is market makers or larger holders slow to pull or step quotes; takers at 3-30 s are humans and slower bots. One competitor fires exactly 200 contracts at +1.5 s every big release, then stops. Siblings have separate, thinner books with fewer watchers.
idea.must_be_true: (a) We get the number within ~1-2 s: api.bls.gov answered 200 in 0.24 s today but its update time at the release second is unknown; www.bls.gov returns 403 to a script; paid wires are faster than us. (b) The ladder-surprise direction rule keeps working (3 of 3 big moves -- tiny n; mixed reports are the danger). (c) The next meeting stays uncertain (Oct H25 67-68c now); a foregone meeting shrinks moves to 0-3c. (d) Stale depth stays at tens of thousands of contracts. (e) Siblings are the same event or monotone in it (rate-level vs decision wording).
