chk.measured:
This source is the TRADE TAPE (other people's fills), not our fills. I made 383 read-only GETs covering every NFP and CPI release from 2025-02 to 2026-09: 36 real releases, plus 5 controls. The controls are dates in the 2025 shutdown when the ladders closed but no number came out. For each release I pulled the next-meeting KXFEDDECISION legs over [t0-1800 s, t0+905 s]. Trades from before 2026-07-27 come from /historical/trades.

1) HOW OFTEN THE FED BOOK MOVES: 13 of 36 releases moved some next-meeting leg by 5c or more. It is regime-dependent: the Mar-Jun 2026 meetings were foregone and there were zero moves in those 4 months. The Oct 2026 meeting is in doubt right now: H25 bid 0.67 / ask 0.68, H0 0.31/0.32, 54k-68k contracts within 5c each side of H25, open interest 498k. Fee type is quadratic_with_maker_fees, multiplier 1.

2) DIRECTION RULE (no hindsight). Inputs are the Kalshi ladder's own last pre-print prices plus the printed value (expiration_value). Ladders that traded after the print are excluded (26JAN payrolls). Rule: headline outside the ladder's 20-80% band gives the direction. It fired 20 times: 12 right-way (the expected rate change moved at least 1 bp our way), 0 wrong-way, 8 no move. The idea's filter ("secondary number must not contradict") only removed two winners, 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-07, so drop it.

3) CAPTURE. Our order arrives at +T s and takes the liquidity that other takers actually hit on our side at or below the pre-print price +6c, re-swept for 60 s. Exit at the 2-15 min VWAP minus both taker fees and 0.5c. Size is capped at 20% of the leg's 2-15 min volume. Leg = whichever of the two extreme legs is nearer 50c; the middle legs are not monotone, and trading C25 on 2025-09-11 would have lost $164.
- $900 cap, over 601 days: +2.5 s gives $1,422 total (13 fills). +10 s gives $800.
- Since 2026-07-01 (86 days, 5 fills): +2.5 s gives $726 (07-02 $42, 07-14 $206, 08-07 $186, 09-04 $94, 09-11 $199). +10 s gives $143.
- The top 3 releases (2025-07-03, 2025-08-01, 2026-07-14) supply $740 of the $1,422.

4) SPEED RACE (the key finding). The first trade after the print on the traded leg came at +5.5 to +39 s in 2025, +6 to +8 s in Jul-Aug 2026, and +1.27 s / +1.46 s in Sep 2026 (a 200-lot bot). Time for the leg to go half-way to its new level (from the pre-print price to the 2-15 min average): 38-200 s in 2025, 22-31 s in Jul-Aug 2026, 10-19 s in Sep 2026. At +10 s the two September releases paid $0-53.

5) ARTEFACT CHECKS.
- Flipped direction loses $1,217 in total at $900 (-$37 to -$424 per event).
- A coin-flip direction at a no-news second loses $3.09 per fill (n=88), which is just the fees.
- On the 5 no-print shutdown dates the rule stayed silent and the book moved 0-3c.
- Remaining artefact: the capture assumes nobody faster than us eats the stale depth between +1 and +2.5 s. That is exactly what is changing.

6) READING THE NUMBER. www.bls.gov returns 403 to a script even with a browser UA. api.bls.gov v2 returns 200 with no-cache headers (latest CES0000000001 = M08 159,075). Its limit is 50 requests per 10 s and 500 per day with a free key. When it updates relative to the release second is UNMEASURED.

7) CALENDAR. Government is funded to Dec 11 (CR signed 09-02, news source), so Oct 2 NFP and Oct 14 CPI are on. Current Oct 2 ladder: payrolls median about 90k, 20-80 band about 17k to 125k+ (the top strike clamps it); U3 median 4.06%. CPI Oct 14: headline band 0.44-0.62, core 0.12-0.27. The sibling-series part of the idea was NOT measured.

8) Collector and crypto_feeds both alive; 15.8 GB disk free.

chk.worst_case:
The measured losses come from the flipped-direction control (what a misread, stale value or reversed rule would have done):
- $500 cap: worst -$230 on one event.
- $900 cap: worst -$424 (2025-09-11, 5,413 cheap C26 contracts); more typically -$160 to -$250.
- $5k: worst -$2,048 on one event.

The direction rule itself was never wrong in 20 fires, but n is small. The realistic worst day at a $900 bank is about half the bank on one misread print. Guards: cap each event at $500 and 5,000 contracts; require the reference period in the API reply to match the month expected.
chk.killer_risks:
1) SPEED. The edge is being competed away right now. The first reaction went from +9-39 s (2025) to +1.3 s (Sep 2026), and at +10 s the last two releases paid $0-53. The strategy lives or dies on reading the number by about +2 s, and api.bls.gov's timing at the release second is unmeasured. Paid wires and the existing +1.3 s bot are ahead of us, and every new bot at +1-2 s eats the stale depth before our +2.5 s order.

2) REGIME. It only pays while the next meeting is in doubt: the Mar-Jun 2026 meetings were foregone and it paid $0 for 4 months.

3) SMALL SAMPLE. 20 rule fires and 13 fills; 3 releases supply half the dollars.

4) CAPITAL CLASH. At a $900 bank, a $500-900 position for about 15 minutes starves pinrun for 1-2 crypto closes on each release morning.

5) DATA OUTAGES. Government funding runs out Dec 11, which could cancel the December releases (it did in Oct-Nov 2025).

6) LEG CHOICE. The middle legs are not monotone in the surprise (C25 on 2025-09-11 lost $164), so only the extreme leg may be traded.

7) SIBLINGS. The sibling-series add-on is unmeasured.

ref.strongest_objection:
The profit only exists in a gap of about 1.6 seconds, and two named competitors are closing it. On the latest big print (CPI 2026-09-11), all of the money sat between +1.46 s and +3.07 s after 12:30:00Z.
- At 12:30:03.0676Z one bot swept the whole stale layer on H25: 8,875 contracts from 0.60 to 0.64 in a single order.
- 2.4 ms later (12:30:03.0700Z) it swept H0: 12,055 contracts from 0.39 down to 0.35.

The same large sweeper shows up on every big 2026 print, in orders of 10k-36k contracts. Its reaction time has fallen:
- 07-14: +5.34 s (35,944 contracts on H25)
- 08-07: +7.96 s (20,000 on H0)
- 09-04: +4.84 s (10,000+ on H0)
- 09-11: +3.07 s, and this time on both legs

A second bot is already in front of us. It trades both legs at +1.18 to +1.46 s (09-04 and 09-11) and stops at 200 contracts each. If it simply raises its size, the layer disappears at about +1.2 s.

Arrival time decides everything. On 09-11, arriving at +2.5 s nets $205 and arriving at +3.1 s nets $7. At +10 s the last two prints paid $0 and $14.

The +10 s money in the recent sample came from the sweeper hitting the other leg:
- 08-07 paid $172 at +10 s only because the sweeper hit H0, not our pre-registered H25.
- 07-14 paid at +5 s only because it hit H25, not our H0.
- On 09-11 it hit both legs.

So the checker's +10 s fallback of $1-2/day is really about $0 going forward.

Our only free source, api.bls.gov, has release-second latency that nobody has measured, and the documents I found lean slow:
- BLS's own API features page still says "There is a one day lag between published data and its availability for retrieval from the API". That is the v1.0 addendum, dated 2013.
- PageCrawl, a web-monitoring vendor, says "API series sometimes update slightly after the headline release, so the page monitor usually fires first."
- The LABSTAT flat-file timestamps (Last-Modified exactly 12:30:00 GMT) are nominal. ci.data.0.Current carries 12:30:00 for 07-31 even though its directory was modified at 11:01 ET, so those timestamps tell us nothing about when data actually appears.

Capital: pinrun's 12:30 close is still unsettled at the print. Positions are about $85 each (autosize 83-85, max 2 per close), so only about $650 of the $900 bank is free.

Not refuted as "needs data": if the API really is live within about 0.5 s, a 4 Hz poller could land at about +1 s and beat both bots. But the pre-registered pass bar should be tightened from "value visible by +2.0 s" to "value visible by +1.0 s". The sweeper was 0.57 s behind a +2.5 s arrival and gaining roughly 1-2 s per month.

idea.name: Sign-up bonuses at other US venues (prediction venues and sportsbooks), hedged on Kalshi
idea.family: promotions x Kalshi sports hedge (matched betting with Kalshi as the lay side)
markets: state-licensed online sportsbooks (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Caesars, Fanatics)
idea.mechanism: Open each venue/book account he does not already hold (he holds Kalshi, Polymarket US, Gemini). Spend each bonus/credit on an underdog (10-30c, or long sportsbook odds) in a game Kalshi also lists, and immediately buy the other side on Kalshi sized to equalise outcomes: h = B*(1-a)/a contracts for a credit B spent at price a (same formula as the Poly credit idea). Kalshi game books run ~1c spreads with fee <= 1.75c at 50c (MLB multiplier 0.5), the cheapest hedge leg in the country. Stake-not-returned bonus bets convert at ~70-85% on longshots. The bot places the Kalshi leg and computes sizes; the venue legs are manual. Underdog's 50% deposit match (up to $1,000, 1x playthrough) adds ~$0.45 per $1 deposited minus 1-2% playthrough cost if spare cash exists.
idea.why_mispriced: Customer-acquisition budgets: venues pay credit/bonus bets to get sign-ups. No trading counterparty is harmed; nothing deceptive (real accounts, own money, hedging elsewhere is not prohibited as a general rule).
idea.must_be_true: He is a NEW user at each; his state is not excluded (NV excluded by most; sportsbooks need a licensed state). Each credit is stake-not-returned or better. Each venue's terms do not void bonus winnings for hedging (read each for 'bonus abuse'/'hedging' language). Sports settlement rules (ties, postponements, overtime, cancellations) match Kalshi's for the chosen game. Nobody bans him before payout. Not bot-runnable beyond a helper calculator. Promo amounts below come from public listings, NOT verified in-app.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not per day: a one-off. Prediction venues ~$300-400 net from fixed offers (DK $200 as 4 weekly $50 drops, FanDuel up to $100 as $20/day for 5 days expiring 24 h after receipt, ProphetX $75, Novig $25, Plus500 $20, OG $10) at ~70-85% conversion. Sportsbooks $500-2,000 total if his state is licensed, $0 if not. Kalshi hedge capital ~$150-400 per game for the game's duration.
idea.data_needed: His state of residence; each venue's current offer terms read for hedging/abuse clauses and credit mechanics; one game hedged end to end at the smallest offer first.
idea.evidence_so_far: Offer amounts from si.com/prediction-markets/promos, covers.com and casino.org listings read 2026-09-25 (web, not verified in-app); sportsbook sizes are general knowledge, not measured. Kalshi game books ~1c spread (median 1c on 6 NFL games in the lead-lag pull). Novig: CFTC DCM since 2026-06-16, live in 47 states since 2026-08-04.

The promo amounts are not: they come from third-party listings (si.com, covers, cbssports, casino.org) and none was checked in-app. The two primary terms pages that matter most (fanduel.com/predicts/bonus-offer-terms and predictions.draftkings.com/en/promos) returned 403.

1) Kalshi hedge-leg cost. Read-only books on 2026-09-25, about 150 GETs. Script: books.py, output in books.out and books.json.
- Median half-spread 0.5c on each of: 18 MLB, 18 NFL and 17 NCAAF games. The exceptions are games a day or more out.
- Taker fee: MLB 0.62-0.87c (multiplier 0.5), NFL/NCAAF 0.5-1.74c. The fee type is quadratic_with_maker_fees, so makers pay too.
- Median depth within 1c of the best ask: MLB $159k, NFL $1.2M, NCAAF $329k. Our size never touches it.
- NHL (preseason): median half-spread 3c and median $19 within 1c. Unusable.

2) Settlement rules (rules.py, rules.json).
- NFL tie: Kalshi pays 50c to each team. 4 of 164 settled NFL markets were ties (2 preseason games). A sportsbook pushes a tied 2-way moneyline, so the Kalshi hedge loses about 30c a contract. Avoid NFL.
- MLB: 1,000 of 1,000 settled markets were a clean yes/no. A postponed game stays open up to 2 days on Kalshi while books void it, so we exit the Kalshi leg at about 1.5c a contract.
- NCAAF: no ties.

3) Conversion model (calc.py, calc.out). Per $1 of stake-not-returned credit at the best underdog price, with the venue's price 1-2c above fair:
- MLB 0.69-0.75, NCAAF 0.67-0.72.
- DraftKings Predictions charges $0.01 a contract, which drops these to 0.61-0.68.
- At a 20c underdog: 0.61-0.71. At a 30c underdog: 0.57-0.64.
- Sportsbook bonus bets, with the book 2-3 points of probability over fair on the underdog: 0.62-0.69 at +425 to +525.
- IF a prediction venue pays the credit back on a win (unverified), the favourite becomes the best buy and conversion is 0.91-0.97 under the 60c/80c price caps.

4) Offer facts found. All are listings unless marked primary.
- DraftKings Predictions: now $150 as 3 x $50, one every 7 days. Sports contracts in only 18 states (those without legal online sportsbooks). $0.01/contract fee.
- FanDuel Predicts: sports in 18 states. Up to $100 as $20/day for 5 days, each needing a $1 cash trade and expiring 24 h after receipt. FanDuel's own terms-page title says '$25'.
- ProphetX: $75 as 3 x $25, trades at 80c or below, $50 of qualifying trades; all states except Nevada. Its terms say 'proceeds ... withdrawable', which is ambiguous on whether the credit comes back.

ref.strongest_objection:
I found nothing that stops this from making money. I did find four things that change the verdict.

1. It is not established as viable. Everything depends on facts nobody has checked:
- which state he lives in;
- whether he has ever had a DraftKings or FanDuel account, sportsbook or prediction app;
- the real in-app terms of each offer.
The checker lists his state as "unknown and decisive", so "viable" claims more than was shown. It is a one-time manual promo grab, not a repeatable edge the bot can run.
- Novig is closed in Arizona, Michigan and Nevada (si.com, 2026-09-24).
- Kalshi sports are court-blocked in Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, Nevada and Washington.
- In the roughly 18 states without legal online sportsbooks, DraftKings and FanDuel sports predictions exist but sportsbook offers do not. In sportsbook states it is the other way round.

2. The checker's baseball numbers are too high. It gives baseball 0.69-0.75 of each credit dollar back, but that needs underdogs priced 11-15c, and baseball barely has them.
- Of 15 baseball games on today's slate, 1 had an underdog below 30c (Dodgers at Giants, 23.5c).
- Of 43 baseball games listed on Kalshi, 5 had an underdog between 10c and 35c.
- Kalshi lists baseball games only through 2026-09-27, the last day of the regular season. Playoff underdogs sit at about 40-48c, which returns about 0.50-0.55 of each credit dollar.
- The cheap underdogs are in college football (Saturdays only) and the NFL.
- The checker's 0.60-0.66 used for the totals is about right for NFL and college games, not for baseball.

3. Tax cuts about another 20 points off every credit dollar. The repo's own ledger (results/tax/kalshi_2026_ledger.csv, "base C") covers the case where betting income counts as gambling and he takes the standard deduction. Then:
- when the underdog wins, the whole win is taxed, and the Kalshi hedge loss that same day cannot be deducted;
- so the taxed amount is about 1.23 times the credit, while the real gain is only about 0.65 of it;
- at a 22% tax rate he keeps about 0.38 of each credit dollar, against 0.51 if the result is taxed as one net number.

4. The checker's warning that a hedge over about $209 halts the live bot is wrong. EXTERNAL_DETECT is on in live (restart_bot.ps1 does not pass --no-external-detect). classify_bank_move therefore reads the hedge's cash leaving as a withdrawal and lowers the bot's record-high balance (the one its 20% loss stop is measured from) by the same amount, so the stop does not fire. The real side effects:
- the bot sizes itself smaller while a hedge is open, costing roughly $0.50-1 per hedge;
- a losing hedge never counts toward that 20% loss stop;
- the bot does not pick up the sports position as its own: its position check (ktruth) skips series it does not trade.

idea.name: PortWatch Tuesday sniper (chokepoint transit counts)
idea.family: politics/shipping chokepoint counts x public IMF PortWatch ArcGIS feed
idea.mechanism: All six series settle on IMF PortWatch daily transit counts and close Tuesday 13:00Z. PortWatch's public ArcGIS layer (services9.arcgis.com/.../Daily_Chokepoints_Data/FeatureServer/0, no key) gets the new week's rows before that close. (1) Poll the layer every 2-5 s on Tuesdays 11:30-13:00Z. (2) Only when all 7 daily rows for the week are present (never act on a partial load: first-wave trades came 9 s BEFORE the edit stamp), compute weekly sum, peak day and max-day per chokepoint. (3) Buy every stale ask on the now-locked side up to 95-97c, only on strikes >= 2 transits away from the computed number. (4) Hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: Resting makers (the same LIP-farming depth, tens of thousands of contracts) and overnight limit orders are not pulled when the data lands. On 09-22 Hormuz was swept within seconds, but Panama and Suez were repriced only 1-5 minutes later.
idea.must_be_true: (a) The layer updates before 13:00Z on most Tuesdays -- verified exactly once (09-22 12:15:34Z, 44.4 min before close); the tape shows repricing bursts 0-50 min before close in 6 of 8 weeks and none in 2. (b) Kalshi settles on first-published numbers: current API sums reproduce 218 of 228 settled markets; all 10 mismatches are weeks ending 07-19..08-16 (later data revisions). (c) Enough locked-side asks survive our poll latency on Panama/Suez/Bab-el-Mandeb.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $10-40/day averaged (one burst a week, ~$70-280 per Tuesday at $900). Tape gross across all takers: ~$11.4k over 8 weeks in the last hour; $6.4k within +/-5 min on 09-22 alone, $3.9k of it 60 s or more after the edit stamp.
idea.data_needed: Four Tuesdays of read-only logging: the ArcGIS layer every 5 s (first-visibility time, row completeness) plus books of the ~40 open markets every 5 s 11:30-13:00Z. Pass bar: data complete >= 2 min before close in >= 3 of 4 weeks, and >= $50 of locked-side asks at <= 95c still resting 10 s after first visibility.
idea.evidence_so_far: pw_meta.json lastEditDate 2026-09-22 12:15:34Z. pw_check.py 218/228 reproduced. pw_wave.py (week ending 09-20, all 6 series, contracts bought on the true side at <= 95c): -60..0 s $2,398; 0-10 s $0; 10-60 s $138; 60-300 s $3,360 (Panama $1,092, Suez $1,535); 300-2,700 s $518. hormuz_path.py: bursts at 0-10, 20-30, 20-30, 0-10, 30-40, 40-50 min before close; 2 weeks no burst. chk.measured:
WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM: Kalshi's trade history (other people's trades), not our fills. A trade only proves someone was selling at that price at that moment. It does not prove we would have been the one to buy it. The Tuesday data release was timestamped exactly once.

1) THE RULES MATCH THE IDEA. All 6 series have the standard Kalshi fee (0.07 x price x (1 - price)). They close at 13:00Z, and the rules say "resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM ... once complete data is available." Kalshi settled 09-22 at about 14:37Z, roughly 2h20m after the data appeared. Kalshi types the settlement value in by hand: some weeks read "Above 290" or "September 18" instead of a count.

2) THE SOURCE'S OWN SCHEDULE IS THE PROBLEM. PortWatch's methodology page says the daily chokepoint data is "updated weekly on Tuesdays at 9 AM ET". That is exactly Kalshi's close. An early upload is a habit, not a promise. On 09-22 the data layer's last edit was 12:15:34Z, which is 44 min before close. The layer has not been edited since (checked 09-25). That means one load a week, with no mid-week revisions this week.

3) THE UPLOAD TIME, READ FROM WHEN PRICES FIRST JUMPED EACH TUESDAY (8 Tuesdays, 9 weekly events): 44.6, 33.9, 28.7, 26.6, 5.4 and about 30/10 min before close. On 2 Tuesdays (09-01 and 09-08) there was no jump before close, and one week's event (JUL26) was pushed back a week. The upload has been getting earlier week by week.

4) SETTLED VALUES vs WHAT THE DATA SAYS TODAY. Every week from AUG23 on matches exactly. Hormuz weekly for weeks ending JUL19 to AUG16 settled at 85, 17, 27, 31, 25, but the data now says 44, 25, 37, 39, 31. Bab el-Mandeb AUG02 went 208 to 215, Suez 285 to 291. So early numbers do get revised, by as much as +10 and once by -41. Kalshi paid out on the first-published number; every one of those revisions appeared after settlement.

5) HOW MUCH CHEAP SUPPLY WAS LEFT AFTER THE FIRST SNIPER. This counts buys on the side that won, at 95c or less, at least 10 s after the first jump, only on strikes 2 or more transits from the final count, after fees. When the budget runs out, the best-paying buys are taken first (chosen with hindsight). Result per Tuesday, oldest to newest, at a $900 budget: $6, $122, $81, $321, $0, $0, $1,152, $1,590. Total $3,272 over 56 days. At $400: $2,179. At $5k: $4,891. With no budget limit: $5,484. The two newest Tuesdays make up 84% of the $900 total. SEP13 used today's data because Kalshi recorded "Above X" instead of a count; without it the $900 total is $2,120.

6) WHAT THE LATE SUPPLY LOOKED LIKE. 09-22: Panama T200 NO sold at 36-42c at +65 s and +226 s; the count was 183, 17 below the strike. Suez T290/T280 YES sold at 28c and 47c at +65 s; the count was 293. 09-15: Suez T270 NO sold at 10-11c ten minutes after the jump; the count was 265. Bab el-Mandeb T175 YES was still trading at 69-73c 5-9 minutes after the jump; the count was 191. A faster sniper is already active: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb were swept 9-10 s BEFORE the 09-22 edit stamp, and there were 1-contract test buys on Suez at -7 s on 09-15.

7) TODAY'S BOOKS FOR THE 09-29 CLOSE (45 reads). Contested strikes show 200-2,000 contracts per side at mid-range prices, for example Panama T200 NO at 77-79c (about 1,080) and Suez T280 NO at 34c (1,462). That is roughly $300-1,000 per strike, so a $900 bank is limited by its own cash in a good week, not by supply.

8) THE DATA SITE'S CACHE. It holds answers for 30 s, but adding a random tag to each request gets fresh data. PortWatch's usage meter showed 1,500-1,850 of its 6,000-per-minute limit on a Friday, so heavy polling could get throttled.

chk.worst_case: We read a count that Kalshi does not settle on. Causes: a half-finished upload we took as complete; a revision loaded between the release and Kalshi's reading at about 14:00Z; or Kalshi deciding the data is "not complete" and waiting a week while it gets revised. Revisions of +6 to +10, and one of -41, did happen on Hormuz in July-August. All 6 series come from one upload, so one bad read hits every position at once. Worst plausible loss: the whole Tuesday stake, about $400-900 at the $900 bank (a 36c buy loses 36c a contract, a 90c buy loses 90c), and $2-5k at the $5k bank. The "2 or more away from the strike" filter protects against small revisions only. How often this happens is NOT measured: 0 mismatches in the 5 numerically settled weeks since AUG23, and it is unknown whether the July-August revisions came before or after the first trades. The milder bad case is PortWatch loading at its official 9 AM ET, which is Kalshi's close: $0 for that week (2 of 8 Tuesdays so far).
chk.killer_risks: (1) PortWatch's official release time, Tuesday 9 AM ET, is exactly Kalshi's close. The whole edge depends on them uploading early, which they happened to do on 6 of 8 Tuesdays. Kalshi could also move the close earlier. (2) Competition: a bot already acts 10 s before the edit stamp on Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. The Panama/Suez delay was 65 s on 09-22 and about 10 min on 09-15. Anyone can see that profit on the tape and add those two series next week. (3) The sellers who got picked off (about $3k lost on 09-22, much of it on resting quotes paid for by Kalshi's liquidity-rewards program) may pull their quotes before Tuesday mornings. (4) Kalshi settles by hand and has the "once complete data is available" escape clause, and PortWatch labels the data preliminary and has revised it by up to 41 transits. (5) Thin history: 8 Tuesdays, with 84% of the ceiling from the last 2. The trade history only shows what others took, not what we would get. (6) All six series settle off one upload each week, so it is effectively one bet per week, not six. (7) Heavy polling may be throttled (PortWatch was at 1,500-1,850 of its 6,000-per-minute limit on a quiet Friday).

ref.strongest_objection:
The checker's best-case profit assumes every cheap winning-side offer traded 10 s or more after the first price jump could have been ours. That assumption fails for 09-15, the second-biggest week ($1,152 of its $3,272). On that day the Suez number evidently was not final at the first upload.
- At the first jump (-6 s), the same bot that swept Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb bought only three 1-contract probes on Suez T280 NO at 10c, plus 16 and 5 contracts on T290 and T300.
- It did not touch T270 NO at 10-11c, which would have been a sure 90c profit per contract if Suez had read 265 then. With 6 of 7 days in (244), T270 would still have been a coin flip, which fits what it did.
- Nothing traded on Suez for 594 s. Then the same bot probed T270 with 1-lots at +594 s and swept 755 contracts at 10-11c at +598 s, about 4 s later.
- So a 10-s bot that waits for all 7 rows would have lost that race. That week's best case at $900 is about $500, not $1,152.
- It also means the published data changed or completed after it first became visible in 1 of 6 weeks that published before the close. That is exactly how the worst case happens: acting on a partial or provisional number, and every chokepoint bet that week rides on the same upload.

Two structural facts make this a recurring risk, not a one-off:
- The PortWatch table is wiped and reloaded in full every week. ObjectIds run 1..78,960 with no gaps, count 78,960, and the schema, data and last-edit stamps are identical (2026-09-22 12:15:34.689Z). So reading a half-loaded table is possible.
- PortWatch's own stated schedule is Tuesday 9 AM ET, which is Kalshi's close. 3 of 10 weekly events had no trading before the close at all (AUG02, AUG30, SEP06). AUG30 and SEP06 were only settled on Wednesday.

A competitor bot already covers all four chokepoints. On 09-22 it swept Suez T270/T280/T290 and Panama T200 inside 50 ms at +65 s. On 09-15 it reacted about 4 s after Suez locked. If its 65-s delay on Panama and Suez shrinks, most of the 09-22 lump goes with it.

None of this kills the idea. The edge is positive even in the pessimistic case, and Kalshi's liquidity-reward programs pay about $100 per market per day right up to the 13:00Z close. That keeps stale maker quotes resting through the release, which argues for supply lasting.

idea.name: Poly pin: the 1-cent tick gift on Polymarket US BTC 15-min and 1-hour windows
idea.family: cross-venue / crypto pin on a second book (same BRTI 60-s settlement)
idea.mechanism: Run pinrun's own feed and fair-value maths against Polymarket US's BTC books. 15-min: in the last 45 s, when the model gives the winner >= 99.5% and Poly's best ask for that side is <= 98c on 2+ consecutive seconds, buy it with an immediate-or-cancel limit at that ask, hold to settlement (Poly settles within ~1 minute, capital returns every window). 1-hour: same rule on the 1-hour window, whose strike is the hour-open 60-s average -- different from the Kalshi xx:45 15-min strike on the same top-of-hour print, so it gives ~24 extra pin chances a day. Use a settlement-margin guard (launch window mismatch). Pairs naturally with I45 (the corridor makes some of these hits riskless).
idea.why_mispriced: Poly prices in whole cents 1-99c while Kalshi's BTC book moves in 0.1c at the extremes, so when Kalshi's winner is 99.2-99.7c Poly's winner sits at 98c. Sellers are Poly retail: holders dumping the winner at 98c and lottery bids of 2-4c on the loser (at 04:29Z Poly takers sold the winner at 98c while Kalshi's bid was 99.3-99.6c; at 05:14Z Poly takers paid 3-4c for the loser Kalshi sold at 0.5c). The 1-hour book is thin and stale at the end: loser bids of 10-30c resting since earlier in the hour, 1-600-share quotes with 30-80c spreads.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Model calibrated at 1-7 bps margins in the last 45 s: 0 losses in 44 hits only rules out loss rates above ~6.6%, and break-even at 97-98c is ~2-3%. (2) Displayed asks executable: the public history differs from the real-time book on 22-39% of seconds; one 0.42 'ask' (1h) was an artefact (real-time 0.99). (3) Size >= our order: real-time 1h sizes at hits were only 8-560 shares. (4) Poly settles like Kalshi: 222 of 223 windows (exception: launch window 2026-09-22 15:15Z, settle - strike +$0.29: Kalshi YES, Poly Down). (5) A Poly US order path exists (current key is read-only) and his account can trade via API. Artefact if the history's cheap asks were display prices, not resting offers.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: 15-min: model-expected $22/day at 60 contracts a hit (current Poly bank ~$60), before unforeseen losses; one loss at 60 contracts = -$58 (~2.6 days of edge). Realistic $5-20/day at $60; $40-70/day at 200 contracts if the Poly bank were ~$200 and sizes hold. 1-hour: $3-12/day at 60 contracts (model-expected $12.6/day assumes sizes the recording rarely showed). Shares Poly capital with I11, I14, I43, I45.
idea.data_needed: (1) The 3-day recorder (scan_poly_ws.py, ends ~09-28) incl. 1h sizes -- note the recorder has a resubscribe bug that misses the xx:30/xx:45 15m windows. (2) Index-only calibration of the model at 1-7 bps in the last 45 s over the whole BRTI tape (pincalib style). (3) Join the live bot's BTC entries to Poly's real-time book. (4) 1-contract live test with per-order sign-off, ~30 hits (~3 days).
idea.evidence_so_far: Public per-second history (gateway /v1/price-history, fidelity=1), 181 15-min windows since launch: with 2+ consecutive seconds inside 45 s, model >= 99.5% and ask 0.85-0.98, 32 windows hit (18%, ~12/day); asks 0.91-0.98 (13 at 0.98); margin p10/median/p90 1.3/4.1/25.3 bps; model's winner lost 0; average expected edge 3.07c/contract; Poly cheaper than Kalshi's ticker in 52 of 59 comparable hits. Real-time recording (8 windows): 3 hits (tau 30/38/52 s, sizes 1,566/2,014/96 shares), all won, while Kalshi's winner cost 98.2-99.7c. 1-hour history: 42 windows, 12 hits (29%, 4.5/day) at 0.90-0.98, avg expected edge 4.65c, 0 losses; real-time: 05:00Z Down offered 0.89-0.90 (8-153 shares) for 40 s at model 0.99-1.00 (margin -1.7 bps), 06:00Z 0.96-0.98 (69-560 shares) (margin -0.6 bps), both won. The pre-registered U1 bar FAILS as written (0 seconds at >= 10 bps margin; on the rebuilt book 2 of 3 Kalshi moves >= 5c took Poly > 3 s to follow): supply lives at 1-7 bps, which the bar excluded. chk.measured:
The idea as written is roughly break-even. Its main leg buys the BTC 15-min winner at 98c with 21-45 s left, and in that same band our own Kalshi fills lose about as often as a 98c price can afford. A different slice of the same books does look good, but the sample is small: stale cheap offers on the winner of the 1-hour window, and in the last 3-10 s.

1) Our own Kalshi fills (source rank 3; `power/calib/livefills.json`, 908 fills, 09-08 to 09-24, same kind of order: take the favourite with immediate-or-cancel). Loss rate by seconds left, counted per market:
- 3-10 s: 0 of 91
- 11-20 s: 3 of 148 (2.0%)
- 21-30 s: 11 of 345 (3.2%)
- 31-45 s: 5 of 278 (1.8%)
- With margin under 3 bps and 20 s or more left: 11 of 302 (3.6%); BTC only 3 of 81.
- Break-even loss rate on Poly: 1.86% at 98c, 2.80% at 97c, 3.73% at 96c, 4.67% at 95c, 9.4% at 90c.
- So the 98c leg nets somewhere between +0.9c and -1.3c per contract. The model's "3.07c average edge" assumes the model's own probability, which is 8-20x too sure at these margins (point 2).
- Script and output: `check-I10/livezm.py`, `livezm.out`.

2) Index-only loss rate, no order book (`check-I10/densecal.py`, `densecal.out`, self-test PASS). BTC settlement index, every 1-minute close 09-01 to 09-25 (1.96M prints), strikes placed at 0.5-3 bps, model at 99.5% or more:
- Favourite loses 1.0% at 1 bps, 0.66% at 1.5 bps, 0.50% at 2 bps (all 20-45 s cells pooled). At 1-1.5 bps with 40-45 s left: 1.3-2.5%. The model says about 0.1%.
- Cross-check on real strikes (MODEL_CALIBRATION rows): BTC at 1-2 bps, 20 s or more left, lost 4 of 259 cells (1.5%). Output: `xcheck_rows.out`.
- The hits sit at 0.55-1.8 bps, so the realistic loss rate there is about 1% before adverse selection and 1.8-3.6% on our own fills.

3) Real-time Poly book (`check-I10/rt_hits.py`, `rt_hits.out`, `rt_hits.json`; recorder 03:11 to 10:16Z 09-25; pinrun's own fair() through a stub on the index tape):
- 15-min: 3 of 16 recorded windows had the winner at 98c or less on 2+ seconds with the model at 99.5% or more. All were 98c, sizes 1,566 / 1,894 / 4.5, all won.
- 1-hour: 3 of 7 windows hit, at 0.90, 0.90 and 0.97. Size at the best price 5-562 shares; depth at 98c or less 566-1,052.
- In the 04:00Z and 05:00Z 1-hour windows (margins 1.7 and 0.55 bps), the winner stayed on offer at 0.95-0.97 until 1-5 s before close: 87-614 shares, model 1.0. These are stale bids on the loser at 3-4c.
- Trades print up to 0.0-0.3 s before close, so the book is still tradeable. Other takers also hit those 4c bids (the 1-hour 0400 and 0500 windows had BUY_SHORT prints at 0.04 with 4-10 s left). Output: `late_trades.out`.
- The recorder captured only 16 of 29 15-min windows (resubscribe bug).

4) Forward paper bot (`research/polypaper.py --report`, 11 windows 08:00-10:30Z 09-25): 0 buys. The winner had no offer in 40-45 of the 45 seconds in every window; all 11 were decided by more than 5 bps.

5) Public touch history, prices only, no sizes (`check-I10/late_hist.py`, `late_hist.out`; 182 15-min and 42 1-hour windows, 2.65 days; this history disagrees with the real-time book on 22-39% of seconds):
- Winner at 97c or less on 2+ seconds with 3-10 s left: 15-min 4 of 182, 1-hour 5 of 42 (median 0.94).
- With 21-45 s left: 15-min 13 of 182, 1-hour 5 of 42.
- The model's winner lost 0 in every band.

6) Poly's settlement matched the index on 222 of 223 windows. The one miss was the launch window, settled 0.34 bps from the strike. Polymarket US docs: POST /v1/orders supports immediate-or-cancel and fill-or-kill for identity-verified individuals, with keys from polymarket.us/developer (the current key is read-only). Taker fee is 0.0695*p*(1-p), rounded per fill to the nearest cent.

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
These numbers use a narrower rule than the idea: the 1-hour window, plus late seconds on the 15-min. Buy the winner at 97c or less with 3-10 s left, or at 95c or less with 11-45 s left. Skip if the projected margin is under 0.5 bps. Drop the 15-min 98c buys with 21-45 s left, which are +0.9c to -1.3c per contract (point 1).

Inputs:
- Qualifying 1-hour windows: 3/day (history) to 10/day (real-time, 3 of 7). Use 3-6/day.
- Net edge about 3c per contract after the fee (0.2-0.6c) and a loss allowance.
- Fill rate about 0.6. Our Kalshi takes fill 70%, and other takers are visibly hitting the same bids.

Arithmetic:
- Current $60 Poly bank, 60 contracts a hit: 3-6 × 0.6 × 60 × $0.03 = $3-6.5/day.
- $900 on Poly, about 150 contracts (the real-time depth allows it in the hits seen): 3-6 × 0.6 × 150 × 0.03 = $8-16/day.
- $5k: the book caps size, not the bank. About 250 contracts: 3-6 × 0.6 × 250 × 0.03 = $13-27/day.

The size figure comes from 3 real-time windows. The frequency figure comes from 7 real-time and 42 history windows.

The idea's own 15-min 98c leg at 60 contracts and about 15 hits/day: between +$8 and -$12/day. The sign is not established.
chk.worst_case:
One losing hit costs size × about 96c:
- -$58 at 60 contracts (the whole $60 Poly bank)
- -$145 at 150
- -$240 at 250

A 15-min window and the 1-hour window that close on the same second settle on the same print. If both are held on the same side, one bad print can double the loss.

The realistic source of a loss in the last 10 s is not the index: 0 of about 38,000 index cells lost at 5-10 s, and 0 of 91 of our late Kalshi fills. It is Poly settling differently from the index. That happened once in 223 windows, on the launch window at 0.34 bps. A Poly settlement delay or dispute would lock the capital instead.
chk.killer_risks:
1. The idea's main leg (15-min, 98c, 21-45 s left) is break-even or worse. Break-even is a 1.86% loss rate, and our own fills in that band lose 1.8-3.2%. The model's 99.5-99.97% is 8-20x too sure at 1-2 bps margins.
2. The part that looks good rests on 7 real-time 1-hour windows (3 with supply) and on history touch prices that have no sizes and disagree with the real book on 22-39% of seconds.
3. Competition: other takers hit the same stale 3-4c loser bids in the last 10 s. Our home-laptop speed on Poly is unmeasured.
4. Supply shows up only in close windows, those under about 2 bps. 11 straight decided windows (08:00-10:30Z) had nothing, so supply may be bursty and weekday-dependent.
5. Needs a Poly trading key (the current one is read-only), per-order sign-off, and the operator's OK for a new strategy family.
6. Settlement mismatch at tiny margins (1 in 223, launch window). Needs a margin guard of at least 0.5 bps.
7. The Poly bank is $60, and every other Poly idea draws on it (I11, I14, I43, I45).
8. The recorder misses about 45% of 15-min windows (resubscribe bug), so 15-min real-time evidence is thin.
chk.next_test:
Cheapest decisive test: re-run the real-time check when the existing recorder ends (~09-28 06:11Z, about 72 1-hour windows). Command: `python check-I10/rt_hits.py` in the scratch folder. Extend it first to walk book depth for 60 and 200 contracts and to apply the rule above.

Pass bar, written before reading: all four must hold.
- At least 18 of about 72 1-hour windows (1 in 4) with the winner fillable at the cap for 60 shares or more.
- Median fillable size of 60 shares or more.
- 0 index-side losses.
- Average edge after fee of at least 2.5c per contract.

Fail if fewer than 9 windows qualify, or if any loss happens with 3-10 s left.

In parallel:
- Fix the recorder's resubscribe bug so 15-min windows stop being skipped.
- Point `polypaper.py` at the 1-hour slug and at 1-10 s left, as a second forward check.

If that passes: a live test at 5 contracts a hit on a Poly trading key, per-order sign-off, about 30 hits. Pass: fill rate at least 50% and at most 1 loss.
chk.capital_needed: $60 already on Poly caps size at about 60 contracts a hit. About $900 lets it take roughly 150 contracts a hit; above about $1-1.5k the Poly book, not the bank, sets the size (measured depth at 98c or less was 566-1,052 shares in the 3 real-time 1-hour hits). Capital returns every window, around a minute after close; exact payout timing is not in Poly's docs.

ref.strongest_objection:
I could not show the narrowed 1-hour rule loses money. What I could show is that it is small, and that the checker's next test will probably read FAIL even if the edge is real.

1) How often it happens. The cheap winner on Poly shows up only when BTC finishes the hour within about 2 bps of where it started. The real-time sample caught 3 such hours out of 7. Over 22 days of the index tape the rate is 45 of 530 hours (8.5%), about 2 a day, and anywhere from 0 to 5 on a given day. So the real-time sample ran about 5 times hotter than normal. The checker assumed 3-6 hits a day; the rate is about 2, or about 3 if supply at 2-3 bps counts.

2) The pre-registered pass bar is set 3 times too high. It asks for 18 or more of about 72 hours. At the 22-day rate, 72 hours should produce about 6 qualifying hours, or about 9.5 if the cut-off is 3 bps. That gives a 40-85% chance of landing under the bar's own fail line of 9, and less than a 2% chance of reaching 18, even if every hit pays. The bar needs rewriting before anyone reads the data: judge the result per qualifying hour (size, fill, loss), and take the frequency from the index.

3) Proving it is safe will be slow. One loss at 60 contracts costs about $57, which is 2-3 weeks of expected profit. At about 1 fill a day, it takes months to tell a 1% loss rate from a 4% one.

4) The 15-minute leg adds nothing under the narrowed rule. None of the 16 real-time 15-minute windows qualified. The idea's own 98c 15-minute leg was already break-even (checker).

5) Competition is real. Other takers bought the same cheap winner in every qualifying hour: 261, 1,578 and 4,377 shares. The seller ladders refilled each time, so there was still supply, but our own fill rate on Poly is not measured.
ref.independent_checks:
A) Frequency from the index only (sweep/refute-I10/baserate.py, baserate.out, baserate.json; self-test PASS, my fast model matches pinrun.fair to 5.9e-17 on 60 real cells).

- The flag sorts all 23 real-time windows correctly. All 6 real-time hits are flagged (1-hour 0300/0400/0500Z, 15-minute 0500/0515/0645Z). None of the 16 non-hits is.

B) Size on the real-time book under the checker's narrowed rule (rtsize.py, rtsize.out). Rule: 97c or less with 3-10 s left, 95c or less with 11-45 s left, margin guard 0.5 bps. Book read only up to the second in question; the checker's script looked 1 s ahead.
- 3 of 7 1-hour windows qualify, at 37, 24 and 7 s left, asks 0.90, 0.90 and 0.96.
- Shares fillable at the cap: 248, 80 (up to 851 in later seconds) and 472. All three won.

C) Book sizes are shares, not dollars. Bid ladders multiply out to exactly $10 a rung (34.48 at 0.29, 40.00 at 0.25).

D) The launch-window settlement miss was $0.29 on $86,291, which is 0.034 bps, not the checker's 0.34 bps. A 0.5 bps guard is about 15 times that miss, which helps the idea.

E) The history's 4 large-margin 1-hour hits (6.8-73 bps; histpeek.out) are sparse, noisy touch prices, for example Down at 0.81 with 3 s left at 10 bps on 09-24 2200Z. They have no sizes and were never seen in real time (0 of 4 large-margin hours had any). Possible upside, unverified.

F) Poly US docs:

idea.name: Two books, one print: riskless Kalshi-Polymarket package at the extremes
idea.family: cross-venue arbitrage (same BRTI 60-s average, same strike to the cent)
idea.mechanism: When Poly bid(Up) > Kalshi ask(Up) + both taker fees: sell Up on Poly (buy Down) and buy Up on Kalshi. When Kalshi bid(Up) > Poly ask(Up) + both fees: buy Up on Poly and buy Down on Kalshi. One leg pays $1 whatever happens. Only take it when the index margin to strike is >= $5, so a settlement mismatch like the launch window cannot hurt. Prefer taking the thinner Poly leg first.
idea.why_mispriced: The same whole-cent tick: Poly lottery buyers pay 1-4c for the loser that Kalshi's deep book sells at 0.4-1.5c, and Poly sellers dump the winner 1-2c under Kalshi's bid.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Both legs fill within ~1 s (legging is the main risk). (2) Nobody faster takes the quotes: they sat 2-45 s at night, but other Poly trades hit the same price during 30 of 47 episodes. (3) Settlement identical (222/223 windows; strike equality 16/16 windows checked to the cent). (4) The 8-window night sample (03:15-06:30Z) is typical. (5) A Poly US API order path for his account. Artefact checks done: the Kalshi book rebuild matches Kalshi's ticker and trade prints in checked episodes (ep_check.py); Poly trades at those prices confirm the levels were live. The earlier cached-gateway 'arbs' were a 30-s cache artefact; this uses the real-time WebSocket.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Capital-capped with quotes persisting >= 2 s: $0.41/window at 60 contracts, $3.30 at 500, $10.97 at 2,000. Ceiling ~$39/day at the current ~$60 Poly bank (96 windows, perfect execution, no competition). Realistic $5-15/day at $60; toward ~$50-100/day with a larger Poly deposit before competition.
idea.data_needed: Several days of the real-time recording across US daytime hours (fix the recorder's resubscribe bug first), then a 1-contract two-leg test with per-order sign-off to measure leg-fill rate and slippage.
idea.evidence_so_far: 8 recorded windows against the Kalshi book rebuilt from orderbook_delta: 558 seconds with edge > 0 after both fees = 130 episodes, 47 lasting >= 3 s: 38 at extreme prices (<= 5c or >= 95c; $43.52 at first-second size, $156 at best second) and 9 mid-price ($2.86; mostly 1-2 s timing effects). Largest confirmed: 05:15Z close, 29-37 s before close, 1,566-2,285 shares, edge 1.0-1.2c. Files: sweep/cross-venue/xv_sim.out, xv_sim2.out, xv_episodes.json, ep_check.py; sweep/anything-anywhere/ptb_check.py.

idea.prior_reason: Riskless by construction once both legs fill, and the episodes are confirmed by real Poly trades at those prices; but dollars are small at a $60 Poly bank, the sample is 8 night windows, competition hits the same quotes, and the Poly order path is not built.

WHAT DECIDES IT: at the extremes the gap is real and survives realistic delays, but everything comes from 16 overnight windows on one night (23:15-05:30 ET, 09-25), on a venue that opened on 09-22. There are no live fills yet.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED (read-only; everything is in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/check-I11/):

- Execution model (xv_xtr3.py, the final version): a 0.1 s grid; fire when the package edge after both taker fees is at least 0.3c and the projected index average is at least $5 from the Kalshi floor_strike. Leg 1 is a Poly IOC that fills only from size still resting when it arrives (+0.1 to 0.5 s). Leg 2 is a Kalshi IOC after the Poly fill is known, at whatever Kalshi then offers (+0.1 to 0.5 s more; any remainder priced 2c worse). Kalshi fees are rounded up to the cent per order; Poly fees are also rounded up (conservative, since Poly uses banker's rounding). Capital is capped on both venues. Size we already took is subtracted from the book for the rest of the window: the first version re-took the same resting 143 shares 13 times, and that bug is fixed.

RESULTS, extremes only (Poly leg >= 95c or <= 5c), sequential, EMIN 0.3c:
- Poly $60 / Kalshi $300 cap (the $900 bank): out-of-sample $1.59-1.66 per 8 windows = $0.20-0.21 per window, at every delay from 0.1 to 0.5 s. In-sample $0.29-0.33 per window. 7 of 8 OOS windows had a fill. Worst single package -$0.01.

- Poly $2000 / Kalshi $2000 (the $5k bank): OOS $44-48 over 8 windows = $5.5-6.0 per window at delays up to 0.25 s (about 1,550 contracts per window at about 0.38c each); only $1.0 per window at 0.5 s (worst package -$25.46). In-sample $6.7-8.3 per window.
- Edge per contract is 0.3-0.8c. The mechanism is the tick: Poly's winner sits at 99c because its tick is 1c, while Kalshi's winner bid sits at 99.5c because its tick is 0.1c there. Kalshi's cheap loser leg did not move during the delay (0.005 -> 0.005 on most fills).

WITHOUT THE EXTREMES FILTER (xv_exec.out): mid-price 'arbs' are timing artefacts. With a 0.5 s delay they lose -$2 to -$22 per window, because Kalshi moves 4-9c before the hedge lands. ref.strongest_objection:
The price gap is real, so I could not kill the idea on the data. What stands against it is that the money is small and easy to lose, and running it on the live bot's Kalshi account would break the live bot.

(1) SIZE. At the $900 bank the Polymarket side is capped at about 60 contracts a window. That is about 0.3c a contract, or at most $0.20 a window. On the first fresh US-morning data (8:00-9:00 AM ET today), my own model with full book depth made $0.075 a window with a 0.25+0.25 s order loop and $0.21 with a 0.5+0.5 s loop. The five packages were +$0.04, -$0.01, +$0.23, +$0.19 and -$0.15. Morning gaps happen 55-104 s before the close, when BTC is only $27-92 from the strike. There Kalshi's price moves 0.5-1c inside a second and eats a 0.3c edge.

(2) THE GAP COMES AND GOES BY THE HOUR. Share of time with a 0.3c+ edge, counting only time when the Polymarket price was at an extreme:
- 11:15 PM-2:30 AM ET: 13-45%
- 2:45-3:45 AM ET: 7-13%
- 4:00-5:30 AM ET: 0.1-2.6%, even with 710 s at extreme prices
- 8:00-9:00 AM ET: back to 34-58%
So multiplying one night by 96 windows is not a valid way to get a daily figure.

(3) ONLY 88 WINDOWS A DAY, NOT 96. Polymarket US lists no BTC 15-minute markets from 6:00 to 8:00 AM ET: I found 404s for every window on 09-24 and 09-25. That gap is also why the recorder went quiet after 5:30 AM ET, not only its resubscribe bug.

(4) IT CLASHES WITH THE LIVE BOT. Kalshi merges a market's Yes and No into one position, and pinrun's startup check adopts and hedges any position in its series that its own books do not hold (research/pinrun.py lines 3000-3006 and 16045-16163). So a leg bought on Kalshi for this idea (for example 60 No at 3c) would be taken over and hedged by the live money bot on its next restart. That leg settles as a loss, which can trip pinrun's stop rail. The fix is a Kalshi subaccount: they exist but can only be used through the API. It has to be in place before any live test.

(5) OTHER BOTS TAKE THE SAME CHEAP OFFERS. At 4:00 AM ET about 1,400 contracts at 99c were taken in one order 1.1 s after the gap opened. In the 4:00-5:30 AM ET windows other traders took or traded 1.0-1.2x the shown size on the two gaps that lasted over 1 s. The simulation assumes nobody gets there before us.

(6) THE $5k CASE IS OVERSTATED. My own simulation gives $2.1-3.0 a window at a 0.25 s loop and $0.56 at 0.5 s, with packages as bad as -$18. The checker's $5.5-6.0 a window does not hold up.

idea.name: CPI two-complex consistency (MoM vs YoY on the same release)
idea.family: economics / CPI release markets, cross-series arithmetic
idea.mechanism: Once MoM is out, YoY is fixed by arithmetic: YoY = NSA(last month) x r x (1+MoM) / NSA(same month last year); both NSA levels are already public (BLS API) and r is the month's seasonal-factor ratio. So 'YoY above 3.6' and 'MoM above 0.5' are nearly the same event. When the complexes disagree, buy YES on the cheap one and NO on the rich one; if the two cutoffs match exactly the pair pays $1 in every outcome. Enter only in the last days before the release, only on pairs whose cutoffs are within ~0.005 pp (gap computed from BLS item-level seasonal factors, cross-checked against the Cleveland Fed nowcast's own MoM/YoY pair), and only when the pair costs < $1 minus fees minus the gap risk. Extends to core CPI MoM vs YoY.
idea.why_mispriced: Different people trade the two complexes: YoY traders anchor on the YoY headline and nowcast, MoM traders on the SA headline; nobody on the book runs the seasonal-factor arithmetic. The losers are whichever side's takers pay 10-20c more than the linked market for the same outcome.
idea.must_be_true: (1) r can be pinned to ~0.0002 before the release from published item factors and relative importances (history-based r is NOT good enough: Sep r ranged 0.9979-1.0007 over 2014-2025). (2) BLS rounding works as assumed (percent changes from 3-decimal indexes, then rounded to 1 decimal). (3) Gaps recur. Artefact risk: the Aug gap is measured from last trades in 6-hour buckets, not simultaneous asks.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $2-10/day averaged ($50-300 per monthly release at our size). August hindsight: ~9-22c per pair on thousands of contracts. September live: ~3-7c EV per pair after gap risk. Monthly and lumpy.
idea.data_needed: (a) Compute September r from BLS's published 2026 seasonal factors and relative importances, or reproduce it from the Cleveland nowcast's MoM/YoY pair on 3-4 past months and check vs actual prints. (b) Snapshot both books every 10 min for the 3 days before the Oct 14 release. (c) Repeat the Aug check with book asks for Jul/Aug/Sep. ~1 day of work, zero risk.
idea.evidence_so_far: BLS API: NSA Aug-26 334.980, Sep-25 324.800, SA Aug-26 334.131. Aug 2026: with actual r=0.99922 the pairs YoY>3.3/MoM>0.3 and YoY>3.4/MoM>0.4 had cutoffs 0.3512 vs 0.35 and 0.4483 vs 0.45 (effectively the same event); for 3 days YoY traded 5-24c above MoM (last 6 h: 0.70 vs 0.46 and 0.26 vs 0.15); both pairs resolved the same way. Live Sep books (06:xxZ 09-25): MoM>0.5 ask 0.64, YoY>3.6 ask 0.45; YoY-YES + MoM-NO costs $0.82 with 709 contracts at the touch; the 0.4/3.5 pair $0.95 (3,488 deep). YoY complex implies r ~0.9990-0.9993; recent years 0.99947/0.99959; a Cleveland nowcast read by WebFetch (0.50% MoM / 3.57% YoY, unverified -- the same fetch mis-stated Aug actuals) implies r ~0.99921, at which the Sep 0.5/3.6 pair has a 0.03 pp gap where both legs lose (~12% chance). Scripts: sweep/econ-fin-commodities/cpi_arb.py, pair_hist.py.
merged_from: econ-fin-commodities: CPI two-complex consistency (MoM vs YoY)
idea.novelty_vs_killed: Earlier econ kills were 'release markets close before the number'. This trades the arithmetic link between two markets on the same number.
idea.prior_reason: The link is exact arithmetic and live books show a 18c-cheap pair with real depth; but the outcome depends on pinning r, which is not yet done, the August evidence is last-trade not book, and it is one release a month.
idea.worst_case: r misjudged so MoM lands in the gap between cutoffs: both legs lose, $0.82 per pair, ~-$410 at 500 pairs on one release.

chk.measured:
The link between the two markets holds, and the price gap is real on today's book and was there in 4 of the last 7 releases. The money is small, and one bad month can wipe out a whole position.

1) Pinning the September seasonal-factor ratio r (the step that decides it). I used BLS's own files: the 2026 seasonal factor workbook (cpi-seasonal-factors.xlsx), the December-2025 relative importance table and the flat-file component indexes (cu.data.*). From these I rebuilt the all-items seasonally adjusted index from its 81 components, using BLS's published aggregation list.
- Check that the build is right: given each component's actual monthly move, the model reproduces the published all-items r for Feb to Aug 2026 to within 0.000002. The workbook's factors match the published NSA/SA index ratios to within 0.003 factor points.
- Forecast before the release, with no component moves known: error over Feb to Aug 2026 has sd 0.000124 and max 0.000191.
- Same forecast with only the motor-fuel move known: sd 0.000020, max 0.000054. That is 0.005 percentage points of monthly (MoM) inflation.
- EIA weekly gasoline tracks the CPI motor-fuel move to within 1.0 percentage point every month in 2026.
- September: EIA gasoline is up 6.2% (3 of 4 weeks in), which gives r = 0.99936 ± about 0.00005.
- The prices on the yearly (YoY) side imply r of about 0.9990. That would be 9 standard deviations of model error away.
- The Cleveland nowcast pair implies 0.9992. Earlier Septembers were 0.99947 and 0.99959.

2) Settlement rules. 232 of 232 settled KXCPI/KXCPIYOY markets from Feb to Aug 2026 match the value computed as round(percent change of the 3-decimal indexes, 1). There were zero mismatches. None of these months printed close to a rounding boundary, so this does not test the half-way case.

3) September at r = 0.99936: 'YoY above 3.6' is the same event as 'MoM at or above 0.5645', while 'MoM above 0.5' means 'MoM at or above 0.55'.
- If MoM lands between 0.55 and 0.5645, both legs lose. At the MoM ladder's density (about 4 per percentage point), that happens about 6 times in 100.
- Book at 06:58 AM ET and again at 07:09 AM ET: MoM>0.5 NO costs 0.37 with 692 available (then thin at 0.40-0.42). YoY>3.6 YES costs 0.42 with 1,133 available, then 0.43 with 2,908.
- Pair cost is 0.79, or 0.823 with taker fees (0.07p(1-p) per leg). Expected value is +0.118 per pair.
- Walking both books: 1,158 pairs can be filled at an expected value of at least 2 cents each, using $958 of capital, for about $94 expected.
- The 0.6/3.7 pair is worth about $5. The 0.4/3.5 pair has no edge.
- Core CPI: the same model works (sd 0.000028, max 0.000068), but the September core cutoffs are about 0.025 points out of line and priced consistently (0.99-1.07 all-in). No core trade this month.
- Same-number siblings: the KXECONSTATCPI and KXECONSTATCPIYOY exact buckets agree with the threshold ladders to within 2 cents before fees, so no trade there.
- KXCPINDEX (a market-maker ladder, 100 lots per level) is off by 9-27 cents. 'YoY>3.6 YES + INDEX>336.60 NO' costs 0.76 all-in, needs no r, and has a both-lose band worth about 6.5 in 100. Only 100 contracts are there.

4) Past releases, from hourly book candles (yes_bid/yes_ask via /series/.../candlesticks and /historical/markets/.../candlesticks, 128 GETs), not last trades.
- Ex-ante rule: r from the model plus EIA gasoline; both-lose band probability at a density of 4.5 per percentage point, error sd 0.006; enter when expected value is at least 5 cents.
- It fires in Mar, Jun, Jul and Aug; nothing in Feb, Apr or May, because the two strike grids were out of line.
- Entries cost 0.755-0.936 all-in. Every entered pair paid $1, for +$0.665 realised on $5.34 of capital (1 contract per pair).
- Tape check that the cheap asks were real:
  - Jul 12, 21 h before close: 4,057 YoY YES traded at ≤0.53 and 2,647 MoM NO at ≤0.20 in that hour.
  - Aug: the YoY NO leg was thin (0-1 contracts traded at the ask).
- Only 7 releases, and the both-lose band was hit 0 times when about 0.2 hits were expected. The downside is modelled, not measured.

Moving $250 into CPI pairs (the checker's $900-bank plan) cuts pinrun from 88 to about 66 contracts (-24%), which is roughly 17% fewer contracts. Pinrun's lifetime crypto rate on Kalshi's ledger is about $35/day since 09-08, which puts the cost near $6/day. The bot's last 6 full ET days were about -$11 in total, so the true cost could be near zero. Nobody knows the bot's forward rate. The pair beats the bot per dollar only when held under about 5 days (12% per hold vs roughly 2.4%/day forgone). In the checker's own replay of the last 72 hours of past releases, entries gave only +5 to +10 cents a pair, and the depth was unproven (August's leg was about 1 lot).

Second, operational: the bot has a 20% drawdown halt (from its high-water mark on disk). The edge itself survived my checks. My own r model agrees. idea.name: Same-number twin books: gas daily vs weekly/monthly (and other pairs settled by one published number)
idea.family: economics / cross-horizon same-number consistency
idea.mechanism: The weekly gas market for date D (e.g. KXAAAGASW-26SEP28) and the daily for the same date settle on the identical AAA national average and trade side by side for ~15 hours (the daily lists ~13:00Z the day before). When one book's bid for 'above K' exceeds the other book's ask for 'above K or lower' plus fees, buy the cheap YES and the rich NO: pays $1 in every outcome; hold overnight. Same for month-end monthly vs daily, NJ weekly vs NJ daily, the Nov 3 election-day market vs the Nov 3 daily. Maker variant: daily and weekly series charge makers nothing, so rest the cheap leg as a bid. Generalised as a daily watcher over every pair fixed by one release: KXU3MAX vs KXU3EOY and monthly KXU3 prints; KXU3-26DEC vs KXU3EOY once December lists; gas monthly-max vs weekly/monthly; core CPI MoM vs YoY; annual GDP vs Q4 advance (bounded risk only, earlier quarters get revised).
idea.why_mispriced: Different crowds: the weekly has week-long makers, the daily lists fresh with its own makers, and nobody arbitrages the two on the one day they overlap; long-dated ladders have 200-lot makers not linked to each other.
idea.must_be_true: Both books settle on the same number: checked, expiration values identical on 16 of 16 matched dates (10 national weekly, 2 monthly, 4 NJ weekly). Both prices executable at the same moment: evidence is hourly candle closes, not the book -- the weak point. Identical definitions for the other pairs (seasonally adjusted, same release, one decimal).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Gas: $1-4/day averaged, ~$5-20 per event for us; tape proxy ~$27 per event (best package each hour x contracts traded at or better than both prices, $298.68 over 11 dates). Other pairs $0-3/day; today's best near-miss 'any 2026 month above 5%' ask 5.5c vs 'December above 5.0%' bid 6c = +0.5c before fees, -0.25c after, 200 contracts.
idea.data_needed: Live read with depth of KXAAAGASW-26SEP28 vs KXAAAGASD-26SEP28 from ~Sep 27 13:00Z to Sep 28 03:59Z, and KXAAAGASM-26SEP30 vs the daily Sep 30 market (a handful of orderbook GETs an hour). Run the pair list daily; check KXU3-26DEC vs KXU3EOY once December lists.
idea.evidence_so_far: 11 overlapping dates (Jul 20-Sep 21), every date had positive packages after taker fees: 81 positive date-hours, best 1.6c to 13.4c. Example 07-26 16:00Z: daily above 4.115 bid 21c while weekly above 4.114 asked 6c = 13.4c after fees. No package broke nesting on settled results. Other pairs consistent (gas monthly-max vs weekly/monthly; CONTROLH vs seat ladders). Files: sweep/combine-consistency-arbitrage/gas_pairs.py/.out, gas_depth.py/.out, gas_same.py/.out, probe_pairs.py/.out.

idea.novelty_vs_killed: D03 killed gas as a directional pin (needs a private station feed). This needs no feed or forecast, only that two books settle on the same number.

chk.measured:
The gas price gaps are real, but at least one other bot is already taking them, usually within the same second. That rival, not the size of the gaps, is what limits how much we could make.

1) Minute-by-minute prices, not hourly. I pulled 1-minute price records for every gas date where the daily market and the weekly or monthly market settled on the same AAA number: 11 national dates (Jul 20 to Sep 21) and 4 New Jersey dates. These records are only written when the book changes, so carrying the last price forward is valid. Each date overlapped for about 16 hours (956 minutes). On national dates, a combined bet that pays $1 whatever happens was positive after taker fees on both legs in 198 to 904 of those 956 minutes. That came to 1,469 separate windows: 526 lasted 1 minute, 258 lasted 15 minutes or more. The biggest gaps (up to 67c) were the minute the daily market listed (12:00Z) and had no trades on either leg, so they cannot be counted as real. Files: check-I13/gas_min.py, gas_min.out, gas_min.json.

2) The quotes were real, not stale. I compared the quotes against actual trades inside the windows (verify_ep.out). Trades printed at the quoted bid and ask levels. The off-price trades were takers buying or selling through several price levels at once, or the price moving within the minute. Settlement never broke the logic: 0 of 1,469 windows had the higher-strike market pay YES while the lower-strike one paid NO. An earlier check found the settlement numbers identical on 16 of 16 dates.

3) How much other people actually traded at our prices. I counted contracts traded at prices at least as good as the combined bet, inside each window, using each market only once per date (per_date.out):
- National, 11 dates: median $19.48 per date, mean $29.96, range $0.53 to $90.94.
- New Jersey, 4 dates: median about $1. New Jersey is dead.
These figures include whatever the rival took, so they are what everyone got, not what we would get.

4) The rival. I took the 14 biggest traded windows and timed the two legs against each other (simul.out). For 13% of the cheap-leg contracts, the other leg traded within 10 seconds. For 68% it was within 60 seconds, and 95% within 30 minutes. Several were matched 75 to 100 contract pairs on both books in the same second: Sep 13 20:21:41Z, Sep 13 16:56:42Z, Sep 6 17:11:58Z, Sep 20 12:27:14Z, Aug 24 03:02:44Z. That is one bot trading this exact pair. Many other fills were one-sided bets against the new daily's bad opening quotes (for example 25c to 47c bids at 12:03Z on Jul 27, when the weekly market was pricing the same outcome at 1c).

5) Live books now (11:00Z Sep 25, live_pairs.out, depth_now.out). No same-date pair is open until Sep 27 12:00Z. I also priced 53 other pairs where one market logically implies another (single day vs month-high/month-low, the Election Day market vs the yearly high/low). One was positive: month-high above $4.60 at 5c plus Sep 30 NOT above $4.60 at 92c, for +2.15c after fees on 25 contracts ($0.54). The weekly book shows about 200 contracts at the best price on each side. The monthly shows 1 to 30.

6) The other pairs are dead:
- Unemployment: a Nov/Dec rate above 5.0% against 'any 2026 month above 5%' is at best +0.5c before fees and negative after. The money would be tied up until Jan 8 2027. Live Nov T5.0 has no bid.
- Core CPI month-on-month vs year-on-year are not the same number. One is seasonally adjusted and the other is not, so it is not an arbitrage.
- Annual GDP vs Q4 GDP is not the same number either (earlier quarters get revised).

GETs used: about 560.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
These numbers come from other people's trades, not our own fills, and our share against the rival bot is unmeasured.

- How often: about 5 national chances a month (weekly market every Monday date, plus month-end), which is about 0.17 a day. New Jersey adds nothing.
- Each chance: at most about $19.50 (median) to $30 (mean) went to everyone combined. Against a bot that already trades both legs in the same second, assume we get 25 to 50%. That is $5 to $15 per chance.
- $900 bank: $5 to $15 x 5 a month / 30 days = about $0.80 to $2.50 a day. The always-open single-day vs month-high/low pairs add roughly $0.50 a day at most (today: one positive pair worth $0.54).
- $5k bank: the same, about $1 to $3 a day. The limit is how many cheap contracts show up, not money. A bet costs under $1 a contract and is tied up about 12 to 20 hours to settlement, so 200 contracts is under $200 and fits even the $900 bank.
- Fees are already taken out: taker fee is 0.07 x p x (1-p) on each leg. The monthly market charges fees to makers too, so the resting-order version only works on the daily and weekly markets.
chk.worst_case:
The worst case is buying one leg and losing the race for the other. The rival bot is the likely winner of that race, so this is the realistic failure, not a rare one.

That leaves an unhedged gas bet until settlement. The leg was bought below what the other book was paying, so on average it is not a losing bet, but it can lose its full cost:
- At a 200-contract cap on a 92c to 96c leg: up to about $190 on one day.
- At a 50-contract cap: about $48.
Suggested size: 50 contracts until the watcher measures how often we lose the second leg.

If both legs fill, the loss is zero: in 1,469 windows the paired bet never failed to pay $1, and the settlement numbers matched on 16 of 16 dates.
chk.killer_risks:
1. A rival bot already trades both legs in the same second, in 75 to 100 contract clips (seen on 5 of the 14 biggest windows). Our share of the ~$20-per-chance supply could be close to zero. Nothing measured so far says it is not.
2. The largest gaps (15c to 67c, at the 12:00Z daily listing) often had no trades on either leg, so they may have been 1-contract quotes. Only the windows backed by trades on both legs count, and those were 82 of 191 national windows lasting 15 minutes or more.
3. The long windows (1 to 6 hours) were mostly 1c to 3c gaps with 1 to 2 contracts behind them (for example the Aug 31 month-end market at 95c to 96c vs the daily at 99c). They look big in minutes and are small in dollars.
4. Only about 5 chances a month, so a year of results is about 60 events. Weekly results will be noisy.
5. The monthly market charges makers a fee, which cuts the resting-order version down to the daily and weekly markets.
6. It is small: at best about $1 to $3 a day, whatever the bank size.
chk.next_test:
A paper watcher, read-only, recording live book depth (not candles) on both books during the next two overlaps:
- KXAAAGASW-26SEP28 against KXAAAGASD-26SEP28: Sep 27 8:00 AM ET to 11:59 PM ET (12:00Z Sep 27 to 03:59Z Sep 28).
- KXAAAGASM-26SEP30 against KXAAAGASD-26SEP30: Sep 29 8:00 AM ET to 11:59 PM ET.

For every moment the paired bet is positive after taker fees on both legs, log:
- the size available: the smaller of the two legs' depth at those prices;
- how many seconds the gap lasts;
- whether it is still there 1 second and 3 seconds after first seen, which is roughly our reaction time.

Pass bar, written before any number is seen: over the two events, at least $10 per event of paired-bet value that stays for 1 second or more at 20 or more contracts, and at least half of such gaps still there after 1 second.
- If it passes, go to a 10-contract live test: fill-or-cancel on the thinner leg first, then the other leg, only on gaps of 3c or more.
- If under $5 per event survives 1 second, it is dead: the rival takes it all.

Cost: about 2 days of watching and a few hundred reads, no money.
chk.capital_needed: Under $200 at a time: a 200-contract paired bet costs under $1 a contract and is tied up about 12 to 20 hours until settlement. More money would not help, because the number of cheap contracts on offer is the limit, not the bank.

ref.strongest_objection: The gaps are not left for us. One bot already takes them, firing its two legs 59-61 ms apart (median; p90 at most 77 ms). It did this on 8 of the 9 overlap dates since Aug 3 and was absent only on Aug 31. I checked with a placebo: shifting one leg's trades by 30-120 s leaves only $0.03-6 of matched value per date. After that correction, the bot made $126 on Sep 7, $177 on Sep 14 and $62 on Sep 21. That is 3-9 times the checker's "everyone combined" median of $19.48. The checker came in low because its greedy pairing used each market only once per date. So the real pot is bigger, but almost none of it is open to a slower bot. Over 7 dates the bot took $544. Only 7% of that ($36) was liquidity still sitting at arbitrage prices 5-60 s after the bot's previous clip. In September, no bot event had other traders printing at its prices on both legs in the 60 s before it fired. Our speed: our order round trip is 96 ms median (FACTS F-X07) plus about 37 ms of feed delay, against the bot's ~60 ms. We would be second in almost every race. What a second-place bot can provably collect is the leftovers. First, the "re-fire" liquidity (still there after the bot's clip): $7.07, $9.48 and $3.34 on the three September dates. Second, gaps below the bot's roughly 3-4c cutoff (its 10th-percentile edge is 3.9c) that had trades on both legs: $0.04, $1.38 and $8.97 per September date. Together that is about $3-18 per overlap date, not the 25-50% share the checker assumed. Evidence against my own case: 50-90% of the bot's events hit gaps that were already positive at the previous minute close, 1-58 s earlier. On Sep 21 it fired on a fixed 30-second cycle (at :12 and :42 past each minute; phase test 0.62 vs a random-timing 95th percentile of 0.26). So it may react more slowly than its 60 ms leg lag suggests. The trade tape cannot tell a tiny leftover quote (dust) from real size, so this is not a clean kill.

Bank size does not matter: under $200 is ever at risk. The only upside is on days the rival skips (like Aug 31) or if the live watcher shows it reacts in seconds rather than milliseconds. The full pot it takes is $62-177 per September date, about $10-25 a day, but winning it means beating a 60 ms bot from a 96 ms machine.

idea.name: Convert the Polymarket US promo credit into withdrawable cash (riskless hedge, insurance, or future deposit-match campaigns)
idea.family: promotions x cross-venue hedge (Polymarket US + Kalshi)
idea.mechanism: $48.34 of the ~$60.52 Poly balance is non-withdrawable promotional credit that can open positions; balances above the credit are withdrawable after positions settle. Variants (the first tiny test decides which): (a) riskless package: Poly leg paid with credit + opposite side on Kalshi for the same close (same strike, checked before sending); the scouts disagree on what becomes withdrawable -- if the full $1 payout of a credit-funded winner is withdrawable, spend credit on the 98-99c favourite with a 0.5-2c Kalshi hedge (~99% conversion); if only the excess over the credit is withdrawable, spend it on the cheap side a ~0.10-0.20 (ideally as a resting maker bid, avoiding the measured +1.2c taker premium) hedged with h = B*(1-a)/a Kalshi contracts (~70-80% conversion). (b) Burn it as collateral for the pin trade on Poly (I10) so its expected profit becomes withdrawable ($5-20). (c) Insurance: when the live bot fills a KXBTC15M early leg (21-45 s left, ~29 contracts, ~6/day on BTC), right AFTER (never before or instead of) the Kalshi fill, buy the same window's opposite side on Poly with credit; it pays withdrawable cash exactly when the Kalshi position loses. (d) If his account is offered a deposit-and-trading cohort (docs: $10->$10 up to $250->$500, caps $1,000/campaign, $2,000/participant; only fills at 10-90c count), meet the volume requirement with hedged maker fills (rest Poly Up bids at 10-90c, buy Down on Kalshi when filled), then convert the credit via (a). Refer-a-friend: $50 each side, max 50, real friends only (never self-referral).
idea.why_mispriced: No counterparty loses: it spends Polymarket's acquisition budget the way it was issued. Hedging is not among the listed abuse grounds (fraud, manipulation, self-dealing, self-referral, coordinated activity).
idea.must_be_true: (1) Credit-funded winnings really land as withdrawable balance, and which part (full payout vs excess) -- the docs imply it, unverified in his account. (2) The window's price-to-beat equals the Kalshi strike (16/16 so far; 222/223 settlements agree). (3) Poly does not treat the hedge as abuse; he reads the in-app terms (and the credit's expiry date). (4) The $9.67 deposit clears (availableToWithdraw is $0 now). (5) For (c): a Poly order path in the bot (not built, latency unmeasured) and the live early-leg loss rate holds over the covered week (BTC 5 of 98 is a wide interval). (6) For (d): a campaign is actually offered and its volume ratio (not stated in docs) is modest.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One-off, not daily: ~$33-49 of real cash from the existing credit (variant a), $5-20 via (b), ~$38-58 expected via (c) (offsets ~$29 of a $100+ BTC loss if one lands in the covered week; $0 cash if none does). Up to ~$350-500 more if a $250->$500 campaign is offered; $50 per genuine referral. Kalshi hedge capital ~$150-400 for < 15 minutes.
idea.data_needed: Operator reads the promo terms and credit expiry in the Polymarket US app and checks for offered campaigns; then one tiny signed-off test ($5 of credit + matched Kalshi hedge on one window) and confirm how availableToWithdraw moves.
idea.evidence_so_far: GET /v1/account/balances (read-only): currentBalance 60.5244, bonusReservation 48.337, displayedBonus 50, bonusHold 50, depositReservation 9.6674, availableToWithdraw 0. Docs (docs.polymarket.us/incentives/user-programs, faq/withdraw-promo): credits 'may not be withdrawn as cash'; 'the full promo credit must first be used as trading collateral and the related positions must settle'; balance above the credit is normal collateral that may be withdrawn; credits posted within 7 days; only $0.10-$0.90 fills count toward Deposit-and-Trading. Strike equality 16/16 (ptb_check.py). Measured Poly taker premium on longshots +1.2c. box_early.py: at 21-45 s Poly's loser ask was 2-5c, 1.70c above Kalshi's (median); live early class 09-08..09-23: all coins 21 losses of 592 (-$824.35), BTC 5 of 98 (-$333.67), BTC net -$168.87. Hedge cost for playthrough: -0.19c/contract hedging every Poly print at Kalshi's touch; +0.43 to +0.76c for a maker at <= 0.3 s. Files: sweep/cross-venue/poly_incent.out; sweep/anything-anywhere/ptb_check.py; sweep/combine-structure-incentives-hedging/box_early.py.
