WHAT DECIDES IT: nearly all the money sits in one week, and in that week the idea's own rule, "read CNN's category at 4 PM", picked the LOSER.

1) The contract terms (assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/FEAR.pdf) say the payout is on the value "at 4:00 PM ET on <date>; if no value is available at 4:00 PM ET, the last available value", and revisions after expiration do not count. Settlement is human-paced: markets closed 6 min to 23 h after 4 PM.

2) CNN REWRITES ITS OWN HISTORY. I pulled Wayback Machine copies of CNN's JSON taken on each Friday evening, as it looked at the time. Every one of the 9 Fridays differs from CNN's current history by 0.5 to 3.4 points (07-24 39.43 then vs 40.77 now, 07-31 42.46 vs 39.57, 08-21 55.17 vs 54.66, 09-04 41.86 vs 45.23, 09-18 29.11 vs 30.43). So:
- the earlier "09-04 mismatch" is an artefact of that rewrite. At the time CNN showed 41.86 (Fear), which matches Kalshi's Fear.
- the real anomaly is 08-21. CNN showed 55.51 labelled 'greed' at 17:39Z and 55.17 labelled 'greed' at end of day, yet Kalshi settled NEUTRAL. The earlier sweep only saw a match there because the history now says 54.66.
- No backtest can be built from CNN's history. There are no copies near 20:00Z on any Friday.
Script: check-I38/wb.py. The capture list is in cdx_*.json.

3) Trade tape for the 9 settled Fridays (07-24..09-18; late_KXFEAR.json from the econ sweep; my breakdown in check-I38/late_ev.py and late_ev.txt), net of taker fee:
- 08-21 at 4 PM: the first-minute buyers took GREED at 93-98c and lost $30 on 31 contracts.
- 08-21 at 20:12:18Z (+12.3 min): the market flipped. Others then bought Neutral at 57-75c: 1,321 contracts, +$379. That one week is 88% of all post-4 PM winner profit.
- 08-21 in the 30 minutes before 4 PM: buyers of the favourite (Greed at 80-97c) lost $446 on 503 contracts. Across all 9 Fridays, buyers of the favourite at 80c and up made +$61 in the other 8 weeks. Net about -$385.
- The other 8 ("clear") weeks after 4 PM: winner bought below 97c was 659 contracts (+$40.3; 612 of those on 08-14, which stayed open 23 h). Winner at 97-99c was 1,209 contracts (+$26.5). Total $66.8 in 8 weeks, and that is if WE had taken every contract.

4) How often a week sits near a category line (CNN's rewritten daily history, 251 days; check-I38/dist.py and dist.txt):
- 10 of 50 Fridays ended within 1 point of a line, 16 of 50 within 3.
- A one-day move is 2.5 points typical, 8 points in 1 day of 10, 13.6 in 1 day of 100.
- Starting 7-10 points from a line, the category still changed next day 5 times in 65. So today's Fear at 92c, with the index at 36, is roughly fair. There is no morning edge.

5) CNN's JSON returns HTTP 418 (bot block) to the request fear_rec.py sends. Its next-test script would have recorded nothing from CNN; adding an Accept header fixes it (check-I38/cnnprobe.py). CNN's cache also served data 171-208 s old while saying max-age=5.

6) Live recorder started for TODAY, a clear week (index 36, 9 points from the 45 line). Process 2980772, read-only, 28 MB. It sleeps until 19:45Z and stops itself at 21:45Z. It logs CNN every 5 s, Kalshi prices every 30 s and the top-2 order books every 60 s to check-I38/fear_today_KXFEAR-26SEP25.jsonl. kalshi_collector (pid 2532788) and crypto_feeds (pid 105352) are alive. Free disk 87 GB.

Smallest effect this sample can detect: with 1 week near a line out of 9, the sample cannot tell the rule in boundary weeks, or even whether they make or lose money.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
Weeks far from a line: all winner supply below 99c after 4 PM was $66.8 net in 8 weeks, or $8.35 a week, if we got 100% of it. That is $1.19 per calendar day. At a realistic 30-50% share against the others who took it, that is $0.36-0.60 a day. It needs under $700 of capital for minutes to 1 day, so it is the same at $900 and at $5k: supply sets the limit, not the bank.

Weeks near a line (about 5-10 Fridays a year): each is roughly a ±$100-450 bet whose SIGN depends on a rule we do not know. The only example, 08-21, went against the naive rule.
- If a rule is learned that the next boundary weeks confirm: maybe 2-5 usable weeks a year × $100-380. That is about $0.5-5 a day, not measured.
- Until then, expected value is unknown and possibly negative.

Honest total today: under $1 a day, at either bank size.
chk.worst_case:
A week near a line, bought on CNN's own 4 PM label:
- 100 contracts at 95c: -$95.3 including fee.
- Sized to the favourite supply that existed on 08-21 (about 500 contracts at 80-97c): about -$450. That is what the market's favourite buyers actually lost that day, and it is 6.7x the $66.8 that all 8 clear weeks paid to every winner buyer combined.
chk.killer_risks:
1) We do not know how Kalshi reads the value. On 08-21 CNN's own JSON label said Greed at 17:39Z (55.51) and at end of day (55.17), but Kalshi paid Neutral. Two explanations fit and cannot be told apart from one example:
- Kalshi uses the rounded whole number (55) and CNN's 45-55 Neutral band.
- Kalshi reads the page whenever its settler gets to it (that close came at +67 min), after the value had moved.

2) The market flipped at 20:12:18Z for a reason we cannot see. Whoever bought Neutral knew something 12 minutes after 4 PM; a bot that locks in the 4 PM reading would have held the loser.

3) No backtest is possible. CNN rewrites past values by 0.5-3.4 points, and the Wayback Machine has no copies near 4 PM on any Friday. Every past claim built on CNN's history is contaminated, including this idea's "8 of 9 match".

4) Tiny supply in clear weeks. Offers of the winner below 97c are mostly gone by 4 PM, and 85% of the clear-week money came from one 23-hour slow settlement (08-14).

5) The data feed is fragile. CNN blocks bare requests with HTTP 418, and its cache served 3-minute-old data.

6) Kalshi's settlement is human-paced and it can start an outcome review. Correlation across events does not apply (one event a week).

Rule and pass bar, written down before any boundary week is seen:
- Rule: the whole number shown at 20:00Z, mapped to 0-24 / 25-44 / 45-55 / 56-75 / 76-100.
- Before any money: at least 3 recorded boundary Fridays (within 1 point of a line at 4 PM) where this rule matches Kalshi's result 3 of 3, including at least one where it disagrees with CNN's own label.
- Then 1-contract live trades on boundary weeks only.
- Clear-week bar: at least $10 a week of winner offers below 97c still on the book 60 s after 4 PM, averaged over 4 Fridays.
- Expect 3-6 months to see 3 boundary weeks.
chk.capital_needed: Under $700 per week, tied up for 6 minutes to 23 hours after 4 PM on Fridays. A bigger bank adds nothing, because supply sets the limit.

ref.strongest_objection:
The idea assumes the category is decided at 4 PM ET, so a bot can read the result right afterwards and buy it. That assumption is wrong.

The contract (assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/FEAR.pdf) pays on "the value of the Underlying as documented by the Source Agency on the Expiration Date at the Expiration time". Kalshi moves that expiration time to whenever its settler acts. Over the 9 real weeks, the settler acted anywhere from 6.2 minutes to 23.5 hours after 4 PM.

CNN's number keeps changing after 4 PM:
- components re-stamp about every 5 minutes until roughly 20:20Z
- S&P momentum and put/call update between 20:14Z and 22:32Z
- breadth and strength update between 23:45Z and 00:59Z
- CNN then rewrites past days for up to a week

In a week near a category line, which are the only weeks with money in them, that movement is larger than the distance to the line. So buying "the settled category" after 4 PM is really a bet on when a Kalshi employee looks at the page. It is not reading a fact.

08-21, the only week that paid, shows exactly this:
- Greed bought at 93-98c in the first minute.
- Neutral bought at 57-75c at +12 to +14 min, while someone else bought Greed at 41-42c at +13 min.
- Neutral reached 99c at +14.4 min.
- At +64 min, 2.5 minutes before Kalshi closed at 21:06:40Z, someone sold Neutral back down to 83-87c and bought Greed at 18c.
- CNN's own value for that day moved 55.51 (Greed) at 17:39Z, 55.17 (Greed) at 23:59Z, 54.51 (Neutral) by 08-25, and 54.66 today. It crossed the line twice.

The Neutral buyers won because the settler happened to look at +67 min. The weeks read at +5.3 h (09-04) and +23.5 h (08-14) show the settler sometimes reads the late value.

The one repeatable rule that could be learned is "Kalshi uses CNN's whole number, not its label". Whole number and label disagree on about 1 Friday a year: 1 of 51 Fridays and 5 of 252 days in CNN's history. The checker's pass bar needs 3 boundary weeks including one of those disagreements, which would take years to reach.

Weeks far from a line pay at most $1.19 a day even if we had taken every contract, and 85% of that came from one week (08-14) that happened to settle 23 hours late.

idea.name: Hurricane markets: NHC b-deck/recon lead and the first-Atlantic-hurricane fan-out
idea.family: weather / hurricanes x NHC raw feeds (one advisory settles many markets)
idea.mechanism: (1) NHC's ATCF best-track files (ftp.nhc.noaa.gov/atcf/btk/b<basin><nn><yyyy>.dat) and Hurricane Hunter HDOB/vortex messages can show a storm crossing a Saffir-Simpson line (64/83/96/113/137 kt) before the public advisory; buy the threshold YES in that gap. (2) Fan-out: the moment an official product states >= 64 kt for the first 2026 Atlantic hurricane (Fay or next), buy YES on its T1, FIRSTHURRICANE-<name>, NAMES-<name> and every NEXTHURDATE rung, and NO on every other name in FIRSTHURRICANE; start with the thinnest, least-watched books. (3) After an event the market stays open until the first 10 AM ET: a 1-2c post-lock sweep. Hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: Retail reads advisories on TV/apps; makers quote from the last advisory. Watchers of the storm's own market are not the holders of 'next hurricane date' or other-name lottery tickets, so those resting orders may stay stale for minutes to hours.
idea.must_be_true: b-deck/recon updates reach the public 30-90 min before the advisory; Kalshi settles on operational advisories, not a later best-track revision (rule: 'reaches maximum sustained winds >= X' from NOAA/TWC; expiry first 10 AM ET after the event); sibling books lag the storm book (NOT measured: no Atlantic hurricane yet in 2026) and have depth at that moment.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0-5/day averaged, lumpy and seasonal; fan-out one-off $0-200 when the next Atlantic storm upgrades.
idea.data_needed: Over the next 2-3 active storms: b-deck FTP modification times vs advisory issuance vs Kalshi 1-minute candles on the crossed threshold. Fan-out watcher: snapshot all sibling books plus NHC product times every 30 s until the first Atlantic upgrade; bar >= 500 contracts at <= 90c on locked-YES rungs or >= 10c on locked-NO names still resting 60 s after the product time.
idea.evidence_so_far: Active 09-25: Fay (TS 45 kt, T1 7/10c then 9/12c, 36k volume), Gonzalo (TS 40 kt), Odalys (HU 95 kt, T3 80/85c), Polo (b-deck peak 145 kt, T5 99/100 -- priced), Nolo (65 kt hurricane at 06Z while KXHURCAT-26NOLO-T1 sat at 97/98c). FIRSTHURRICANE-FAY 10/15c (series OI ~334k), other names HAN 30/35c, ISA 17/21c, GON 3/4c; NAMES-FAY 6/11c; NEXTHURDATE Oct 1 8/16c, Oct 15 22/36c, Nov 1 58/70c, Nov 15 68/92c, Dec 1 70/87c. East Pacific precedent (Odalys): T1 and NAMES-ODA both reached 97-98c within the same hours around 09-23 09-12Z with only 10s-100s of contracts an hour (no lag seen, books too thin to say). v24 ~38k contracts across the family. Files: sweep/combine-information-speed/hur_list.py, hur_tape.py; sweep/weather-science/.

chk.measured:
PLAIN ANSWER: part (3) of the idea, buying a threshold after NHC has already published it, has made real money for other people. But 86% of that money came from one surprise event. Part (1), the b-deck lead, and part (2), the fan-out, are unproven.

1) Settlement rule (Kalshi contract terms, ct_HURCAT.pdf). HURCAT pays YES if ANY NHC or CPHC Discussion 'INIT ... MPH' value reaches the threshold (74/96/111/130/157 mph). It settles on the published advisories, not on NHC's later cleaned-up storm record. So once a discussion prints the number, the market is decided and there is no revision risk. The b-deck is NOT the settlement source. Trading runs until the first 10 AM ET after the event, and money comes back in about 1-1.5 days (Fausto T2: locked 07-24 09Z, settled 07-25 14:40Z).

2) Release timing (NWS API, 75 discussions 09-19..09-25, tcd.json). Discussions go out 5-25 minutes before their nominal time, for example 08:32-08:56Z for a 09Z advisory. The Odalys special advisory went out at 11:43Z.

3) Every 2026 threshold crossing. There were 32, across 9 East/Central Pacific hurricanes from 07-20 to 09-25; the Atlantic has had ZERO hurricanes this year. I parsed all 347 archived discussions (disc.py -> disc.json) and pulled Kalshi trades from 12 hours before to 96 hours after each crossing (crosstape.py, stale.py).
 - 22 of 32 left nothing to buy cheaply: the market was already at 98-99c, or nobody traded.
 - In 10 of 32, takers bought the already-decided side at 97c or less after the lock. Total 7,003 contracts, $2,795 profit after fees.
 - FAUSTO T2 alone was $2,405. The 07-24 09Z CPHC discussion said 85 kt / 100 mph when NHC had been forecasting weakening. The market sat at 3-4c. The first buyer arrived 2h14m later (11:13:58Z) and swept 4c up to 70c. The price reached 99c at 12:51Z. I checked for a measurement bug: I read the discussion text myself (INIT 24/0900Z 85 KT 100 MPH), the market settled YES, and there were no trades between 09:00Z and 11:13Z.
 - ODALYS T4 was $277. The special advisory went out at 11:43Z and someone swept 40c to 99c at 11:45:05Z. That is a competitor 2 minutes from publication.

chk.worst_case: Buying a contract I wrongly think is already decided costs the whole stake. The basin mix-up already happened in this check: I counted NAMES-EPAC-LOW as decided when Lowell became a hurricane in the Central Pacific. On a surprise event sized to the bank, that is up to -$900 at $900 and -$2-5k at $5k. All fan-out legs rest on the same parse, so they fail together. A cap of about $400 per event at $900 limits it to -$400. Trading on the b-deck (not a lock) risks the full price paid if the advisory does not confirm; the Odalys file-vs-advisory gap shows this can happen.

ref.strongest_objection:
What's left of this idea is a speed race against traders who are already in these markets. It is not a lead nobody else has. The $2,405 Fausto windfall (86% of the measured money) happened in July. Since late August, other traders are there within seconds to minutes:
- KXHURCAT-26LOWELL-T4: someone bought at 02:37:02.5Z. The locking NHC discussion went out in minute 02:37 (the timestamp in the product's header). So they bought within about 2 seconds of it going out.
- KARINA-T3: someone bought 5 seconds before the discussion went out, probably off the public advisory or the short update NHC sometimes issues just before it.
- MARIE-T2 was swept at +158 s and ODALYS-T4 (today) at +126 s. On Odalys T4 one order cleared every offer from 40c to 99c in the same second.

There is also a large buyer resting orders at 99c: 35,000 to 67,000 contracts on every one of the 10 still-open decided East Pacific markets, with nothing offered for sale. That kills part (3), the 1-2c sweep after a lock: there is nothing left to sweep. It also means any cheap offer is gone the moment that buyer places its order.

Only 2 of 32 threshold crossings were real surprises (price under 50c just before NHC published): Fausto T2 at 3c (first buyer +155 min, July) and Odalys T4 at 35c (+126 s, 09-25). What remains is a winner-take-most race. Winning it needs an automatic buy triggered by reading the NHC text, and a misread loses the whole stake.

Two corrections to the checker:
1. Money is NOT back in 1-1.5 days. Across the 18 settled crossings, the median from lock to settlement is 8.7 days (range 1.2 to 18.7 days). The escape is selling into that 99c buyer for about 1c a contract.
2. Kalshi uses its discretion. It listed KXHURCAT-26LALA on 09-24, four weeks after Lala died and after it had already reached 130 mph. Those markets trade at 87-95c, and the 99c buyer stays out. The contract's underlying is 'wind speeds ... between Issuance and <date>', so a 'lock' there is a bet on how Kalshi reads its own rule.

None of this makes the idea dead. On Odalys T4 today the winner took 126 s, so a poller detecting within 30-60 s would have won about $215. But the realistic figure is well below the checker's $5-15/day.

chk.measured:
What kills it: the idea needs the bot's volatility estimate to lag after a big print, and it does not. The bot has also traded almost none of the closes the gate would skip. Every script below passed a planted-answer self-test first.

1) THE BOT'S OWN VOLATILITY READING AFTER BIG PRINTS (raw index tape, no replay code). The live bot measures volatility as the spread of 1-second index moves over the last 5 minutes (SIGMA_RULER="live", SIGMA_WIN=300 in research/pinrun.py; no flag in restart_bot.ps1 changes that). At the 45-second entry of the 8:45 ET close, those 5 minutes run from 8:39 to 8:44 ET, which is all after the 8:30 print. BTC's reading against what the index then did over the rest of the window: 09-04 (jobs report) 1.66 vs 1.90 bps, so it read 13% low; 09-11 (CPI) 1.85 vs 1.55 bps, so it read high. Median across all 11 coins: 1.43x under on 09-04, 0.62x over on 09-11. FOMC 09-16, 2:15 PM ET close: 0.97. Across the 6 big-print closes (66 coin-decisions where the bot's math said 95%+ sure) the model missed 0 times. The biggest miss in standard deviations was 2.8.

2) THE SAME QUESTION ON EVERY CLOSE ON TAPE, which has far more data. 2,647 closes from 08-25 to 09-25, 86,622 coin/close/time-left rows. Each close is grouped by 'burst': volatility over the last 15 minutes divided by volatility over the hour before. A big print pushes this to 4-6. In the top 5% of burst (burst of 2.36 or more), realised volatility over the rest of the window was a median 0.64-0.67x the bot's reading, so the bot OVER-reads. In the calmest fifth it was 0.84x. The model's miss rate at 95%+ confidence, 45 s out, top 5% burst: 1 miss in 1,362 decisions (1 losing close of 705). Every other bucket: 95 misses in 24,440 (0.39%, 77 losing closes of about 8,900). At the calmer rate we would expect about 6 losing closes; we saw 1. With this sample, a doubling of risk after bursts would have shown clearly, and the data points the opposite way. This is the model's miss rate on the index. It is NOT our loss rate (rule 5).

3) LIVE FILLS, the only source for our losses. 990 settled live markets, 09-08 to 09-25. Six named releases (claims 09-10, 09-17, 09-24; CPI 09-11; FOMC 09-16 plus the 2:30 press conference). On closes a print can actually reach, the bot traded 4 distinct closes in 18 days, 0 losing, +$2.03. On the one big 8:30 ET release since going live (CPI 09-11) it traded NEITHER the 8:45 nor the 9:00 ET close: the log says 'decided but NOBODY OFFERED the winning side' at 8:45 and only 2 thin offers at 9:00. The market already prices the storm. So the gate would have blocked $0 of trades since live started.

4) THE EVIDENCE IN THE IDEA HAS A CLASSING BUG. pin_macro.py's '1 losing close of 7 in the named-release windows, -$7.03' classed closes by the settle-record time (close + 20 s). That pulled in the 8:30 ET close itself, whose settlement average ended 1 second BEFORE the print. The one loss is KXSOL15M-26SEP110830-30, -$12.16 at 59c. The print cannot have caused it. Corrected: 0 losing closes after any print.

5) LIVE MONEY BY BURST (live fills; the tape only supplies the burst number). Burst of 1.6 or more: 21 closes, 1 losing (HYPE 09-21 at 6:15 PM ET, no release), -$10.72. 1.2-1.6: 88 closes, 4 losing, +$143.31. Under 1.2: 642 closes, 18 losing, +$616.88. Flat within noise. With 21 closes, a losing-close rate anywhere from 0% to about 24% fits the data. 78 markets fell in tape gaps and are not counted.

Artefact checks. The ruler code copies pinrun's _sig_over (last 300 held seconds, consecutive differences only). Planted-world self-test (selftest.py): a steady-volatility world reads honest (spread of misses 1.06, forward/reading 0.99). A planted late burst is caught (2.94). A decaying burst reads as over-read (0.92). 23 of 718 tape hours were truncated gzip files; the three big-print hours were readable. The strike was rebuilt from our own prints, which affects the miss count but not the volatility ratio.

Side finding: the idea's claim that every scheduled release lands exactly on a 15-minute roll is right. Also, after a burst the bot is too cautious rather than too bold. That could only be a 'make more' angle, it rests on the tape alone, and offers vanish in those closes.

chk.measured:
WHAT KILLS IT: in the extra minutes the early readings open up, the people selling to us are usually right. On the offered order books, the early clock (0.5F margin, last 4.5 min) lost on 3 of 37 markets. Across all hours, the index ends on the wrong side of a 0.5F-margin strike only 17 of 1,912 times (0.9%) in 10 days, so markets with a seller lose about 9x more often. 1) THE PAID FEED IS NOT NEEDED. idea.name: CME fed-funds/SOFR futures mirror into the Kalshi Fed complex (non-print news)
idea.family: cross-asset (CME futures) x Kalshi Fed markets
markets: CME ZQ (30-day fed funds) or SR3 (SOFR) futures (read-only data feed)
idea.mechanism: Subscribe to a real-time CME feed for the fed funds futures spanning the next meeting; keep a running basis between the futures-implied hike probability (FedWatch arithmetic) and the Kalshi H25 mid. When the implied probability jumps >= 4 points within seconds (scheduled print, flash PMI, FOMC presser, Fed speaker, a Timiraos article, a Trump post), buy the Kalshi leg toward pre-jump Kalshi price + jump while the Kalshi book is stale; exit at convergence. The futures market does the interpretation within milliseconds.
idea.why_mispriced: Same slow Kalshi book as I07, but repricing after non-print news is slower still (minutes); Kalshi Fed traders mostly watch headlines, not futures.
idea.must_be_true: Futures actually moved at the times the Kalshi book staircased (not checked); Kalshi lags futures by >= 20 s on non-print news; the basis is stable over minutes; a retail non-professional real-time CME data subscription is cheap enough (price unverified, roughly $10-25/month); futures moves reflect the target-range decision at the next meeting, not month-average timing effects.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $5-20/day on top of I07: ~1.5 extra >= 5c moves a week repricing over 1-5 minutes, capturing ~1,000-1,500 contracts at 4-8c each, minus the data subscription.
idea.data_needed: One week of a real-time ZQ/SR3 feed (paper) next to KXFEDDECISION-26OCT trades. Bar: >= 3 events where futures moved >= 4 implied points and Kalshi's mid was still >= 3 points behind 15 s later.

chk.measured:
Source: CME futures 1-minute trade bars from Yahoo's public chart API (ZQV26, ZQX26, SR3Z26, 08-27 to 09-25, 21 trading days, 12:00-21:00Z), matched against every Kalshi trade in KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H25 (08-17 to 09-16) and -26OCT-H25 (09-16 to 09-25, 2,311 trades, 781k contracts). Futures price changes were converted to hike-probability points (dp = -dPx/0.25). ZQV26 was used for the Sept meeting and ZQX26 for the Oct meeting. Today's level check: futures imply about a 66% chance of an Oct hike and Kalshi H25 trades 0.65/0.66, so the two agree.

Bar timing was checked against known release times (CPI 09-11 and NFP 09-04 jump in the 12:30 bar, so bars are stamped at their start). An off-by-one in my own code had made Kalshi appear to lead futures by 1 minute. I fixed it before reading any results.

1) Minute-by-minute correlation of Kalshi price changes with earlier futures changes: 10.7k minutes. Same minute 0.160. One minute later 0.043, then 0.015, 0.037, 0.011 and 0.037 at 2-5 minutes (2-sigma noise level is 0.019). So Kalshi mostly moves in the same minute as futures, with a small delayed tail.

2) Gap trade, where futures moved at least 4 points more than Kalshi over 2 minutes: 18 events on 9 days. Kalshi closed 2.61 points of the gap by +10 min (se 0.85, 12 of 18 the right way). Buying at last price +1c and selling 10 min later with the taker fee both ways: -1.67c per contract. At a 6-point gap: 4 events, +0.75 points (se 1.65), -3.40c. For SR3 moves of at least 10 Oct-scaled points: 12 events, +3.6 points at +5 min, -0.4c per contract after costs.

3) Futures-anchored basis reversion, deviation of at least 4 points from the prior-hour median: 21 events. Kalshi moved toward futures 16 to 18 times out of 21, by +2.0 points at +5 min, +2.2 at +10 and +3.3 at +30. Round trip -2.0c to -0.9c per contract. Holding to settlement: -0.5c to +0.6c. The lead is real, but it is smaller than the cost of trading it.

4) Optimistic zero-delay ceiling: enter at Kalshi's last price before the minute the futures began moving (upper.py). In the 12 true non-print events, Kalshi's later move averaged +1.25 points at +5 min and +2.33 at +10 min, against a one-way cost of about 2.75c (1c spread plus about 1.75c fee near 50c). The 3 print-minute events moved +12 points, but I07 already showed Kalshi reprices within 0.07-1.5 seconds of prints. The only clearly good case is the FOMC press conference on 09-16. Futures moved at 18:31-18:33 and Kalshi sat at 0.33-0.34 until 18:34 (2,868 contracts traded at 0.34 in 18:33), then jumped to 0.42, a +7 point gain after 10 min. That is n=1.

5) Futures do not lead cleanly. On 09-10 (PPI), 08-28 14:24 and the flash PMI on 09-23 13:45, futures themselves climbed in steps over 5-12 minutes, and Kalshi followed within about 0-2 minutes. After the trigger, futures gave back 0.4 to 2.5 points on average, which is part of why Kalshi only half-follows.

Fees: the series is quadratic_with_maker_fees, so a maker exit is not free either. Current book: H25 bid 0.65 x 59,031, ask 0.66 (ask depth 4,404). Depth is not the constraint; the bank is.

Smallest effect this sample can detect: 12 non-print events with a spread of about 3 points gives about 1.8 points at 2-sigma. The observed +2.33 ± 0.9 sits below the 2.75c one-way cost and well below the roughly 4.3c round-trip cost.

Artefact checks: a random-minute, random-direction control gave -0.02 to +0.03 points (n=2,000). Futures bars are last trades, and back-month ZQ moves 2 points per tick, so small signals are noisy. I did not verify from a real-time source that Yahoo's history is complete. The live Yahoo feed runs about 10 minutes behind (last bar 13:32Z at 13:43Z), so it cannot be used to trade.

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
$900 bank: about -$1 to $0 a day. The measured edge per contract after costs is negative: -1.7c to -2.4c per contract on a round trip, and about -0.4c holding to settlement, in the optimistic zero-delay version. Holding to settlement also locks the whole bank until the meeting (Oct 28, 33 days), so it can fire only about once per 6-week cycle. Real-time CME data costs about $2-15 a month through a broker such as IBKR (price unverified; the page returned 403), or $179 a month for Databento's live Standard plan.

Only positive corner: FOMC press conferences, n=1, +7 points gross. Roughly +4c net x ~2,500 contracts ≈ $100 per press conference x 8 a year ≈ $2 a day, carrying the risk of losing the whole bank on one hold-to-settle. One observation cannot support that number.

$5k bank: the same negative edge per contract, so size does not help. The press-conference-only version gives about 5,000-8,000 contracts x 4c ≈ $200-300 per press conference, or $4-6 a day, with n=1.
chk.worst_case: Holding to settlement at the $900 bank: about 2,500 contracts at around 35c is the whole bank on one binary Fed decision, a loss of $875 if the meeting goes the other way. Exiting after 10 minutes instead: a press-conference reversal like 09-16 18:35-18:41 (futures 48 to 42, Kalshi 0.42 to 0.38) costs about 10 points x 2,500 = $250 plus about $90 in fees. At $5k with 8,000 contracts: about $800 plus $280 in fees on a reversal, or up to $5k held to settlement.
chk.killer_risks:
The number that kills it: after a futures-led move, Kalshi's remaining catch-up averages only 2.3-3.6 points, even with zero delay. That is less than the 2.75c it costs to get in (1c spread plus about 1.75c fee near 50c), and much less than the 4.3c+ round trip. Maker fees apply on this series, so exiting passively does not escape the cost.

Supporting reasons:
- On prints, Kalshi reprices within 1-2 seconds (I07), so there is no lead to take.
- On slow news, futures themselves climb in steps and partly give the move back (they drift -0.4 to -2.5 points after the trigger), so Kalshi only half-follows for good reason.
- Holding to settlement turns a sub-cent edge into a coin-flip on the whole bank and locks capital for up to 6 weeks.
- Kalshi's Fed book already has market makers who plainly price off futures: the same-minute correlation dominates and today's levels agree to within 1 point.
- The only case with a real edge (the 09-16 press conference, +7 points) is a single observation, and 8 press conferences a year cannot validate it quickly.
chk.next_test: Only if the press-conference corner is worth $2-6 a day to the operator. Databento gives new accounts $125 of free credit. Pull CME GLBX.MDP3 tick-level trades-with-best-quote data for ZQX26/ZQV26/SR3Z26 from 08-17 to 09-25 (likely a few dollars, covered by the credit) and line it up with Kalshi H25/H0 trades to the second. Pass bar, written before looking: over at least 8 non-print events (including the 09-16 press conference), Kalshi must still move at least 4.0 points in the futures' direction between 5 seconds after the futures move starts and +10 min, and at least 3,000 contracts must trade at or better than the entry price within 60 seconds. If it fails, close I42 for good. If it passes, run a paper watcher (no orders) through the Oct 28 FOMC press conference on a real-time CBOT feed. Yahoo's feed is about 10 minutes behind and cannot be used live.
chk.capital_needed: None to reject it. Retesting the press-conference corner needs a Databento signup (free $125 credit), then a real-time CBOT subscription (about $2-15 a month via a broker such as IBKR, which needs an account; or $179 a month via Databento Standard).

idea.name: Maker on Polymarket US, hedge on Kalshi (cheap-side longshot premium first)
idea.family: cross-venue market making + Poly maker rebate
idea.mechanism: Rest Poly quotes at Kalshi's touch + Kalshi taker fee + a margin, rounded away from the market to Poly's 1c tick; re-derive whenever Kalshi's book moves the target by 1c. When a Poly taker fills us, immediately take the same outcome on Kalshi at its ask (same BRTI 60-s average and strike, so the pair pays exactly $1). Preferred form: quote ONLY the cheap outcome (<= ~12-15c) at Kalshi ask + 1c, where Poly takers are measured overpaying and uninformed; locked per contract = Poly sale price - Kalshi ask - Kalshi fee 0.07p(1-p) + Poly maker rebate 0.0125p(1-p) (~+0.6c at p=0.10, ~0 at p=0.20). Unhedged variant keeps the Poly favourite to settlement (adds flip risk). Can double as the volume engine for a Poly deposit-match campaign (I14).
idea.why_mispriced: Poly takers buying the cheaper side paid +1.1c to +1.7c ABOVE Kalshi's same-second price in every one of 9 windows (per-window mean +1.23c, sd 0.36, t=10), on top of Poly's taker fee: price-insensitive Poly-only retail and promo-credit holders (the rational use of non-withdrawable credit is a longshot). Favourite-side takers pay ~0 premium and look informed (Kalshi mid moved +5.0c their way within 60 s, t=2.2), hence one-sided cheap quotes only. Overall Poly takers pay on average 1.05c above Kalshi's mid.
idea.must_be_true: (a) Premium holds across US hours and weekends on the full 3-day recording (~250 windows), not just 03:15-07:00Z. (b) Not an artefact of Kalshi ticker-channel staleness (the ticker lags the book by ~1-3 s; redo with orderbook_delta). (c) A Kalshi+1c ask is the best Poly ask often enough to be lifted (queue competition unknown). (d) Requote round trip <= 0.3 s and hedge <= 0.5 s for the general maker (the sim turns negative at 1 s); our quote strictly better than Poly's touch. (e) Poly allows him API order entry (current key read-only) within its 20 req/s limit. (f) Poly trade 'quantity' units (labelled USD, ambiguous).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Cheap-side hedged: ~$2-20/day at $300-500 kept on Poly (each contract ties ~$0.85-0.90 on Poly + ~$0.10-0.15 on Kalshi); < $1-2/day at today's ~$60. General maker: $5-20/day at <= 0.3 s with current capital; negative at >= 0.5-1 s latency. Anything above $20/day is unproven.
idea.data_needed: Rerun sweep/anything-anywhere/credit_premium.py on the full recording (~09-28) with Kalshi orderbook_delta, split by hour and weekday, clustered by window; a queue replay of how often a Kalshi+1c ask would have been best and lifted. Pre-registered bar: premium >= 1.0c on >= 80% of windows at p <= 0.15. Measure Poly order-entry round trip from this box (and from a Lightsail Ohio box) -- placing any order needs per-order sign-off -- then a 1-contract maker test.
idea.evidence_so_far: 24,412 Poly 15-min trades (unique ids; median size 11, p90 66) over 9-10 windows 09-25 03:15-07:00Z joined to Kalshi ticker: premium vs Kalshi ask by bucket 0-5c +1.11c, 5-10c +1.71c, 10-15c +1.17c, 15-20c +1.21c, 20-30c +1.26c, 30-40c +1.41c, 40-60c +0.54c, 60-80c -0.22c, 80-90c +0.44c, 90-100c -0.05c; 60-s drift of Kalshi mid on the taker's side: < 20c buyers -4.3c (8 of 9 windows negative), >= 80c buyers +5.0c; random-sign control +0.14c. anything-anywhere: Poly US longshot premium: sell the cheap side on Polymarket US, hedge the same contract on Kalshi
idea.novelty_vs_killed: D17/MAKER_SIM killed resting quotes on KALSHI's 15-min books (informed flow, -1.6c). Here the fill is on Polymarket US, on the side where takers are measured to overpay and be uninformed, hedged on Kalshi the same second; MAKER_SIM explicitly says it is not evidence about the Poly book. The SECOND_INCOME cross-venue kill was taker+taker on a 30-s cached gateway.
idea.prior_reason: The longshot premium is strong (t=10) but measured on one night session with the lagging ticker channel; our fill share, latency and Poly API access are unknown, and the hedged margin is only ~0.6c at p<=0.12 on a $60 bank.
idea.worst_case: The premium is an overnight effect or belongs to faster makers; our asks fill only when Kalshi has just moved (stale quote picked off), so the hedge costs more than the premium: a steady small loss per fill (~-1c/contract at 1 s latency), bounded by size; Poly changes the rebate or fees.

chk.measured:
The Poly takers' premium is real, but it is not money we can collect. The makers already on Poly are quoting where we would: about 1c above Kalshi's ask. So our quote only gets filled after Kalshi has moved against us, and the Kalshi fee on the hedge eats the margin.

Sources: both venues' raw books (direct), plus a replay of our fills. By CLAUDE.md rules the fill replay is a hypothesis. The killing number (B) is a direct book measurement, not the replay.

Data and checks:
- Poly: WS recording scan_poly_ws.jsonl.gz. 42,243 unique trades, 135,440 full-book frames. 20 of the 15-min windows have both venues, closes 03:30Z to 13:30Z on 2026-09-25 (a Friday; no weekend in the sample). Only about half the windows were recorded because the recorder hit "max subscriptions per connection reached" 14 times.
- Kalshi: KXBTC15M top of book rebuilt from orderbook_delta for 44 markets (kbook2.py -> kb_*.json). It matches the ticker channel on 91.6% of messages at the same receive time (kbcheck.py). Both venues are compared on this box's receive clock.
- Units question (f) is settled: Poly trade 'quantity' is CONTRACTS, not USD. When a single trade falls between two book frames, book depletion divided by trade quantity has a median of 1.000 in every price band (n = 2,000 / 4,483 / 2,404). The mixed-band median of 0.987 on the "USD" test was a coincidence.

(A) Premium: cheap-side (paid <= 15c) Poly takers paid +1.14c above Kalshi's book ask (mean over 20 windows, sd 0.33, t = 15.6). It held in every hour tested (03Z +0.92, 05Z +1.49, 09Z +0.71, 12Z +1.44, 13Z +1.29). The pre-registered bar (premium >= 1.0c on >= 80% of windows) FAILS: 12 of 20 windows (60%).

(B) THE KILL. At the moment of each cheap-side trade, Poly's own best ask for that side was already Kalshi ask plus a per-window mean of +0.22c to +1.59c. The touch sat at Kalshi+2c or worse for a median of only about 6% of cheap-side volume (range 0-45%). The premium is the existing Poly makers' margin, not an unclaimed gap.

(C) Pickers exist. 1.8% of 391k cheap-side Poly contracts (and 2-16% of all volume per window) were bought below Kalshi's same-side bid, even after the Poly taker fee. That means stale Poly quotes do get lifted.

(D) Replay of our quote (cheap side only, strictly better than Poly's best, hedged at Kalshi's ask, Kalshi fee rounded up per order, Poly rebate rounded per order). Our fills are the bad ones: Kalshi's ask rises before the hedge by +0.44 to +0.58c at 0.3 s quote/hedge latency, +0.71 to +2.3c at 1 s and +1.4 to +4.3c at 2 s. Net per contract:
- 0.3 s latency: -0.03 to +0.42c
- 1.0 s quote / 0.5 s hedge: -0.01 to -1.00c

idea.name: Route BTC entries and hedges to the cheaper book (Kalshi vs Polymarket US)
idea.family: cross-venue execution / lose less
idea.mechanism: When pinrun enters a BTC 15-min market (~10/day; 68 in the last 7 days) or its hedge fires (belief falls to 0.40), compare Poly's price for that side with Kalshi's (ask + fee) and send all or part to the cheaper venue. If Poly does not acknowledge within a set time, fall back to Kalshi; the Kalshi hedge always remains the fallback so routing can never block a hedge.
idea.why_mispriced: Poly's book lags Kalshi's by a median 1.85 s after moves and quotes in whole cents, so it is often 1-2c cheaper on the side being bought; in 'pin in trouble' jumps (loser 5c -> 25c) Poly makers have sometimes lagged several seconds.
idea.must_be_true: The saving survives our size (Poly had >= 50 shares in 73% of cheaper seconds; the pin buys 20-76 contracts). Poly order latency < ~1 s (unmeasured). The lag in rare large jumps is systematic, not the 2-of-3 luck seen. Poly depth and the ~$60 balance cover part of a hedge.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0.5-3/day, weak but pure lose-less; hedge part < $1/day (live BTC hedges: 4 markets, 355 contracts, $260 over 09-08..09-23).
idea.data_needed: Join the live bot's KXBTC15M order records (t_ms_send, exec_price, filled) to Poly's real-time book as the recorder continues; re-run lag_hedge.py on the full 3-day recording (~09-28) restricted to jumps where the dear side starts at <= 10c.
idea.evidence_so_far: Per second over 8 windows, requiring >= 0.5c saving: sides priced 70-95c in the last 120 s: Poly cheaper in 35% of seconds (avg 1.39c); 30-70c: 18-21% (1.5-1.6c); 5-30c: 5% (1.7c); otherwise Poly cost 0.2-1.8c more (xv_route.py). lag_hedge.py over 13 windows (09-25 03:30-08:30Z), Kalshi book rebuilt: 69 jumps >= 5c in 2 s in the last 300 s; Poly's dear side cheaper by median +3.0c at the same instant, 0.0c at +1 s, 0.0c at +2 s, -0.1c at +4 s; >= 5c saving at +1 s in 3 of 69; of 3 jumps with the dear side starting <= 10c, savings at +1 s +11.5c, +6.2c, +1.1c. box_early2.py: at 21-45 s the Poly WINNER is 0.56c cheaper than Kalshi's (median after fees; p10 1.49c), median 1,352 shares at the ask. chk.measured:
WHY IT IS SMALL: Polymarket only quotes whole cents. The pin buys BTC with Kalshi's ask at 0.97-0.98, so Poly is only cheaper when it sits a full cent lower. When it is, the gap usually lasts less than a second. The biggest per-second savings came in contested windows where the pin did not trade.

1) THE ONE REAL OVERLAP. Only one live KXBTC15M entry falls inside the Poly real-time recording (03:16Z-13:45Z 09-25): the 07:00Z close, tau 45, 29.3 contracts at 0.972 on Kalshi. Poly's book at that second would have saved $0.001. Sample: 1 entry. Source: results/pinrun-live-2026092*.jsonl joined to scan_poly_ws.jsonl.gz.

2) PER-SECOND, BOTH BOOKS. I rebuilt Kalshi's BTC ask ladders from the tape (kbook2.py, snapshot+delta, 17 windows). I compared them second by second with Poly's ladder for tau 3-45, all-in: Kalshi fee 0.07p(1-p), Poly fee 0.0695p(1-p), 98c ceiling.
- Of 177 winner-side seconds, 20 had BOTH venues at or below 98c (3 windows: 05:15, 05:30, 07:00). 19 had only Poly (3 windows). 138 had neither: the winner was at 99c on both.
- In the 20 both-venue seconds the best-price gap (Kalshi minus Poly) was median +0.38c, p10 -0.75c, p90 +0.94c.
- Routing saved money in 14 of 20 seconds at 30 contracts (median saving $0.15) and in 16 of 20 at 88 contracts (median $0.32), with Poly capped at 61 contracts by the ~$60 balance.
- In the pin's own zone (Kalshi ask 0.965-0.98, 11 seconds) the saving was about 0.4-0.5c a contract when Poly was cheaper.
- I checked one second by hand (05:15, tau 45): 61 x (0.95707 - 0.94392) = $0.80. It matches.
- The pin actually traded only 07:00 of these 17 windows. The 05:15 and 05:30 windows, which hold the big savings, were refused by the live bot's own gates (edge_floor / price_ceiling / depth_floor).

3) THE GAPS DO NOT LAST. Poly was at least 0.5c cheaper in 7 seconds. Its price was still there 0.3 s later in 3 of 7, and 1 s later in 2 of 7.

4) THE RECORDER IS NOT THE LAG. Poly trade frames reach us a median 0.046 s after the exchange's own stamp (p99 0.17 s, n=43,432). Round trip for a GET, 12 calls each: Poly 31 ms median on a kept-open connection, 80 ms on a fresh one; Kalshi 70 ms. Live Kalshi order latency is about 90-200 ms. So Poly order speed is probably not the blocker. Poly ORDER latency itself is still unmeasured.

5) HOW OFTEN THE PIN TRADES BTC, AND THE HEDGES. 59 BTC markets settled 09-18..09-24 = 8.4 a day, +$23.90 net over 61 markets 09-18..09-25 (one loss). On 09-25 only 2 by 14:00Z. Live BTC hedges: 4 events in 17 days (0.24 a day). Each is 60-176 contracts at 58-87c ($35-150), mostly more than the $60 Poly balance can pay for. The earlier lag_hedge.py found the hedge saving is 0.0c median one second after a jump.

6) CAPITAL. Per results/POLYMARKET_ORDERS.md, the operator's own Poly win was paid 82 minutes after the close. So $60 on Poly funds at most one routed entry about every 85 minutes. Of the $60.52, $50 is a promotional bonus and $10 was still pending. polyorder.py currently caps an order at 5 contracts / $5, which makes routing worth about $0.05 per entry until that cap is raised.

7) BONUS FOR THE POLY-PIN TEST (U1). Across 20 Poly windows, Poly's leading side was offered at or below 98c in 39 of 859 leader-seconds (4.5%; U1's pre-registered bar is 15% or more), in only 3 windows. In those windows Kalshi's ask for the same side was also about 0.975-0.98. Other traders took that supply: 19 taker buys, 1,311 shares, in the last 45 s of 05:15.

8) RECORDER BUG ("identify better"). scan_poly_ws.py (pid 2855732) received only 21 of about 43 15-minute windows since 03:16Z, and nothing at all from 09:30 to 11:45Z. The feed rejected its subscribe requests 54 times with "slug already subscribed" (the whole request) and 14 times with "max subscriptions per connection reached"; the recorder never unsubscribes finished windows. chk.worst_case:
$900 bank: about -$60 on top of today's risk, which is the whole Poly balance. The case: a Poly order reply is lost or unknown, the bot does not know it holds 61 contracts on Poly, and that window loses with that leg unhedged. The mirror case: the bot over-hedges on Kalshi, about 61 contracts x 60-80c = $37-49 at risk.

Rarer: a Poly entry hedged on Kalshi when the two venues settle differently would lose both legs. That happened in 1 of 223 windows (the 09-22 15:15Z launch window, decided by a 29-cent margin).

A Poly outage mid-entry just falls back to Kalshi at a slightly moved price, a few cents on 30-88 contracts. The feed dropped 3 times between 11:51 and 12:01Z.

$5k bank: the same failure scales to the Poly allocation, about $400-500.

Code risk in the hedge path is the bigger and less countable risk. The only losing day so far (09-19, -$106.73) came from new gates blocking hedges.
chk.killer_risks:
1) Whole-cent ticks. At the pin's usual BTC price (Kalshi 0.97-0.98), Poly is usually at 0.98-0.99. A saving needs a full cent lower, and those gaps are short-lived: of 7 seconds at least 0.5c cheaper, 3 survived 0.3 s and 2 survived 1 s.
2) The savings concentrate in windows the pin does not trade. In both-book windows the pin traded 1 of 17, saving $0.001, while the big per-second savings sat in the windows it refused (05:15 and 05:30).
3) Money. $60 on Poly and an 82-minute payout make it one routed entry per ~85 min at most, with Poly usable only up to 61 contracts. $50 of the $60 is a bonus with unknown terms. polyorder caps an order at 5 contracts. Hedges cannot be funded on Poly at all.
4) Live-path complexity. A second venue in pinrun means position truth across two books, lost-reply handling (Poly has no idempotency key), and hedges sized on combined holdings. That is the bug class that caused the 09-19 losing day, and one such bug (-$60) wipes out about 2-3 months of the expected saving.
5) Sample. One real entry overlaps the recording, the both-book comparison covers 3 windows, and the recorder bug means the planned 3-day read will hold about half the windows.
6) Small risk that the two venues settle a window differently (1 of 223 so far).

ref.strongest_objection:
The money is not there once you simulate an actual router instead of comparing prices second by second. When the pin really buys BTC, Kalshi prices in tenths of a cent and Polymarket only in whole cents. So Poly is at best one tick cheaper, which is worth 0.1-0.4c a contract.

(1) THE ONE REAL ENTRY. Across the live bot and all 136 paper-arm logs, only one BTC buy falls inside the Poly real-time recording: the 07:00Z close. The router would have saved $0.026 against Kalshi's book, or $0.054 against the pin's actual 0.972 fill.

The checker got $0.001 because it looked 0.5 s after the whole-second log stamp. By then Poly had moved from 0.97 to 0.98. At the true send instant Poly was at 0.97, and that price lasted only 0.37 s after the send.

(2) A ROUTER THAT DECIDES ON WHAT IT SEES. I rebuilt Kalshi's book myself. Only 3 of the 19 windows with both books ever had the leading side at 90-98c with at least 29 contracts in the last 45 s. In each I simulated the router: it decides at t0 from both books, the Poly order lands at t0+D, and the result is compared with today's Kalshi order landing at t0+0.10 s.
- 29 contracts: total gain -$0.25 at D=0.1 s and +$0.03 at D=0.2-0.3 s. Seen at decision time, the same trades looked like +$0.35.
- 88 contracts, with Poly capped at $60: -$0.50 or +$0.06, against +$0.73 at decision time.

Why: Kalshi makers re-quote their whole ladder in under 100 ms. At 05:15 the Kalshi NO ask fell from 0.959 to 0.935 within 0.1 s while Poly sat at 0.95. A router would have paid $0.13-0.41 more than today's fill.

The checker's figure (60% of entries x $0.15-0.30) came from per-second gaps, mostly in 05:15 and 05:30. The pin refused both windows.

(3) NO WAY TO GET MORE DATA FROM THE PAST. Polymarket's public price history is the ~30 s cache, not a per-second record. It has a median of 4 points per 2-minute window and matches the real-time book only 56-60% of the time. The 23 BTC entries from 09-22 to 09-24 cannot be checked, so every number rests on 09-25's recording.

(4) BTC ENTRIES HAVE DROPPED. 7-8 closes a day from 09-22 to 09-24, but only 1 on 09-25 by 14:09Z.

(5) THE CHECKER'S OWN PASS BAR IS OUT OF REACH. It asks for $0.20 saved per entry. At 29 contracts that needs about 0.7c a contract, which is above the checker's own p90 gap of 0.94c less fees and well above its median of 0.38c.

Meanwhile it adds a second venue to the live path. Polymarket orders are unbuilt (polyorder caps an order at 5 contracts / $5, and the key's ability to trade is unproven), and every Polymarket order needs per-order sign-off. $50 of the $60 is non-withdrawable bonus credit that Polymarket can reverse. Settlement pays 7-82 minutes after the close. One lost-reply or over-hedge bug costs up to $60, which is years of the saving.

idea.name: Top-of-hour corridor: 1-hour window vs the xx:45 15-min window on the same print (all-Poly, or Poly + Kalshi)
idea.family: cross-venue / single-venue riskless package on one settlement print
idea.mechanism: The 15-min window opening at xx:45 (strike K15) and the 1-hour window opening at xx:00 (strike K1h) settle on the same BRTI 60-s average at the next hour. Buy Up on whichever has the lower strike and Down on the higher one: pays $1 whatever happens and $2 if the settle lands between the strikes. Near the close one leg is the winner and the other dead; when the winner is offered at <= 98c and the dead leg at 1c, the pair costs 99c + ~0.2c fees for a guaranteed $1. Take the 1c leg first, then the winner; hold; Poly settles in ~1 minute. Variant: Poly 1h leg + Kalshi xx:45 15-min leg. Natural use for the non-withdrawable promo credit (I14), and it turns some Poly-pin hits (I10) into no-loss trades.
idea.why_mispriced: Poly's whole-cent tick and two thin books priced by different crowds: the market maker leaves the winner at 98c for tens of seconds at the end (tau 2-35 s) and holders dump the dead leg of the other window at 1c.
idea.must_be_true: Display asks are executable and the 1c dead-leg ask has real size; Poly's 1h price-to-beat equals the hour-open 60-s average (verify as K15 was verified 16/16). The 8 other hours with sub-$1 sums (e.g. 0.08+0.17 at 33 s) are almost surely display glitches, so only the winner <= 98c + dead = 1c pattern is counted. The recorder currently never records the xx:30/xx:45 15m windows (resubscribe bug) -- exactly one leg of this trade.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Riskless but small: ~4 hits/day (8 of 45 hours) x up to 60 packages x ~1.7c = up to ~$4/day at the $60 bank; realistic $0-3/day; Poly-Kalshi variant < $1/day. Grows with Poly capital.
idea.data_needed: Fix the recorder's resubscribe bug, record 3 days, count hits with real sizes, then a 1-package test.
idea.evidence_so_far: poly_corridor.py (self-tested) and corridor2.py on the public per-second display history: 64 top-of-hour closes since launch, 45 with a complete index tape, 8 of 45 showed the pattern for >= 2 consecutive seconds; best edge per package 0.79-6.42c, median 1.73c; 6 of 8 inside the last 45 s. Poly-Kalshi variant on the rebuilt Kalshi book: 3 seconds in the 03:00Z window (453-455 s before close) where Poly Up + Kalshi 15-min Down cost < $1 (edge 0.16-3.26c, ~450-500 size); rung checks against the stale batch-quoted KXBTCD ladder produced more, all unconfirmed. chk.measured:
WHY IT DIES: the "winner at 98c" in the display history is not something anyone was selling. Near the close, Polymarket's real book never offers a near-certain winner at 98c. Without that leg, the no-lose package does not exist.

1) DIRECT CHECK OF THE EVIDENCE. Of the 9 display "hits" since launch (49 top-of-hour closes, re-run with 7 newer closes added), exactly one falls inside the real-time book recording: the 05:00 ET 09-25 close. For 15 seconds the display showed the 1h winner at 0.96-0.97. The real 1h book at those same seconds held a 903-contract BID at 0.96 (later 235 at 0.97) and ZERO offers. So the display was showing the bid; the winner could not be bought at any price. 7 of the 9 display hits have the same shape: the winner leg sits $350-$795 from its strike, which is the case where the real book has no offers. Across 26,218 recorded seconds, the display "long" price equalled the real best offer only 68% of the time.

2) HOW THE REAL BOOK BEHAVES, last 45 s of every recorded window (20 fifteen-minute windows, 11 one-hour windows, 00:00-10:00 ET 09-25):
- A winner was offered at 98c or less only when it sat close to its own strike: $14-$48 away on the 15m (4 of 20 windows), $5-$22 away on the 1h (4 of 11).
- At every larger distance the winner had no offer at 98c or lower, usually no offer at all.
- The dead leg at 1c: on the 15m, almost always (816 of 900 seconds, thousands of contracts). On the 1h, only 3 of 11 windows, all $116-$561 from the strike.

3) WHY THE TWO NEEDS CANNOT MEET. The package needs a cheap winner in one market and a 1c dead leg in the other at the same second.
- If the 15m is the winner, the 1h's distance from its strike is at most the 15m's. A cheap 15m winner means under $48 away, but a 1c 1h dead leg means over $116 away. Both cannot be true.
- If the 1h is the winner, both legs must sit about $14-$22 from their strikes. That needs the two strikes within about $8 of each other (1 of about 50 closes; the gaps are listed in corridor.out) and the settle landing in an $8 band. Rough rate: once a month.

4) POLY 1h + KALSHI xx:45 15m VARIANT, both books real (Kalshi from the ticker channel on the tape, same local clock): 11 closes, 0 seconds where the pair cost under $1 in the last 5 minutes. Cheapest was 102.5c. Kalshi's winner sits at 99.x c and Poly's dead leg cannot go below 1c.

5) RECORDER BUG CONFIRMED. Every re-subscribe after the first is rejected with "slug already subscribed", 16 rejections so far. It has never recorded an xx:45 15m window, so the all-Poly pair was never measured directly on the real book.

Files (scratchpad/sweep/check-I45/): ws_legs.py + ws_legs.out (leg books, trades), display_check.py + display_check.out (display vs real book, all display hits, Poly-Kalshi pair), ws_corridor.py + ws_corridor.out (per-slug frame counts showing the recorder gap), display_cache.json. Collector, crypto_feeds and the Poly recorder are all still running. Free disk is 86 GB.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day: $0/day at both $900 and $5k. Bank size does not matter because the missing piece is supply, not capital. If the only shape that can happen does happen, the upper bound is about once a month, times about 100 packages (the largest 98c winner offer seen on the real 1h book was 614-906 contracts, but only when the dead leg could not be at 1c), times about 0.8-1.7c edge each. That is about $1-2 a month, or $0.03-0.06 a day. Poly + Kalshi variant: 0 hits in 11 closes, so $0 measured. Caveat: 0 of 11 alone only rules out a rate above about 1 in 4 hours. The $0 comes from the book behaviour and the geometry, not from the 11 closes.
chk.worst_case: Leg risk at 60 packages. If the 98c winner fills and the 1c leg does not, he holds an unhedged Poly pin: -$58.80 plus about $0.08 in fees if it loses. If the 1c leg is taken first and the winner offer is gone, the loss is about $0.60 plus fee. Given point 1, "the winner offer is gone" is the normal case, so in practice the bot would mostly just buy dead 1c legs.
chk.killer_risks:
1) The winner leg does not exist: Polymarket's market makers do not offer a near-certain winner below 99c in the last 45 s, and usually offer nothing at all. The display history showed the bid, which caused the fake hits.
2) The geometry: a cheap winner needs the price near that market's strike, while a 1c dead leg in the other market needs the price far from its strike. In the 15m-winner layout these cannot both hold. In the 1h-winner layout they need the strikes within about $8 of each other.
3) Poly's whole-cent floor puts the dead leg at 1c or more, and Kalshi's winner sits at 99.x c, so the cross-venue pair costs about $1.00 or more.
4) Everything rests on one day of real book (31 windows). The rule "a winner is offered at 98c or less only when it is under about $50 from its strike" is measured on that day only.
5) Settlement: Poly agreed with the tape rule on 222 of 223 windows. The one disagreement was $0.29 from the strike. It matters only when both strikes and the settle are within cents of each other, which is not a real risk here.
chk.next_test:
Free, read-only, no money. Fix scan_poly_ws.py so each re-subscribe sends only slugs not already subscribed (or opens a fresh connection each window), so the xx:45 15m window gets recorded. Run 7 days, then re-run ws_corridor.py, which already walks both ladders with fees and has a self-test.
Pass bar, written before looking: on at least 1 top-of-hour close per day, 20 or more packages executable at a total cost of 99.5c or less, including both taker fees, using real offered size on both legs at the same second and lasting at least 1 second. Expected result from this check: fail. The fix is still worth making for I10/I14, because today no Poly 15m window opening at xx:30 or xx:45 is ever recorded.
chk.capital_needed: None worth committing. At most about $60 in the funded Poly account (the promo credit is fine) for 60 packages at about 99c each, held for about 1 minute until settlement.

idea.name: Long-dated crypto vs the options market: sell moonshots/crash tails, buy underpriced middle brackets (optionally options-hedged)
idea.family: cross-asset (Deribit/IBIT/CME options as information) x Kalshi yearly, EOY and one-touch crypto; Kalshi APY on positions
idea.mechanism: Build an implied distribution per expiry from Deribit's public option marks (smile linear in log-moneyness, total variance interpolated in time; digital = -dC/dK; one-touch from the driftless reflection formula at the barrier's smile vol). (a) Buy NO on Kalshi yearly upside touches and EOY tails priced well above it (and on the altcoin moonshots, which are 0-2% even at 1.5x realised vol); (b) buy the fee-free (KXBTCY/KXETHY fee multiplier 0) middle EOY brackets priced below it. Hold to settlement; positions earn 3.25% APY; collateral netting (MECNET events) lowers capital for multi-leg tail sales within one event. Optional hedge: ~2x an IBIT or CME call spread around the barrier as a static one-touch hedge (reflection principle), which turns the ~6c Kalshi-vs-options gap into a mostly-hedged spread (needs an options-approved brokerage account).
idea.why_mispriced: Retail directional bettors pay for lottery-ticket upside ('BTC $200k this year', 'XRP to $7'): the favourite-longshot bias documented on Kalshi (Burgi-Deng-Whelan 2025) and strongest in crypto on Polymarket (arXiv 2609.12878: sub-10c buys lose 19.3c per $). The deep options market prices the same tails far lower; the months-long capital lock and no US access to Deribit keep professional arbitrage away. Retail range bettors also over-weight 'about where it is now'.
idea.must_be_true: The risk-neutral options distribution is at least as good a forecast as Kalshi retail's (vol risk premium favours NO; real-world upward drift works against it); Kalshi's per-minute trimmed-mean touch rule ~ continuous touch; year-end index/time mismatch (CF Benchmarks vs Deribit 08:00 UTC expiry) is small; the gap persists; crypto crashes and melt-ups are correlated so the basket is less diversified than it looks; and CRUCIALLY the capital must be capital pinrun cannot use (pinrun returns ~2-3%/day on its bank vs ~3.5-4% per QUARTER here). For the hedge: IBIT options track Deribit, and the residual basis (touch vs European, 2x-ratio slippage) is well under the gap.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Weak: ~$0.3-1.5/day at $1-4k allocated; at $500 ~$0.3-1/day. Visible capacity at edge >= 2c beyond a +/-5-vol band: model EV $155 on $3,713 capital over ~98 days (4.2%); at >= 2c vs the mid model: EV $887 on $25,357 (3.5%). Hedged version $0.5-2/day at a few $k. Only for overflow capital at a larger bank.
idea.data_needed: Calibration of settled Kalshi long-dated crypto markets vs their prices (2025 EOY/yearly markets, price bands at 60-90 days out); weekly re-run of deribit_vs_kalshi.py to see whether the gap persists; for the hedge, price the IBIT chain (cdn.cboe.com delayed JSON reachable, HTTP 307) and simulate residual P&L.
idea.evidence_so_far: Snapshot 09-25 ~06:40Z (BTC 83,929, ETH 2,670, 13 Deribit expiries, 317 Kalshi markets, 69 orderbook GETs): Kalshi YES bid vs model [+/-5 vol]: BTC >= $100k this year 41c vs 34.5% [28-40]; >= $120k 15c vs 8.4% [5.2-11.8]; >= $150k 3c vs 1.7%; >= $200k 2c vs 0.3%; ETH >= $4,750 12c vs 5.1%; >= $6,000 5-6c vs 1.3%; ETH <= $750 6c vs 1.7%; BTC downside (MINY) and monthlies near fair; EOY BTC > $150k 3c vs 0.5%; ETH $2,000-2,500 brackets ask 9.4-12c vs 12.0-15.2%. Realised 30-day vol from our tape: BTC 35%, ETH 46%, SOL 56%, XRP 68%, DOGE 69%; XRP touch $7 by Dec 31 9-13c vs 0.0% (0.2% at 1.5x vol); DOGE $1 by Jun 2027 8-9c vs 0.0% (0.2%); SOL > $300 Jan 1 6-10c vs 0.0% (0.8%); BTC below $40k 6-7c vs 0.0% (0.9%). 11 series carry fee multiplier 0 (KXBTCY 96k contracts/day, 9.87M OI). chk.measured:
What kills it: the price gap to the options market is real, but nothing shows the options market predicts better than Kalshi, and the return is tiny compared with pinrun.

(1) KALSHI'S OWN SETTLED CRYPTO TOUCH MARKETS. This uses no replay. Inputs are Kalshi's daily closing quotes and the actual results: 657 markets across 87 events, 770 candlestick GETs. Covered: monthly MAX/MIN for BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE, Jan-Sep 2026, plus the 2024 and 2025 yearly BTC/ETH/XRP markets and KXBTCMAX150/100. Entry is taken on a fixed grid of days before the scheduled end, as if we bought NO at 1 minus the YES bid and paid the taker fee.
- Monthlies, cheap longshots priced 1-5c: they came true MORE often than priced. Upside touches hit 6.3% of the time against an average 2.1c price (237 observations, 40 events, 8 months), so buying NO lost 4.35c per contract (standard error 6.1c by month). Downside: hit 4.3% against 2.1c, NO lost 2.33c. The longshot bias this idea depends on does not appear in Kalshi's crypto touch markets.
- Yearly markets, 98 days out: at 1-5c, 0 of 20 hit, NO made +2.14c. At 5-10c, 2 of 13 hit, NO lost 9.06c. Both hits were BTC reaching $100k in Dec 2024, a single melt-up. That is effectively two independent years.
- Bug found and fixed along the way: events still open (the Sep-30 monthlies, the 2026 yearlies) had only their already-touched markets settled. My first pass measured days from the touch date, which inflated hit rates. Those events are now excluded (calib.py, NOW cutoff).

(2) REAL-WORLD HISTORY FROM COINBASE DAILY PRICES, 2016-2026. Question: in any 98-day window, did the daily high or low reach the strike, measured as a multiple of today's price? Overlapping windows, so only about 39 independent windows over 2016-26 and about 17 over 2022-26.
- BTC at least $120k (1.43x today): happened 38% (2016-26), 33% (2019-26), 21.8% (2022-26). Kalshi bid is 15c; the options model says 8.4%. History says buying NO here LOSES.
- BTC at least $100k: 43-60% historically, against Kalshi 41c and model 34.5%.
- BTC at least $200k (2.38x): 9.5% / 6.2% / 0%, against Kalshi 2c and model 0.3%.
- ETH at least $6,000 (2.25x): 14.6% / 9.4% / 1.0%, against 5-6c.
- ETH at or below $750: 3.3% / 0.6% / 1.0%, against 6c.
- BTC below $40k: 7.2% / 4.3% / 3.3%, against 6-7c.
Only the extreme tails favour NO, and only if you believe the 2022-26 period over the full record.

(3) FEE-FREE YEAR-END BRACKETS (live book pulled 09-25). Compared with the options model, Kalshi's middle brackets are 1-3c cheap. Compared with history they are 3-6c too expensive. Example, BTC ending $80-85k: Kalshi 12.1c ask, options model 13.2%, history 6.0-7.6%. ETH $2,250-2,500: 11.9c ask, options model 15.2%, history 8.9-11.2%. The two references disagree about which way the edge points. Ask depth within 1c: about $1.95k in total across BTC's 65-105k brackets and about $660 across ETH's middle ones.

(4) SUPPLY AT THE ATTRACTIVE PRICES IS THIN. BTC $120k: 140 contracts at 15c and 111 at 14c. ETH $4,750: 200 at 12c. ETH $6,000: 4 at 6c and 967 at 5c. BTC $200k: 4,727 at 2c. BTC year-end above $150k: about 370 contracts at 2.8-3c.

(5) KALSHI'S 3.25% INTEREST is paid on the whole account value, cash and positions alike (help.kalshi.com, APY on Kalshi). Locking money in positions earns no extra interest.

(6) HEDGED VERSION: the whole gap on BTC $120k at visible size is 140 contracts times 6.6c, about $9. The IBIT call-spread hedge would cost about $30 or more in bid/ask plus commissions for the 3-lot size needed. Dead on cost.

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
At the $900 bank: $0/day. Doing it costs money. pinrun made +$437.82 over about 17.5 days, roughly $25/day on about $900-1,043, which is about 2.5% of the bank per day. Its size scales with the bank (auto-size 88 at $1,043). This idea's best case is about 2-4% per 98 days, roughly 0.03% per day, about 80 times less per dollar. Moving $300 here earns about $0.05-0.10/day by the options model, and it could cost pinrun up to about $7/day if pinrun is limited by bank rather than by available offers.

At a $5k bank, only for cash pinrun genuinely cannot use: the far-tail-only basket is the one part not flatly contradicted by history.
- BTC $200k NO: about 2,000 contracts at 98c, about $1,960, model edge about 1.5c after the 0.14c fee, about $30 per 98 days.
- ETH $6,000 NO: about 967 contracts at 95c, about $920, edge about 3.5c, about $34.
- Total: about $64 of options-model expected value per 98 days on about $2.9k, about $0.65/day.
- By the 2016-26 or 2019-26 history that same basket loses money, because break-even requires a 2.3x+ quarter less than about 2 times in 100. It happened in 6-10 of 100 windows.
- Full visible capacity (about $7-8k) is about $1.3-1.5/day of model value and needs more than the $5k bank.
Realistic after fees and model risk: somewhere between -$1 and +$1 per day.
chk.worst_case:
A melt-up quarter takes the whole basket at once, because every leg is 'crypto goes up a lot'. BTC went 2.7x from Sep to Dec 2020; ETH went 2.1x.
- Far-tail basket at $2.9k: lose about $2.9k, roughly 45 quarters of the expected gain.
- Full idea basket including BTC $120k and ETH $4,750: the Q4 2024 analog (BTC +71% from 09-25 to 12-17-2024) would have taken the 1.43x and 1.78x legs. Loss about $3.7k at full band capacity per the idea's own figure.
- At $900 with $300 in it: lose about $300, about 12 days of pinrun profit.
chk.killer_risks:
1) There is no evidence the options model beats Kalshi on real outcomes.
- Kalshi's own crypto longshots at 1-5c came true 2-3 times more often than priced (monthlies, 8 months).
- 98-day history says 1.2-1.5x upside moves happen 22-38% of the time, where the model says 8-17% and Kalshi prices 15-41c.
- The options market is a risk-neutral price. It leaves out BTC's historical upward drift and the momentum of its big rallies.

2) The edge cannot be verified in reasonable time. Each quarter is about one independent observation. A 2c edge with a per-quarter standard error of 6-9c would take 50+ quarters to confirm.

3) Opportunity cost: about 0.03% per day here against about 2.5% per day in pinrun.

4) Every leg loses together in a melt-up.

5) Supply at the good prices is a few hundred contracts per market.

6) The hedged version: the hedge costs about 3 times the gap at this size and needs an options-approved brokerage account.

7) The 3.25% interest is not an advantage; cash earns it anyway.

What could make the good snapshot an artefact: Deribit's far-wing marks are extrapolated beyond listed strikes (a smile that is linear in log-moneyness underprices wings), and the one-touch formula ignores spot-vol correlation in rallies. Both push the model's upside-touch numbers too low. That fits history showing far more 1.4x touches than the model.
chk.next_test:
No money test is worth running. The only cheap step is a zero-cost paper logger, which is optional.
- Once a week, snapshot every Kalshi crypto touch and year-end market price next to the options model (re-run anything-anywhere/deribit_vs_kalshi.py). Score every settled market against its snapshot price, clustered by coin-month.
- Pass bar before any money: at least 24 month-clusters in which the far-tail NO (YES bid 5c or less, a move of 2x or more needed) earns at least +1.5c per contract after fees, and the model-says-cheap side beats the market price, with the lower 95% bound above 0.
- Only revisit if the bank passes about $5k AND pinrun's logs show idle cash it could not deploy. Cap at $500 in far tails only.
- Expect this to take about 2 years to decide.
chk.capital_needed: Uneconomic at $900; needs $0 from the bank. At most $500-3k of cash pinrun cannot use, and only at a bank of $5k or more. Locked about 98 days. Full visible capacity is about $7-8k.

All calls were read-only GETs (about 53), made 2026-09-25 around 14:00-14:20Z. Scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/check-I47/ (measure.py/.out/.json, eligfrac.py/.out/.json, payout.py/.out).

(1) Programs that exist right now. There are 0 volume programs anywhere on Kalshi: 0 active, 0 upcoming, 0 closed-but-unpaid. All 6,285 active and 598 upcoming programs are liquidity programs, which pay for resting orders, not for trades. On the series we trade, the only programs are liquidity programs on KXCRYPTOLEAD15M (5 active, 275 upcoming, $20 per 15-minute market). Those belong to the separate Coin Race liquidity-program idea (IDEAS #11), not this one. Kalshi's history (crypto-other/incent_volume_paid.json) shows volume programs on only two of our series, KXBTC15M and KXETH15M, from 2026-02-16 to 2026-05-12, paying $10-20 per market. The last volume program on any series was KXMLBSEASONGAMES on 2026-09-15.

(2) The rules, from the Kalshi help center. A volume program pays pro rata by volume, only on trades priced 3-97c, and never more than $0.005 per contract.

(3) Our own fills, last 7 days, from /portfolio/fills: 1,693 fills, 25,045 contracts, 100% of them taking an existing offer. Only 8,527 contracts (34%) were priced 3-97c. 66% were above 97c and would earn nothing under any program. That is 1,218 eligible contracts a day across 11 series, about 45-89 per market we touch.

(4) Market volume, median per market over the last 24h (96 settled markets per series): BTC 2,789,348 contracts; ETH 117,936; XRP 78,203; SOL 47,258; DOGE 34,929; HYPE 20,988; ZEC 17,746; NEAR 16,706; BNB 12,222; Coin Race 284. Trade totals matched volume_fp exactly, so the paging was complete.

(5) What a program would pay us, per-market pro rata with the 0.5c cap:
- Absolute ceiling: 1,218 x $0.005 = $6.09/day. That needs a large pool on every series at once. The cap only binds when a market's pool reaches $35 (BNB), $36 (HYPE), $42 (NEAR), $67 (ZEC), $88 (DOGE), $103 (SOL), $197 (XRP), $297 (ETH) or $7,015 (BTC).

- The historical program coming back unchanged (BTC and ETH only, $20 per market): BTC pays $0.0006 per market (88 of 2.79M contracts) and ETH about $0.013. Together that is about $0.03/day.

(6) Polymarket taker rebate, from web sources only, not measured. Bronze tier gives 3% of taker fees back after $2,000 of 30-day weighted volume. At 97c our taker fee is 0.20c per contract, so 3% back is 0.006c per contract, which is negligible. Whether it applies to Polymarket US crypto contracts is not confirmed.

Artefact check. A good number would be fake if the market's eligible share were far below total volume, because that would shrink the denominator. I measured it: 50%, so the denominator is not inflated. There was no good number to explain away. Both recorders were alive afterwards (2 processes, 23 MB and 43 MB), and free disk is 86 GB.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
Now, at either bank size: $0/day, because no volume program exists on Kalshi.

$900 bank, if programs come back:
- The only kind Kalshi has ever run on our series (BTC and ETH, $20 per market): about $0.03/day. For BTC that is 89 eligible contracts / 2.79M market contracts x $20 = $0.0006 per market x 17 eligible markets a week.

ref.strongest_objection:
Under the Polymarket limits written into research/polyorder.py, a new coin listing adds $0.00 a day. The limits are $10 of money put at risk per day across ALL Polymarket orders (DAY_MAX_RISK), 5 contracts per order and a 98c maximum price. That buys about 10 contracts a day. The whole Polymarket account can therefore make at most about 10 x (2-3c minus a ~0.2c fee), which is $0.19-0.28 a day, whatever it trades. Bitcoin alone already offers enough deals to use up that $10: 8 of the 31 recorded BTC windows had the likely winner for sale at 98c or less (see checks). The checker's ceiling of "about $0.5-1 a day under those limits" leaves out the $10-a-day cap and is 2-5x too high. There is also less real money on Polymarket than the ~$60 suggests: of the $60.52 buying power, $50 is a held promotional bonus, $10 is a pending deposit and $0.52 can be withdrawn (results/POLYMARKET_ORDERS.md).

So I48 has no value of its own. It is a free trigger that pays only if three things all happen: (1) Polymarket US lists another coin on a CF Benchmarks USD index, (2) the Bitcoin test on Polymarket (U1) turns out profitable, and (3) the operator raises the limits and deposits real money. This does not refute the checker's verdict. The watcher costs nothing and cannot lose money. It does refute the checker's conditional dollar figure.

Two corrections the checker and U1 need:

(a) The "99c wall" is only half of it. In every window already decided by 5 bps (0.05%) or more, nobody sold the winner at 98c or less; usually nobody sold it at all. But in close windows, the ones that settled within 0.6-2.6 bps of the start price, the winner WAS offered at 85-98c in depth: hundreds to about 3,500 shares. That happened while a simple model was at least 99% sure. Example: the 1-hour window closing 1:00 AM ET had Up bid 10-15c with 45 s left; 579 shares of Down were available at 97c 2 s before close; Down won. This is where any Polymarket money is. It is also exactly where the bot's losses come from, and a tape cannot show how often we would lose.

(b) Recorder bug, which weakens the evidence for U1 and therefore for I48. scan_poly_ws.py sends [current window, next window, current 1-hour window] as one subscribe request. Polymarket rejects the WHOLE request when any slug in it is already subscribed ("slug already subscribed"). So after startup it only picks up windows at :00 and :15 past the hour. Measured from 11:15 PM ET 09-24 to 10:15 AM ET 09-25:
- 22 of the 37 listed 15-minute windows were recorded; the other 15 have no frames at all.
- 58 "already subscribed" error frames, plus 14 "max subscriptions per connection reached".
The 09-28 read of the recorder (OPEN_WORK A11) will have about 60 of every 100 windows it is assumed to have. Separately, Polymarket listed no 15-minute windows from 6:00 to 7:59 AM ET on 09-25; the 1-hour windows still ran.

idea.name: Kalshi APY on cash and positions (check it is being paid)
idea.family: capital efficiency
idea.mechanism: Kalshi accrues a variable 3.25% APY daily on net portfolio value at 12 AM ET (cash + positions at last traded price), paid monthly, for balances >= $250 (SSN on file if interest > $10/yr). Automatic; the only action is to confirm the monthly credit appears in the ledger (pinxfer/kalshi_ledger) and to keep the balance >= $250 at midnight ET. It also sets a floor yield for any long-dated hold (I36, I46).

chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
At a $900 bank: 900 x 0.0325 / 365 = $0.080/day, about $29/yr. At a $5k bank: 5000 x 0.0325 / 365 = $0.445/day, about $162/yr. At today's $1,054: $0.094/day.
- It is taxed as ordinary interest, and a 1099-INT is issued at $10 or more a year, which happens at any bank above about $310.
- It costs nothing and needs nothing new: the bot holds 15-minute positions, so the midnight value is almost all cash and already counts.
- INCREMENTAL value over what already happens: $0/day. The account qualified automatically from 2026-09-14.
chk.worst_case:
$0. Ways to get nothing:
- Kalshi cuts the rate (it is variable).
- The balance is below $250 at 12 AM ET after a drawdown or withdrawal.
- The SSN is not on file. That caps interest at $10 a year and cannot be seen through the API.

There is no way to lose money on this.

One bookkeeping side-effect: the first credit (~$1.23) is above pinrun's EXTERNAL_MIN of $1.00. If it lands between two bank polls, pinrun.classify_bank_move will book it as a ~$1.23 'deposit' and shift the high-water mark up by $1.23. That direction is harmless.

At $5k (~$13.5 a month) this happens every month. pinxfer/taxledger reconciliation will then show a +$1.2 (later +$13.5) residual that /portfolio/deposits cannot explain. It should be labelled interest, not treated as a mystery or a trading gain.
chk.killer_risks:
Not a killer, but it adds no new money. It is already happening. Nothing here lets the bot make or save more than it does now.

Open items:
- SSN on file is unverified. If it is missing, the October credit will be capped or absent.
- The '$250' test is ambiguous (per day or per month). The difference is $0.08 for September.

A correction to the idea card's 'floor yield for long-dated holds' framing. Open positions earn the SAME 3.25% as cash, valued at last traded price. So interest is NOT an opportunity cost of locking money in a long-dated Kalshi contract. I36 and I46 should not subtract it; they should compare against cash earning 3.25% either way. The one catch: an illiquid position with a stale low last trade earns on that lower value.

Could the $0.03 gap be an artefact hiding a credit? Only if an interest credit and an unrecorded loss of the same size cancelled out. The settlement ledger reproduces the balance to 3 cents across 1,127 markets and 7 deposits, so that is very unlikely.

ref.strongest_objection:
The facts are right, but this is not a way to make more money. The interest has been building up automatically since 2026-09-14, so doing I49 adds $0 a day. Two things are still unproven:
- No payment has ever arrived. My own check finds $0.04 of unexplained money against a $1,058 balance.
- The 3.25% rate comes from one Kalshi help page last updated 2026-03-17, and the rate can change.

The one thing that could change the payout is whether a Social Security number is on file, and that turns out not to matter until 2027:
- Kalshi's SSN article (updated 2026-08-25) says an SSN is NOT needed to deposit, trade or withdraw. So it may well be missing.
- Without one, interest is capped at $10 a year.
- The payments due in 2026 are for Sept, Oct and Nov: about $1.23 + $2.92 + $2.83 = $6.98. That is under the cap.
- From 2027 the cap costs about $24 a year at today's bank, and about $152 a year at $5,000.
