idea.name: Stale derived ladder: NFL wins-by-week priced exactly from game moneylines
idea.family: sports / derivative-vs-underlying consistency (the measured form of unchecked I61)
markets: KXNFLWINSWEEK-26W4 (and W8, W12, KXNFLWINS when their remaining games are all listed)
idea.mechanism: 'Team X wins at least k of its first 4 games' is an exact function of wins so far (from settled KXNFLGAME markets) plus the win chances of its remaining listed games, read from the 1c-wide game books and treated as independent. Every few minutes the bot recomputes each rung's fair value. It takes any ladder quote that sits beyond fair value by more than the taker fee plus 1c, holds to settlement, caps size per team (rungs of the same team move together), and skips a rung if any of its games is in progress.
idea.why_mispriced: The 4-week ladder is quoted by a coarse maker: 600-lot quotes about 10c wide, median mid within 0.1c of fair, but single rungs far off. KXNFLWINSWEEK-26W4-CHI3 was bid 31c x 603 when Chicago (1-1, needs both of PHI@CHI at 31.5% and NYJ@CHI at 63%) is worth 19.9c. A taker even bought it at 40c on 09-24. JAC2 was offered at 49c when fair is 76.7c. The maker appears to use a team-strength prior rather than the game books, and ladder flow is too thin for anyone to police it (JAC2: 13 trades ever; CHI3: 40).
idea.must_be_true: (1) The game books are the right fair value (they sit on the sharp line per I59). (2) Outcomes are independent across a team's different games. (3) The ladder counts only games in the stated weeks; an NFL tie counts as not-a-win while the game market pays 50c (about 0.3% of games). (4) The stale quotes are still there when we hit them. Artefact risk: the rung counts are from ONE snapshot at about 17:00Z 09-25, and a data bug in the team or week mapping would look exactly like a stale quote. I hand-checked CHI, JAC, IND, PHI, WAS against their 09-13 and 09-20 results.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Measured snapshot (W4 only): 7 rungs past fee+1c, $144 of expected value at top-of-book size. Taking all of it risks about $2k, so at $900 cap it near 100 contracts a rung: about $25-40 per cycle. Exact pricing is possible only when every game in the horizon is listed (W4 now, W8 late Oct, W12 late Nov, season early Jan), so this averages about $1-4/day at $900 and $5-10/day at $5k during the NFL season, lumpy. It is on exchange_index 0, which pinrun does not trade from.
idea.data_needed: Re-snapshot the W4 ladder against the game books after Sunday's games (09-27/28), before W4 settles on 10-04/05. These figures depend on two measured points: one book snapshot and one 3.6-day hourly history. They are not an observed yearly rate.

Mistakes like the Cleveland and Jacksonville ones would have locked about $160-180 each if the dealer's usual 600 contracts were on offer, but that size is UNMEASURED.

Prices can only be computed exactly while every game in a ladder's horizon is listed. Kalshi lists games about 12 days ahead, so that means roughly 4 windows a season: week 4 (now to 10-05), week 8 (about 10-20 to 10-26), week 12 (about 11-17 to 11-23), and the full season (about 12-29 to 01-03).

$900 bank: the current set alone needs $1,100 and the bank is shared with pinrun. With $300-500 set aside, about $20-35 per window, so about $80-140 a season: roughly $1-2/day during the 4-month season and about $0.3/day over a year. Putting all $900 in gives about $57 for this window, but starves pinrun for up to 10 days.

$5k bank: take all measured supply, $70 per window, up to about $370 if the mistakes carry 600-contract size. That is about $280-1,500 a season: roughly $2-12/day in season and $1-4/day over a year. Adding quoting at fair±3c would add at most about $9/day while a ladder is open (upper bound, see measured point 7).

Fees are inside every number: the ladder's taker fee of 0.07×p×(1-p), plus the game-market fee and half its buy/sell gap on every hedge contract.
chk.worst_case:
Unhedged, all 7 markets at the displayed size: worst -$2,117 (about 1 time in 1,250: Chicago wins both games, Washington beats Indianapolis, and so on). 1-in-20 result -$1,507. Loses 40 times out of 100.

Unhedged, scaled to $900: worst -$923, 1-in-20 result -$657. That is two-thirds of the bank on one Monday night, so the unhedged version is not acceptable at this bank.

Hedged set (Chicago 3+ and Philadelphia 3+, about $1,100 of capital): the realistic worst is the week-4 game price jumping about 15c on an injury before the second hedge, or the first hedge not filling before kickoff, costing about $50-90. A tie pays the game hedge 50c while the ladder counts no win; it happens about 3 times in 1,000 games and costs under $1 in expectation. The 4-week ladder's rules have no clause for a postponed game (the 8- and 12-week rules do), so a postponement could leave a hedge unmatched. That risk is unpriced.
chk.killer_risks:
1) SIZE: the dollars are small and capital-heavy. Each dollar locked needs about $15 of collateral held for days, and pinrun needs the same bank. At $900 it cannot pay more than about $1-2/day even in season.

2) UNKNOWN RECURRENCE: the history holds prices but not size. So whether the big mistakes (Cleveland at 36c, Jacksonville 3+ at 57c) had real size, or were a few contracts, is unmeasured. The 8-week, 12-week and season windows are unmeasured too.

3) The dealer may fix its model, or simply pull a quote after the first time it is hit. The whole supply is basically one dealer's 600-contract quotes.

4) Unhedged, it is a correlated game bet with a 40-in-100 chance of losing. It only makes sense with the game-market hedge, which doubles the order count and adds execution risk around kickoff.

5) The 4-week rules have no clause for a postponed game.

6) This is a different market group from pinrun and needs new order and hedging code. Every order needs per-order sign-off under the current rules, which is impractical for a two-legged hedge unless the operator widens the sign-off.

7) Most hedged edges are only 1-5c a contract, inside the error of the hedge-cost estimate. Only Chicago 3+ (7.6c) and Jacksonville 2+ (23c, 10 contracts) are clearly positive.

idea.prior_reason: critic round
idea.name: Two books, two thermometers: ForecastEx NO plus Kalshi YES on the same city's high
idea.family: cross-venue / settlement-source asymmetry (weather)
markets: ForecastEx UHLAX, UHSFO, UHMIA, UHMDW, UHAUS (and about 5 more shared stations)
Kalshi KXHIGHLAX, KXHIGHTSFO, KXHIGHMIA, KXHIGHCHI, KXHIGHAUS
idea.mechanism: ForecastEx 'high exceeds K' pays if the MAXIMUM HOURLY reading is above K. Kalshi's brackets pay on the NWS climate-report high, which is always at least the hourly maximum (0 exceptions in 402 non-NYC station-days). So buying ForecastEx NO at K together with Kalshi YES on every bracket starting exactly at K+1 pays at least $1 in every outcome. It pays $2 when the hourly max is at or below K but the report comes in above it, which happened on 57-76% of days at the sampled stations. The bot watches both books, and whenever the pair costs under $1 after fees buys both (ForecastEx through the IBKR API), then holds to settlement the next morning.
idea.why_mispriced: Two separate crowds price two different numbers for 'the same' high, and most traders do not know ForecastEx settles on hourly readings while Kalshi settles on the climate report. Occasionally one side prices K as if the other venue's number applied.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Climate-report high >= hourly maximum on the same day (0 of 402 exceptions outside NYC; NYC fails and is excluded anyway because the stations differ). (2) Day boundaries: ForecastEx uses local daylight midnight to midnight, Kalshi local standard time (01:00-01:00 daylight). A new maximum set between 00:00 and 01:00 daylight time could break the package; this is rare for highs but not measured. (3) Only strikes where K+1 equals a Kalshi bracket's lower bound are clean (Kalshi brackets are 2 °F wide). (4) The ForecastEx fee is about $0.01 a contract and he can open an IBKR ForecastTrader account. Artefact risk: the evidence uses ForecastEx prints (someone else's fills) and Kalshi 1-minute candle asks carried forward up to a minute, so the depth we would actually get is unmeasured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Measured lower bound (package paying $1, ignoring the $2 upside): $136 across 10 city-days (5 cities x 09-23/24) from 117 of 4,447 matched prints, all traders combined. About 10 stations are shared, so about $130/day of qualifying flow for everyone. Our share is unknown. Realistic about $5-25/day at $900 (capital about $300-600 split across IBKR and Kalshi index 0, returned the next morning), about $15-50/day at $5k. It costs pinrun nothing if read_bank is limited to index 2.
idea.data_needed: 14 days of ForecastEx pairs (free download) joined to Kalshi 1-minute candles for the 10 shared stations. Pass: at least $40/day of qualifying package-positive flow at a cost of $0.97 or less. Then confirm the ForecastEx fee, IBKR eligibility in his state, Kalshi ask depth at those minutes, and the frequency of midnight-hour maxima. Scripts: critic/fx_pkg.py, fx_vs_kalshi.py, fx_lock.py, tgroup_cli.py.
idea.evidence_so_far: fx_lock.py: ForecastEx settlement = hourly METAR T-group max > K on 359 of 359 contracts (09-21..09-24, 15 cities). tgroup_cli.py: climate-report high below the hourly max 0 of 402 station-days at MIA, DEN, AUS, LAX, PHL, MDW, 07-20..09-24 (NYC 1 of 67). The climate-report high exceeded the hourly max on 38-51 of 67 days per station. fx_pkg.py: 117 positive packages, $136.20 lower bound, 0 outcomes paying under $1 in the settled cases checked (e.g., SFO 09-23 K=76: ForecastEx YES; climate report 78, so the Kalshi leg paid).
idea.novelty_vs_killed: D22 killed ForecastEx on a false premise, and D12 (Kalshi-Gemini) failed because two different indices can settle opposite ways. Here the two sources are ordered: one is always at least the other, which is what makes the package pay at least $1. It is not the dead evening/lock trade either: I measured that ForecastEx and Kalshi both price the hourly lock at 98-99c.
idea.worst_case: A day-boundary maximum (00:00-01:00 daylight time), a climate-report correction below the hourly max, or a Weather Underground display change leaves both legs losing on that package, up to its full cost of about $1 a pair. Or both venues stop disagreeing once someone runs this, and it earns $0.

chk.measured:
What decides it: the two-thermometer package is real and safe. It never paid under $1 on 38,893 settled prints. The people who traded it together cleared about $77/day of guaranteed edge across 10 stations. What stays unmeasured is how much of that flow WE would get: the ForecastEx order book is not public, and every price below is someone else's fill.

1) SAFETY, on Kalshi's own settled numbers. Script: check-N02/safety.py, output safety.json.
- 18 shared stations x 67 days (07-20 to 09-24) = 1,206 station-days.
- Kalshi's settled high came in below the ForecastEx-day hourly max (the only way the package loses) on 2 days: BOS 08-31 (73 vs 74) and DCA 09-22 (65 vs 66). Both maxima were set in the 00:00-00:59 local daylight hour, the day-boundary risk the idea named.
- Kalshi's value differed from the NWS climate report once (MIA 08-29: 90 vs 85). Kalshi now names The Weather Company as its source.
- Kalshi minus hourly max: 0F on about 30% of days, 1F on about 55%, 2F or more on about 15%.

2) FLOW. Script: pkg_wide.py, output pkg_wide_rows.json.
- 10 shared stations (LAX, SFO, PHX, LAS, SEA, MIA, AUS, ATL, MDW, HOU), event dates 09-17 to 09-24 = 80 station-days.
- 38,893 ForecastEx prints (2.35M contracts) matched to the Kalshi 1-min candle ask in force at the print, with no look-ahead.
- Fees: ForecastEx $0.01/contract/side, confirmed at forecastex.com/faq. Kalshi taker fee rounded up per leg order.
- Package cost under $1: 468 prints, 15,448 contracts, $618 guaranteed edge = $77/day for all traders combined. That covers 58 of 80 station-days and 126 (station, date, K) clusters.
- Median edge 3.4c; median print 20 contracts.
- By station: LAX $186, MDW $108, LAS $90, SEA $80, SFO $69, rest under $41. Top station-day is 16% of the total; top 3 are 32%.
- Cost of $0.97 or less: 7,562 contracts, $512.

3) PAYOFFS.
- 0 of 38,893 settled prints paid under $1.
- In the positive set, 54 prints (12.3% of contracts, 9 of 126 clusters) paid $2. All 9 clusters were checked independently against the airport's hourly readings (Iowa State archive) and Kalshi's value (kick_verify.py): VERIFIED.
- Base rate of the $2 case over 297 clean clusters is 11.8% (regime.py).

4) OUR SHARE: a model, not a measurement.
- Tick rule (a price rise means the buyer of YES was the one who crossed): positive prints split into buyer-of-YES-crossed 9,999 contracts ($451), buyer-of-NO-crossed 3,973 ($93), unknown 1,476.
- Maker model: we rest ForecastEx NO priced so the package costs $0.97, and get every YES buyer who paid at least that. That is 5,516 contracts in 8 days = 690/day.
- Guaranteed part at that 3c margin: $20.7/day at 100% capture. Capped at 200/contract/day: $17.4. Capped at 50: $9.0.
- The $2 bonus realised on top: $123/day. Bootstrapping by station-day, the total is $43 to $278/day (5-95%); the guaranteed part alone is $14 to $28/day.

5) LEG RISK. Script: drift.py; top 25 station-days, 342 positive prints.
- After a positive print, the Kalshi leg's cost rose on average +0.85c within 60 s, +1.0c within 2 min and +2.1c within 15 min (median 0).
- 16% of contracts saw a rise of 2c or more within 60 s; 11% saw a rise larger than the whole edge.
- Only 118 of 468 positive prints had a Kalshi candle 60 s old or newer (184 had one 120 s old or newer, worth $30/day). Treating an older candle as "the book did not change" is an assumption, not a measured fact.

6) COST BANDS, one vote per cluster (bands.py). Realised profit per cluster:
- cost < 0.95: +19.7c (63 clusters)
- 0.95-0.97: +11.4c
- 0.97-1.00: +7.4c
- 1.00-1.03: +4.2c (214 clusters, about 15k contracts/day all traders)
- 1.03-1.06: +1.5c
- 1.06-1.10: 0
- 1.10-1.20: -1.3c
So break-even including the $2 bonus sits near $1.06-1.10. Above $1.00 the bonus is expected value, not guaranteed.

7) REGIME CONTROL (regime.py): over the same clusters, ForecastEx YES price minus outcome was +5.9c and Kalshi ask minus outcome was +10.9c. ForecastEx is no worse calibrated than Kalshi, so selling ForecastEx YES on its own, unhedged, is not supported (fx_calib.py and fx_calib2.py looked like a +5-8c edge before this control).

Volume: ForecastEx daily-high contracts trade about 350k/day across 24 stations; LAX alone had 2.36M in 12 days. Collector (pid 2532788) and crypto feeds (pid 105352) alive; 85.5 GB disk free; 1.81 GB RAM free. About 700 Kalshi GETs used in total.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
Per package, if we rest the ForecastEx NO: 3c margin minus about 1c Kalshi leg drift = about 2c guaranteed, plus about 7c expected from the $2 case (9 of 126 clusters paid $2; base rate 11.8%). About 9c expected per contract.

$900 bank: capital is the limit. Say $300 at IBKR and $100 on Kalshi, packages cost about $0.96 and are held 1-2 days, so about 250 new packages/day, which is roughly 35% of the 690/day that qualify.
- Guaranteed: 250 x 2c = about $5/day.
- Expected $2 cases: 250 x 7c = about $17/day.
- Realistic: $5-20/day. It is lumpy: most days $0-10, with an occasional +$50-150 day when a $2 case lands.

$5k bank: the flow is the limit, not capital.
- At 100% capture of 690/day: guaranteed $20.7 minus about $6 drift = about $14/day, plus about $48/day expected from the $2 case (the 8 days realised $123/day). Ceiling about $60/day.
- At a more believable 50% capture: about $30/day.
- Taking packages up to $1.03 (realised +4.2c per cluster, not guaranteed) could add volume, but our capture there is unmeasured.

All of this rests on 8 days and 80 station-days, and on an assumed share of a book we cannot see.
chk.worst_case:
The package loses only in two ways:
- A day-boundary high: the ForecastEx-day maximum set between 00:00 and 00:59 local daylight time. That happened 2 times in 1,206 station-days, each at a single strike. Or a Kalshi value that diverges downward (it diverged once, upward).
- Leg risk: a jump in the hourly airport reading while our ForecastEx NO order is still resting. Example: SFO 09-23 went 72 to 77 in one hour, and the Kalshi 77+ leg went from 5c to 60c+.

In dollars:
- A day-boundary failure costs the whole package, about $0.96 each: about -$50 at 50 contracts ($900 size) or about -$190 at 200 contracts ($5k size).
- A jump caught with the order still up costs about -$25 to -$55 per event at 50-100 contracts.
- Worst plausible day: about -$60 to -$100 at $900 size, about -$200 to -$250 at $5k.

Mitigation, not yet tested: skip day-ahead packages when the forecast midnight temperature is within 3F of K, and pull ForecastEx orders around the :51-:56 minute when the hourly reading is published.
chk.killer_risks:
1) Our share is unmeasured. The ForecastEx book is visible only through an IBKR account. Every ForecastEx price used here is someone else's fill, and who crossed the spread comes from a crude price-direction rule.
2) Engineering and ops: a new broker (IBKR Gateway plus its API, ForecastEx contract setup, 2FA re-logins) running as a second always-on process on a laptop with 1.8 GB RAM free next to the live bot.
3) Leg risk: the Kalshi leg drifted +0.85c on average within 60 s, and on 11% of contracts it moved by more than the whole edge.
4) Concentration and sample: 8 days; LAX is 30% of the guaranteed dollars; most of the money is the $2 case, which came from 9 clusters, and one station-day (LAX 09-24) was 41% of it.
5) Settlement sources can drift. Kalshi now names The Weather Company, and its value differed from the NWS report once in 1,206 days. A Weather Underground display change could break ForecastEx = hourly max.
6) Capital sits 1-2 days per package and is split across two brokers, which competes with pinrun's bank at $900.
7) The IBKR commission on ForecastEx is unconfirmed (the IBKR pages returned 403). The ForecastEx $0.01/side fee is confirmed.
8) Competition: whoever already rests the NO side at these prices may be doing this, which would squeeze the margin to zero.
9) The rule "an old Kalshi candle means an unchanged book" is assumed; only 184 of 468 positive prints had a candle 120 s old or newer.
chk.next_test:
Cheapest decisive test. The operator opens a free IBKR cash account with ForecastEx permission and market data; no money has to move to watch.

Then run a 7-day read-only watcher on the 10 stations. It polls every 10 s and logs:
- ForecastEx best YES bid and ask, with size, for every listed strike, plus ForecastEx trades;
- the Kalshi KXHIGH books (asks and depth) for the matching brackets.

It paper-books two things:
(a) A taker package whenever the ForecastEx YES bid is at least the Kalshi ask sum plus fees plus 3c, with depth. It re-reads the Kalshi ask 5 s later to measure the leg slip.
(b) A maker package whenever a ForecastEx trade prints at or through our would-be NO quote.

Pass bar, written before looking:
- at least 300 contracts/day of executable package at a cost of $0.97 or less, with size at the top of both books, on at least 5 of 7 days;
- median Kalshi slip of 1c or less at 5 s;
- zero packages paying under $1 at settlement.

If it passes: one contract per package, live, for 7 days, next to the paper log.

Scripts already written and reusable: check-N02/pkg_wide.py, drift.py, safety.py, bands.py.
chk.capital_needed: $900 bank: about $300-500 at IBKR for the ForecastEx NO legs and about $100 on Kalshi for the YES legs, tied up 1-2 days per package. $5k bank: about $2-3k at IBKR and $300-500 on Kalshi. There is no IBKR minimum on a cash account. Engineering cost: an IBKR Gateway and API client, roughly a multi-day build.

ref.strongest_objection:
Someone is already running this exact package with a fast bot, so the under-$1 flow the checker counted is either that bot's own fills or what it left behind. Kalshi's own trade tape shows it:

- **All legs bought.** After a ForecastEx print where the package cost under $1, every Kalshi leg, including the 1-2c tail brackets nobody buys to bet on direction, was bought by someone crossing the spread within 10 s on 17.3% of prints (283 prints, 15 station-days). The same prints shifted 300 s earlier: 0.0%. Shifted 60 s earlier: 1.8%. Ordinary mid-priced prints: 1.3%.
- **Same size.** The Kalshi buys match the ForecastEx print exactly. For example, SFO 09-19 K=71: 25 contracts on ForecastEx, then 25 on each of B74.5, B76.5 and T77 within 0.3-0.5 s. Median ratio of the largest leg bought to the ForecastEx quantity: 1.0.
- **Fast.** Median time from the ForecastEx print to the first Kalshi buy is 0.18 s (p10 0.13 s, p90 2.8 s).
- **It rests the NO side, like the checker's plan.** A crude price-direction rule puts 1,263 of the 1,792 matched contracts (70%) on the YES buyer as the one who crossed. So this bot's resting ForecastEx NO orders were getting filled, which is the checker's maker plan.
- **It pays more than we would.** Its fingerprint rate by package cost: under $0.95 17.6%, $0.95-1.00 17.1%, $1.00-1.03 12.3%, $1.03-1.06 5.4%, above $1.06 about 2%, and 0.5% at $1.20 and up. The placebo stays at 0-1.2%. It accepts packages up to about $1.03-1.06, so it outbids a NO order set to make the package cost $0.97.

What that leaves us: with the incumbent ahead of us in the ForecastEx queue, an order priced to make the package $0.97 fills only when a YES buyer sweeps past the incumbent's level, or after the incumbent has pulled its orders because the Kalshi leg moved. Both are the informed moments. That is the same trap that killed resting quotes on the crypto markets, and it matches the checker's own finding that the Kalshi leg rose about 0.85c on average within 60 s after these prints.

To get filled first we would have to pay at least the incumbent's price, a package cost of about $1.00-1.03. At that price the "always pays at least $1, costs under $1" margin is gone. What remains is a bet on the $2 case, where the checker's own control check found no mispricing and 41% of the $2-case money came from one station-day.

A laptop running IBKR plus Kalshi order calls will not re-price faster than a 0.18 s bot. So when the Kalshi leg jumps, our resting orders are the ones that get picked off.

Visible hedges cover only 16% of positive contracts and 20% of positive edge ($93.9 of $476.6). Hedges placed as resting Kalshi orders would not show up, so this is a lower bound.

Secondary point, settlement: Kalshi's rules changed between 07-21 and 09-01 from the NWS climate report to "The Weather Company" (read on KXHIGHLAX-26JUL21 and 26SEP01). So "Kalshi's value ≥ the hourly max" is now an observed pattern in that company's numbers, not guaranteed by how they are defined. That source has already differed from the NWS report by 5°F once (MIA 08-29, 90 vs 85). A miss in the downward direction would break the $1 floor.
ref.independent_checks:
Checks I ran myself, all read-only: 451 Kalshi GETs, collector (pid 2532788) and crypto feeds (pid 105352) alive, 85.7 GB disk free, 2.2 GB RAM free. Scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/refute-N02/.

1) **Kalshi trade tape, independent of the candles.** kfetch.py pulled every trade on all 6 brackets for the top 15 station-days by positive edge, which hold $476.6 of the $617.8 total edge; the cache is kcache.json.gz. kanalyze.py and kband.py then measured the Kalshi buying after each ForecastEx print:
   - Positive prints: every leg bought within 10 s on 17.3%, at least 2 legs on 17.7%, a tail leg on 19.2%. Median time to the first buy 0.5 s across all positive prints, 0.18 s on the fingerprinted ones.
   - Placebo at -300 s: 0 / 0 / 0.
   - Placebo at -60 s: 1.8% / 2.5% / 3.9%.
   - Control, 8,446 mid-priced prints: 1.3% / 6.1% / 9.0%.
   - Fingerprint by cost band (every leg bought within 10 s, or a leg matching the ForecastEx quantity within 3 s): under $0.95 0.176, $0.95-1.00 0.171, $1.00-1.03 0.123, $1.03-1.06 0.054, $1.06-1.10 0.024, $1.10-1.20 0.023, over $1.20 0.005. Placebo 0.000-0.012 in every band.
   - Fingerprinted share of positive prints: 1,792 of 11,234 contracts; $93.9 of $476.6 edge.
   - Price-direction rule (ktick.py) on fingerprinted positive prints: YES buyer crossed 1,263 contracts, NO buyer crossed 429.

2) **Were the candle asks really buyable?** For each positive print I compared the candle ask with Kalshi trades where the buyer crossed on the same leg within ±20 s. Across 339 leg checks: median difference +0.000, mean +0.0006; 5% were 1c or more above the candle, 1% were 3c or more. Positive edge after raising legs to the traded price: $469.3 of $476.6. So the checker's use of candles is not the problem.

3) **Stale candles (stale.py).** The share of prints that come out positive barely changes with candle age: 1.02% under 60 s, 1.1-1.4% for older candles. Staleness does not create the positives.

4) **Is there a price floor at $1 (wall.py)?** The sharp cliff at $1.00 in the full sample comes from near-certain prints, which cannot cost under $1 by construction. Among mid-priced prints (both legs between 0.10 and 0.90) the costs fall off smoothly and bunch around $1.15-1.25. So there is no hard floor at $1. The under-$1 prints are about 1.2% of prints, a thin tail.

5) **Rules.** /series/KXHIGHLAX, /series/KXHIGHTSFO and /series/KXHIGHCHI: quadratic fee, multiplier 1, settlement source "The Weather Company" (weather.com/kalshi). Event KXHIGHLAX-26JUL21 still settled on the NWS climate report; 26SEP01 and later use The Weather Company. ForecastEx fee $0.01 per contract per side, confirmed at forecastex.com/faq. Its FAQ also says it has "no specialists, market makers". The IBKR pages returned 403, so the IBKR commission is still unconfirmed. I did not re-run the checker's safety count (2 package failures in 1,206 station-days).
ref.revised_dollars_per_day: Guaranteed part: about $0-2/day at a $900 or $5k bank. We would sit behind a 0.18 s incumbent that bids up to a package cost of about $1.03-1.06, so our under-$1 fills would be the swept or abandoned, adversely selected remainder. The $2-case bonus is unproven expected value, not an edge: the checker's own control check shows no mispricing, and 41% of its bonus came from one station-day. Worst case stays about -$25 to -$55 per jump event caught with our order still resting. Net: roughly $0/day in expectation, against a multi-day IBKR build and a second broker process on the laptop. What would revive it: a read-only IBKR book watcher showing our NO price would regularly sit ahead of the incumbent's with size, and fill without the Kalshi leg moving.

idea.prior_reason: critic round
idea.name: Use Kalshi's own cash pools as the second account (index 0 for everything that is not crypto)
idea.family: capital efficiency / lose less (infrastructure that unblocks refuted survivors)
markets: all exchange_index-0 series (KXRAIN, KXHIGH*, KXCPI*, KXNFL*, AI-share, PortWatch, LIP farms)
idea.mechanism: Kalshi already splits cash by exchange_index. Crypto series (KXBTC15M, KXBTCD, KXCRYPTOLEAD15M) are index 2; rain, sports and the rest are index 0. Pinrun's read_bank reads the TOTAL 'balance'. Change it to read balance_breakdown for index 2 only, and have classify_bank_move and ktruth ignore index-0 moves. Every non-crypto strategy then runs out of index 0 with zero effect on pinrun's size, drawdown brake or deposit detector, which is exactly the objection that refuted or cut I25, I12, I14, I17, I30 and I16.
idea.why_mispriced: No counterparty. This removes an internal cost: our own bot treats cash it cannot trade with as its bank, and treats other strategies' spending as withdrawals.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Orders on index-2 markets cannot draw index-0 cash (cmdlive.py already passes exchange_index with its orders, which suggests the split is real). If they can, the fix is purely bookkeeping but still removes the drawdown and detector interference. (2) Cash can be moved between indexes or deposited to a chosen index. Not verified. (3) No live bot today depends on counting index-0 cash.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 directly. It turns the blocked parts of I03 (rain, about $2-4/day), I25 (about $3/day), I12 (about $0.4-2/day) and I17 (about $1-3/day at a bigger bank) from 'costs pinrun' back into additive money, about $5-10/day at $900 before any LIP credit. Lose-less side: pinrun currently sizes and brakes on $139.15 (13% of its reading) that may not back its crypto orders or hedges.
idea.data_needed: Read-only now: log balance_breakdown every 5 minutes for a day beside pinrun's read_bank to see whether index 0 ever changes when pinrun trades. Then, with sign-off, one 1-contract index-0 buy to confirm index 2 is untouched. Check Kalshi docs or support for moving cash between indexes.
idea.evidence_so_far: GET /portfolio/balance (read-only, 09-25): balance 108610 cents = $1,086.11, breakdown index 0 $139.1532, index 2 $946.9554. /series exchange_index: KXBTC15M 2, KXCRYPTOLEAD15M 2, KXBTCD 2, KXRAIN 0, KXNFLGAME 0. pinrun.py read_bank (line 15045) reads j['balance'] / 'balance_dollars' (the total). No 'insufficient' errors found in live logs, so no harm has been observed yet.
idea.novelty_vs_killed: Not a re-proposal. The refutes proposed a separate subaccount 'usable only through the API' and treated it as unavailable; the split already exists in the account and is visible on every balance read.
idea.worst_case: The pools are only a display split, so nothing changes for spendability, and the reader change only fixes the drawdown-detector interference. A careless read_bank edit could mis-size the live bot. It needs the usual VERSIONS entry, a startup-path run and versioncheck, and must never gate a hedge.

chk.measured:
All reads were GET-only via kauth. Outputs are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/check-N03/ (p1_acct.out/.json, p2_shards.out/.json, p3b.out).

1) THE SEPARATE POOLS ARE REAL. Kalshi's docs say "Orders cannot use cash from another index. Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard." Our own history shows it too:
- 2026-09-08: the first pin order was refused `insufficient_balance` while pool 0 held $41 and pool 2 held $0.0026 (results/OVERNIGHT.md).
- 2026-09-06: a $0.025 order was refused on pool 2's balance alone (HANDOFF_ARCHIVE).

Right now: total $1,086.11, pool 0 $139.1532, pool 2 $946.9554. Pinrun's read_bank (pinrun.py:15058) calls /portfolio/balance with no exchange_index. Kalshi's docs say that total "includes all exchange indexes", so pinrun sizes on $1,086 but can only spend $947. The $139 it cannot spend is 12.8% of what it sizes on, so bets are about 91 contracts instead of about 79 (size is proportional to bank). A /portfolio/balance?exchange_index=2 read returns 94695 cents and "946.9554", which passes read_bank's check that the cents and dollars figures agree.

2) NEW, AND IT BREAKS THE IDEA: AN AUTOMATIC REBALANCE IS SWITCHED ON. GET /portfolio/target_balance_allocation returns {0: 15%, 2: 85%}, with resting reservation "sum". Kalshi's docs say that every 10 seconds, if the pools have drifted from the target, Kalshi moves cash between them itself.
- It has fired at least once. On 2026-09-19 at 07:08:59Z a $378 debit-card deposit landed ($7.56 fee, $370.44 net). Sixteen seconds later $234.16 moved from pool 0 to pool 2. That left pool 0 at $139.1532 = 15.00% of $927.62, exactly the target. The $139.1532 reconciles to the cent: $370.44 - $234.16 + $2.8732 left over from 09-15.
- Pool 0 has not changed since (its updated_ts is 09-19 07:09:16Z), even though it has drifted to 12.8% over 6.6 days. So some tolerance exists, and I could not find its size stated anywhere.
- What this means: if another strategy spends pool 0 down, Kalshi can pull cash out of pinrun's pool to top it back up to 15%. The wall between the two pools that N03 relies on does not exist while this setting is on.

3) SERIES DO MOVE BETWEEN POOLS. Our own settlement ledger (results/kalshi_ledger.json, 1,145 rows) shows 1,136 on pool 2 and 9 on pool 0:
- KXBTC15M and KXBTCD settled on pool 0 on 08-15 and 08-23. They are pool 2 now.
- Natural gas, gold and copper 15-minute markets were pool 0 on 09-07. They are pool 2 now; Kalshi names pool 2 "Crypto & Commodities".
So a hard-coded "read pool 2" can silently go wrong.

4) POOL 0 IS NOT "EVERYTHING THAT ISN'T CRYPTO". I read exchange_index on the markets themselves (p2_shards.out):
- Pool 0: rain, daily highs and lows, CPI, Fed decision, payrolls, NFL, college football, EPL, AI-share (KXOPENSOURCESHARE, KXLLM1, KXTOPMODEL), S&P and Nasdaq hourly.
- Pool 2, the same pool as pinrun: WTI oil, gold, natural gas.
- Pool 3: MLB, WNBA, ATP tennis. KXNBAGAME's series says pool 3 but its open market says pool 0, so always read the market's own field, not the series'.
- Pool 1: combos.

5) THE BOT'S DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL DETECTOR ALREADY TREATS EVERYTHING THAT ISN'T PINRUN AS OUTSIDE MONEY. Since 09-17 it logged 31 'external' records:
- 30 were small ±$1 to $5 pairs, the pattern coin-race bets would leave. Coin race is on pool 2, so switching pinrun to read pool 2 only would not remove them.
- 1 was the real $370.44 deposit.
- Separately, the known $58.37 fake withdrawal after a restart.
Because the high-water mark moves with every such move, other strategies' cash moves already do not hit pinrun's 20% drawdown halt. What they do change is pinrun's SIZE.

6) THE REFUTES WERE ABOUT MONEY THAT COULD BE IN PINRUN, AND N03 DOES NOT FIX THAT. refute-I25/p6.out argued that cash parked in rain costs pinrun size. Cash moves between pools in about 4 seconds (8 transfers in /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers), so a dollar on pool 0 is still a dollar pinrun does not size on. Pinrun's recent return, from Kalshi's own ledger via pinday.py, crypto by ET day 09-20..09-25: +109.63, -2.97, +53.70, -42.46, +93.42, +59.99 (09-25 is a partial day). That is +$271.31 over 6 days, about $45/day, or about 4.3 cents per sizing dollar per day. I did not measure whether pinrun's profit grows in step with its size, and the operator found earlier that it does not.

Recorders alive (pids 105352, 2532788). 85.6 GB free.
chk.realistic_dollars_per_day:
$0 directly, at both bank sizes, and no net gain on money that is already in the account.

$900 bank:
- Using the $139 on pool 0 for rain and similar strategies takes it out of pinrun's sizing. Either pinrun reads pool 2 only, which cuts bets from about 91 to about 79 contracts (-13%), or it keeps reading the total and shrinks while those positions are open. At pinrun's recent rate (about 4.3c per sizing dollar per day, from $271.31 over 6 ET days on a $950 to $1,086 bank) that costs up to about $6/day, if pinrun's profit grows in step with size. That is not measured.
- The rain idea's own estimate (other agents, not measured here) is $2 to $4/day. So it is additive only if pinrun's profit does NOT grow with size. The operator's earlier finding says it does not, and this check did not settle it either way.
- On NEW money deposited to pool 0, any gain belongs to that strategy's own verdict, not to N03. What the pool split adds is only that pinrun would not size up on that money, and a bank cap flag would do the same.

$5k bank: the same $0. With the 15/85 rebalance on, about $750 of a $5,000 account would sit on pool 0. Pinrun would size on all $5,000 but could spend only about $4,250.
chk.worst_case:
These are bad outcomes from building N03 as written, not trading losses. Its own direct loss is $0, because it places no bets.

1) Pinrun is switched to read pool 2 while the 15/85 rebalance stays on. A pool-0 strategy spends its cash, and within about 10 seconds of the drift passing Kalshi's unstated tolerance, Kalshi refills pool 0 from pinrun's pool. The separation was never real, and pinrun also loses about 13% of its bet size at once.

2) Kalshi moves crypto to another pool again, as it already did between 08-23 and 09-07. A hard-coded pool-2 read then sizes on the wrong balance. Orders would be refused and pinrun's two-order-error brake halts it: missed trades, not lost money. The same thing on the day a hedge is needed is the 09-19 failure pattern ("a gate must never block a hedge").

3) Today, with no change: this is a rough limit worked out from the bot's own settings, NOT observed. One close could need up to the $544 stake cap plus up to about $400 of hedges (full hedges at up to about 70c, and hedges are exempt from the cap), about $940, against $947 spendable. The $139 pinrun counts but cannot reach is exactly what would be missing. The largest cash use seen so far is roughly half that.
chk.killer_risks:
1) The premise is wrong. The pools separate the bookkeeping, not the money. Cash moves between pools in about 4 seconds, so any dollar used for pool-0 strategies is a dollar pinrun does not size on. The objection that killed I25/I12/I17 was about that lost pinrun money, not about bookkeeping.

2) The account has Kalshi's automatic rebalance ON at 15/85. It fired on 09-19 (moved $234.16 and left pool 0 at exactly 15.00%). It can pull pinrun's cash into pool 0 whenever a pool-0 strategy spends.

3) Kalshi has moved series between pools twice in about 6 weeks (BTC 15-minute 0 to 2; natural gas, gold and copper 0 to 2).

4) "Pool 0" is not "everything except crypto". Commodities share pinrun's pool, and MLB, WNBA and tennis are pool 3.

5) Pinrun's detector already treats every move that isn't pinrun's as outside money, coin race included (30 small records since 09-17). So the detector-interference benefit is mostly already there, and switching pinrun to pool 2 would not remove the coin-race noise.

6) Unmeasured: whether pinrun's profit grows with its size. That is the only number that decides whether moving money to other strategies is a net gain.
chk.next_test:
These are the salvageable lose-less items. None of them puts money at risk.

(a) A settings decision for the operator, no code change. Set Kalshi's target allocation to pool 2 = 100% (and 0% for pool 0), or switch it off and move the $139.15 across by hand. Pass bar: the balance breakdown then shows pool 0 at about $0, pinrun's total equals what it can spend, and the next deposit lands on pool 2 within about 1 minute. This ends the 12.8% gap between what pinrun sizes on and what it can spend, and stops 15% of every future deposit being parked where pinrun cannot use it.

(b) Read-only, about 1 day, 288 GETs. Log /portfolio/subaccounts/balances and /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers every 5 minutes. Any transfer we did not start is the rebalancer firing, and the pool split at that moment gives Kalshi's tolerance. Pass bar: 0 unexplained transfers while the allocation is off.

(c) Only if a pool-0 strategy is actually approved, funded with NEW money. Pinrun then sums the balance of the pools its own markets carry (read from each market's exchange_index, never hard-coded 2) and halts loudly if that set of pools changes. It gets the usual version entry, a startup-path run and versioncheck, and it must never gate a hedge.

Separately, and needed before any claim that moving money out of pinrun is a gain: measure whether pinrun's daily profit grows with its size, using the Kalshi ledger by day against autosize.
chk.capital_needed: $0. It is settings and bookkeeping only. If a separate pool-0 pot is wanted, fund it with new money: using the existing $139 costs pinrun about 13% of its bet size.

abundant.why_more_ideas_likely: Combo prices come from a handful of makers (Oddpool counted 13, and none quoted non-sports RFQs in its test). They quote without hedging, while every leg has its own live book. So model-free limits between combo and legs are broken often: 98 of 152 book-confirmed crypto-combo trades in 7 closes. Sports combos are about 96% of the flow and have not been checked in-game.

abundant.why_more_ideas_likely: Separate series with separate thin maker crowds, joined only by arithmetic that no maker enforces. The gas pair was positive on 11 of 11 overlap dates. Kalshi keeps listing more horizons (state weeklies, election-day gas).

abundant.why_more_ideas_likely: Pre-game they are tightly linked (0 of 727k packages), but during play each book reprices on its own after scores. The scout's two-book parity found $257 in MLB in-play. Nobody has checked the cross-series sums in-play.

abundant.why_more_ideas_likely: Its book reprices in slow steps: 10-60 s after first-order prints and 1-5 minutes after pressers, flash PMIs and speeches. About 10 moves of ≥5c in 5.5 weeks. Anything that reads Fed-relevant news faster (futures, prints, ASR on pressers, Fed-speaker transcripts) has a target here.

wrongful_kills.id: D22 (ForecastEx, killed in SECOND_INCOME_SCAN section 5 / IDEA_LEDGER D22)
wrongful_kills.why_the_kill_is_wrong: The kill says ForecastEx is 'weekly/monthly/quarterly/annual only; no sub-day cadence, no live feed to be faster than'. That is false. Its own public daily summary for 2026-09-24 (forecastex.com/api/download?type=summary) shows daily temperature-high contracts with LAX 130,609 pairs and SFO 116,888 pairs traded in one day, plus 20 more city highs/lows, S&P futures price (92,652 pairs), 2-hourly CF Benchmarks crypto (CFBTC/CFETH/CFSOL expiring 12:00/14:00/16:00 CT, 2,803 / 724 / 369 pairs), daily WTI, and Fed/CPI contracts. Its daily-high contracts settle on the maximum of Weather Underground's HOURLY observations, not on the NWS climate report. I reproduced every settlement from free hourly METAR T-groups: 359 of 359 contracts, 0 mismatches (09-21..09-24, 15 cities). Kalshi settles the same city's high on the NWS climate report, which is never below the hourly maximum (0 exceptions in 402 non-NYC station-days, 7 stations, 07-20..09-24). So the two venues settle on different but ordered numbers, and that ordering makes a one-way package possible (new idea 'Two books, two thermometers'). What I measured against the idea: the easy money is gone. After an hourly reading locks a ForecastEx contract, 92,025 contracts still traded, but only 115 below 98c ($7 of value). Side check with the same data: the old KXHIGH/KXLOWT kills (D01, D05) blamed 'whole-Celsius' readings, and that reason is wrong. The T-group is exact whole °F (161 of 161 hourly readings and 50 of 50 six-hour max/min groups sit within 0.08 °F of a whole number). But their conclusion holds. After a T-group lock, Kalshi KXHIGH (62 locks, 0 wrong) traded 510,275 contracts with the locked side never below 99c. KXLOWT (38 locks, 0 wrong) traded 31,041 contracts with only 15 below 98c.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: 14 days of ForecastEx public pairs files (free, refreshed every 10 min, with trade timestamps) joined to Kalshi KXHIGH 1-minute candles for the roughly 10 stations both venues share (LAX, SFO, MIA, MDW, AUS, SEA, ATL, BOS, PHL, DFW; NYC does not match: ForecastEx uses LGA, Kalshi uses Central Park). Count the moments when 'ForecastEx NO at K' plus 'Kalshi YES on every bracket starting at K+1' costs under $1 after fees. Also confirm: the real ForecastEx fee (assumed $0.01 a contract), whether his state allows an IBKR ForecastTrader account, and Kalshi ask depth at those minutes. Scripts: critic/fx_lock.py, fx_pkg.py, fx_vs_kalshi.py, tgroup_cli.py, khigh_lock2.py, klow_lock.py.

wrongful_kills.id: I25 (refuted as net-negative), plus the same capital-clash cuts applied to I03, I12, I14, I17 and I30
wrongful_kills.why_the_kill_is_wrong: Each refutation priced the idea against pinrun's AVERAGE lifetime return (2.5-4c per dollar per day) on the assumption that every dollar is pinrun's dollar. Two things were not checked. (1) Kalshi already splits cash by exchange_index. Read-only GET /portfolio/balance just now returned balance_breakdown index 0 = $139.15 and index 2 = $946.96. /series shows KXBTC15M, KXBTCD and KXCRYPTOLEAD15M on index 2, and KXRAIN and KXNFLGAME on index 0. Rain, CPI, AI-share and sports ideas therefore trade out of a pool pinrun's crypto orders do not trade from. They only 'touch' pinrun because read_bank (pinrun.py line 15045) reads the TOTAL 'balance' field ($1,086.11), which includes index 0. That is a one-line reader change, not an economic cost. (2) The marginal return of pinrun's last dollar is below its average: the I12 refute itself measured only 59% of full legs and 72% of early legs filling the whole size, and pinrun's last 6 full days were about -$11. So the cost figure used to call I25 'net negative' (-$1.5 to -$5 a day) is an upper bound, not a measurement.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: (a) Whether an index-0 purchase ever draws index-2 cash (buy 1 rain contract after sign-off and read balance_breakdown before and after), and whether Kalshi allows moving cash between indexes. (b) The marginal pinrun return: from live logs, the P&L of the contracts beyond size x 0.8 on fully filled orders, against the average.

wrongful_kills.id: I24 (slow-market pin) -- the KXRT Sunday-to-Monday form only
wrongful_kills.why_the_kill_is_wrong: The general form was rightly killed (no-information favourites are fair; information-locked markets reprice to 99c). But the only form with a live public counter, KXRT strikes at least 2 points from the live rounded Rotten Tomatoes score from Sunday 10 AM to the Monday 10 AM ET settle, was killed without being measured. The checker said so ('needs RT score history at Sunday 10 AM ET, which I do not have'). I32's data shows fast sweepers were wrong 5 of 12 times on score jumps. That argues the book is not pricing the exact count, which is the same assumption a count-guarded pin needs.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Wayback snapshots of RT pages (25-139 per movie per the entertainment notes) at Sunday 10 AM ET for about 20 settled KXRT movies, against KXRT trades after that time on strikes at least 2 points from the rounded score. Kill it if fewer than about 500 contracts per weekend traded at 98c or less on those strikes. Low ceiling: about $2-9 a day even if it passes.

weak_survivors.id: I02, I05, I16, I19, I20, I21, I22 (the LIP family)
weak_survivors.problem: These are listed as seven survivors, but all seven rest on the same unobserved event: Kalshi crediting this account for a resting stack. Adding up their dollar figures double-counts one bet. Two refutes also cite live regulatory pressure on exactly this activity (CFTC letter 26-23; Kalshi publicly blaming fixed-size incentive orders on 09-23). One probe decides all seven, so treat them as one idea until a credit is seen. New fact for the credit test: any credit lands in the TOTAL balance pinrun reads, so it will also move pinrun's size and its deposit detector unless read_bank is changed.

The checker's statement that the farm 'would not touch the money bot's cash' because it sits on exchange_index 0 is half right. Pinrun cannot spend index-0 cash, but its read_bank reads the total balance ($1,086.11 = $139.15 + $946.96, measured now). So every farm fill, loss or credit changes pinrun's size, its 20% drawdown brake and classify_bank_move until the reader is restricted to index 2.

The verdict is 'plausible', but its core step (hedge the legs, then confirm) is barred by Kalshi Rule 5.3(g) unless Kalshi says otherwise in writing. The compliant version (hedge after the print) cannot be told apart from $0 on 10 closes (95% band -$17 to +$45 per close, one close carrying 86%). It should be parked as dead-pending-a-compliance-ruling, not ranked as a survivor.

The refute showed one bot fires both legs about 60 ms apart on 8 of 9 dates, and our round trip is about 96 ms. That leaves about $0.5-2.5 a day of leftovers, with dust and real size impossible to tell apart. At that level it is a watcher, not an idea.

weak_survivors.id: I22 (new-listing LIP on monthly one-touch ladders)
weak_survivors.problem: The refute measured that a 1c stack scores zero on 79-84% of live new_event programs, because others post above 1c within minutes. What remains is about 7 markets a month worth roughly $100 per program, and only if October copies September. The free read-only look at 04:10Z on 10-01 should decide it before anything else is built.

The cheap YES bids that give the 90-97c NO entries are largely LIP farmer ladders. KXRAIN carries about $1,711 a day of active LIP pools in the 09-25 snapshot. If the program ends, the supply goes with it. The band's loss rate is also artefact-prone (1 of 255 becomes 3 when reading the whole minute), and winter has never been observed.

weak_survivors.id: I10 (Poly pin, narrowed to the 1-hour window)
weak_survivors.problem: It rests on 7 real-time 1-hour windows (3 with any supply). The index base rate for qualifying hours is about 2 a day, not 3-6, and the pre-registered pass bar is out of reach even if the edge is real. One loss (about $57) equals 2-3 weeks of expected profit, so the loss rate cannot be verified in months.

In each, most of the measured ceiling comes from 1-2 events: PortWatch 84% from 2 Tuesdays, White House actions 73% from 2 days, hurricanes 86% from one Fausto surprise. Every one of them already has a faster incumbent. Their $/day figures are averages of rare windfalls, and our share of each windfall is unmeasured.

weak_survivors.id: I48, I49 (Poly listing watcher, Kalshi APY)
weak_survivors.problem: Both add $0 a day of new money: the APY is already paid automatically, and the watcher is capped at about $0.2 a day by polyorder's $10-a-day risk rail. They belong in housekeeping, not in the survivor ranking where they inflate the count.

weak_survivors.id: I08, I14 (sign-up bonuses, Poly promo credit)
weak_survivors.problem: These are one-off conversions ($28-31 and $110-230 after tax), not income. I08 is gated by his state and account history, both unknown. They should not sit in a $/day ranking.

new_ideas.name: Stale derived ladder: NFL wins-by-week priced exactly from game moneylines
new_ideas.family: sports / derivative-vs-underlying consistency (the measured form of unchecked I61)
markets: KXNFLWINSWEEK-26W4 (and W8, W12, KXNFLWINS when their remaining games are all listed)
new_ideas.mechanism: 'Team X wins at least k of its first 4 games' is an exact function of wins so far (from settled KXNFLGAME markets) plus the win chances of its remaining listed games, read from the 1c-wide game books and treated as independent. Every few minutes the bot recomputes each rung's fair value. It takes any ladder quote that sits beyond fair value by more than the taker fee plus 1c, holds to settlement, caps size per team (rungs of the same team move together), and skips a rung if any of its games is in progress.
new_ideas.why_mispriced: The 4-week ladder is quoted by a coarse maker: 600-lot quotes about 10c wide, median mid within 0.1c of fair, but single rungs far off. KXNFLWINSWEEK-26W4-CHI3 was bid 31c x 603 when Chicago (1-1, needs both of PHI@CHI at 31.5% and NYJ@CHI at 63%) is worth 19.9c. A taker even bought it at 40c on 09-24. JAC2 was offered at 49c when fair is 76.7c. The maker appears to use a team-strength prior rather than the game books, and ladder flow is too thin for anyone to police it (JAC2: 13 trades ever; CHI3: 40).
new_ideas.must_be_true: (1) The game books are the right fair value (they sit on the sharp line per I59). (2) Outcomes are independent across a team's different games. (3) The ladder counts only games in the stated weeks; an NFL tie counts as not-a-win while the game market pays 50c (about 0.3% of games). (4) The stale quotes are still there when we hit them. Artefact risk: the rung counts are from ONE snapshot at about 17:00Z 09-25, and a data bug in the team or week mapping would look exactly like a stale quote. I hand-checked CHI, JAC, IND, PHI, WAS against their 09-13 and 09-20 results.
new_ideas.rough_dollars_per_day: Measured snapshot (W4 only): 7 rungs past fee+1c, $144 of expected value at top-of-book size. Taking all of it risks about $2k, so at $900 cap it near 100 contracts a rung: about $25-40 per cycle. Exact pricing is possible only when every game in the horizon is listed (W4 now, W8 late Oct, W12 late Nov, season early Jan), so this averages about $1-4/day at $900 and $5-10/day at $5k during the NFL season, lumpy. It is on exchange_index 0, which pinrun does not trade from.
new_ideas.data_needed: Re-snapshot the W4 ladder against the game books after Sunday's games (09-27/28), before W4 settles on 10-04/05. Pass if at least 3 rungs are still past fee+1c 24 h after results are known, which would show the maker does not re-price to games. Then check the settled W4 rungs against the game-implied fair to confirm the mapping. Scripts: critic/nflweek.py, nflweek2.py, horizon.py.
new_ideas.evidence_so_far: nflweek.py, 09-25 about 17:00Z: 128 rungs, 60 two-sided. Mid minus game-implied fair: median +0.001, 10th-90th percentile -4.1c / +3.7c, median spread 10c. 7 rungs past fee+1c, summing $144.07 at top-of-book size (CHI3 sell 31c vs 19.9c fair x 603 = $58; PHI3 buy 75c vs 82.1c x 600 = $34; WAS1, NYJ2, CHI2, IND1, JAC2 the rest). Cross-horizon W4 <= W8 <= W12 <= season: 0 violations after fees (horizon.py).
new_ideas.novelty_vs_killed: I91/I92 killed set-sum and implication arbitrage INSIDE one ladder family; this prices a derived ladder against a different, liquid underlying market. I61 (season futures from game markets) was never checked. This is its first measurement, on the only horizon that is exactly computable today.
new_ideas.worst_case: A mis-mapped week or team makes a 'stale' quote real; the check is exact settlement reconciliation. Correlated rungs of one team all lose together: selling CHI2 and CHI3 both lose if Chicago wins both games, about -$550 at the 600-lot sizes, hence the per-team cap.

new_ideas.name: Two books, two thermometers: ForecastEx NO plus Kalshi YES on the same city's high
markets: ForecastEx UHLAX, UHSFO, UHMIA, UHMDW, UHAUS (and about 5 more shared stations)
Kalshi KXHIGHLAX, KXHIGHTSFO, KXHIGHMIA, KXHIGHCHI, KXHIGHAUS
new_ideas.mechanism: ForecastEx 'high exceeds K' pays if the MAXIMUM HOURLY reading is above K. Kalshi's brackets pay on the NWS climate-report high, which is always at least the hourly maximum (0 exceptions in 402 non-NYC station-days). So buying ForecastEx NO at K together with Kalshi YES on every bracket starting exactly at K+1 pays at least $1 in every outcome. It pays $2 when the hourly max is at or below K but the report comes in above it, which happened on 57-76% of days at the sampled stations. The bot watches both books, and whenever the pair costs under $1 after fees buys both (ForecastEx through the IBKR API), then holds to settlement the next morning.
new_ideas.why_mispriced: Two separate crowds price two different numbers for 'the same' high, and most traders do not know ForecastEx settles on hourly readings while Kalshi settles on the climate report. Occasionally one side prices K as if the other venue's number applied.
new_ideas.must_be_true: (1) Climate-report high >= hourly maximum on the same day (0 of 402 exceptions outside NYC; NYC fails and is excluded anyway because the stations differ). (2) Day boundaries: ForecastEx uses local daylight midnight to midnight, Kalshi local standard time (01:00-01:00 daylight). A new maximum set between 00:00 and 01:00 daylight time could break the package; this is rare for highs but not measured. (3) Only strikes where K+1 equals a Kalshi bracket's lower bound are clean (Kalshi brackets are 2 °F wide). (4) The ForecastEx fee is about $0.01 a contract and he can open an IBKR ForecastTrader account. Artefact risk: the evidence uses ForecastEx prints (someone else's fills) and Kalshi 1-minute candle asks carried forward up to a minute, so the depth we would actually get is unmeasured.
new_ideas.rough_dollars_per_day: Measured lower bound (package paying $1, ignoring the $2 upside): $136 across 10 city-days (5 cities x 09-23/24) from 117 of 4,447 matched prints, all traders combined. About 10 stations are shared, so about $130/day of qualifying flow for everyone. Our share is unknown. Realistic about $5-25/day at $900 (capital about $300-600 split across IBKR and Kalshi index 0, returned the next morning), about $15-50/day at $5k. It costs pinrun nothing if read_bank is limited to index 2.
new_ideas.data_needed: 14 days of ForecastEx pairs (free download) joined to Kalshi 1-minute candles for the 10 shared stations. Pass: at least $40/day of qualifying package-positive flow at a cost of $0.97 or less. Then confirm the ForecastEx fee, IBKR eligibility in his state, Kalshi ask depth at those minutes, and the frequency of midnight-hour maxima. Scripts: critic/fx_pkg.py, fx_vs_kalshi.py, fx_lock.py, tgroup_cli.py.
new_ideas.evidence_so_far: fx_lock.py: ForecastEx settlement = hourly METAR T-group max > K on 359 of 359 contracts (09-21..09-24, 15 cities). tgroup_cli.py: climate-report high below the hourly max 0 of 402 station-days at MIA, DEN, AUS, LAX, PHL, MDW, 07-20..09-24 (NYC 1 of 67). The climate-report high exceeded the hourly max on 38-51 of 67 days per station. fx_pkg.py: 117 positive packages, $136.20 lower bound, 0 outcomes paying under $1 in the settled cases checked (e.g., SFO 09-23 K=76: ForecastEx YES; climate report 78, so the Kalshi leg paid).
new_ideas.novelty_vs_killed: D22 killed ForecastEx on a false premise, and D12 (Kalshi-Gemini) failed because two different indices can settle opposite ways. new_ideas.name: Use Kalshi's own cash pools as the second account (index 0 for everything that is not crypto)
new_ideas.family: capital efficiency / lose less (infrastructure that unblocks refuted survivors)
markets: all exchange_index-0 series (KXRAIN, KXHIGH*, KXCPI*, KXNFL*, AI-share, PortWatch, LIP farms)
new_ideas.mechanism: Kalshi already splits cash by exchange_index. Crypto series (KXBTC15M, KXBTCD, KXCRYPTOLEAD15M) are index 2; rain, sports and the rest are index 0. Pinrun's read_bank reads the TOTAL 'balance'. Change it to read balance_breakdown for index 2 only, and have classify_bank_move and ktruth ignore index-0 moves. Every non-crypto strategy then runs out of index 0 with zero effect on pinrun's size, drawdown brake or deposit detector, which is exactly the objection that refuted or cut I25, I12, I14, I17, I30 and I16.
new_ideas.why_mispriced: No counterparty. This removes an internal cost: our own bot treats cash it cannot trade with as its bank, and treats other strategies' spending as withdrawals.
new_ideas.must_be_true: (1) Orders on index-2 markets cannot draw index-0 cash (cmdlive.py already passes exchange_index with its orders, which suggests the split is real). If they can, the fix is purely bookkeeping but still removes the drawdown and detector interference. (2) Cash can be moved between indexes or deposited to a chosen index. Not verified. new_ideas.novelty_vs_killed: Not a re-proposal. The refutes proposed a separate subaccount 'usable only through the API' and treated it as unavailable; the split already exists in the account and is visible on every balance read.

All GET-only through kauth, about 1,230 calls over roughly 1 hour. Scripts and raw output are in C:/Users/Joe/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--kals-repo/47b37ac1-655c-4d72-a81b-a48e9625d5bd/scratchpad/sweep/calibration-bias/.

(1) Settled-market census (fetch_markets.py, fetch_ladders.py -> markets.jsonl, markets_ladder.jsonl): 34,010 settled yes/no markets in about 130 series, last 30-60 days. Sampled 23,809 (sampled_tickers.json), capped at 2,600 markets per family by whole events.

(2) Tradeable-quote calibration (fetch_candles.py, then analyze.py with --selftest, which plants a +7c favourite edge and a null world; it passes). Batched GET /markets/candlesticks gave hourly yes_ask/yes_bid closes for all 23,809 markets and minute candles for 10,207. At fixed times before a pre-known anchor (event max close for scheduled closes; occurrence_datetime, i.e. scheduled start + 3 h, for sports), buy YES at the ask or NO at 1 minus the bid. Net is after the taker fee with 10-lot rounding and the series multiplier. Clustered by event and by day, whichever is more conservative. Output: cells.json and pooled_s04.txt / pooled_s10.txt, produced by report.py.

KEY 1: without a spread filter the numbers are garbage. Pooled '95-98c' asks at 24 h won only 58%, because lone 97c asks sit on dead rungs: entertainment YES at 95-98c won 6.9% of 565; hourly-ladder YES at 95-98c at 1 h won 41%. Never read a lone ask as a probability; everything below uses spread <=4c.

KEY 2: non-sports longshots are overpriced. YES under 5c at 24 h averaged 2.8c and won 0.6%: -2.52c/contract (1,045 markets / 515 events, t -9.3, halves -2.39 / -2.79, smallest detectable effect 0.76c). The same holds at 1 h (-1.93c) and 5-10c (-2.1 to -4.2c).

KEY 3: the mirror trade does not pay a taker. NO at 98-100c at 24 h gives +0.48c (t 1.5, 484 events); 1 h +0.36c; 6 h -0.54c. The spread and fee eat the premium.

KEY 4: sports pregame is calibrated. At start-6h every bucket is -0.3 to -3.6c (fee plus spread), smallest detectable effect 3.3-5.3c. Longshots pregame are fair (-0.3 to -0.8c). In-game at start+1h, YES under 5c is -2.41c (t -3.5).

KEY 5: no time-of-day or weekend effect (tod.py). Longshots -1.2 to -2.2c in every 6-hour ET bin and -1.65 vs -1.66c weekday vs weekend; favourites -0.3 to -1.2c.

Caveat: the 'both' rows in 35-65c buckets understate their error because YES and NO on the same market cancel (the mid-price t of -40 is that artefact). Tail and single-side rows are unaffected.
